<a id="target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-fundamental-exact-sequence"></a>

### The fundamental exact sequence 0 → Q_p → B_cris^{φ=1} → B_dR/B_dR^+ → 0

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/fundamental-exact-sequence` (theorem).

(1) (Fil^0B_cris)^{φ=1} = B_cris^{φ=1} ∩ B_dR^+ = Q_p, and 0 → Q_p → B_cris ∩ B_dR^+ → B_cris → 0 (map φ − 1) is exact. (2) φ − 1: B_cris → B_cris is surjective, with kernel B_e := B_cris^{φ=1}. (3) (Fundamental exact sequence) 0 → Q_p → B_e → B_dR/B_dR^+ → 0 is exact, i.e. Q_p = B_e ∩ B_dR^+ and B_dR = B_e + B_dR^+. (4) Variants: for r ≥ 0, 0 → Q_p → (Fil^{−r}B_cris)^{φ=1} → Fil^{−r}B_dR/B_dR^+ → 0 is exact; for r ≥ 1, (Fil^rB_cris)^{φ=p^r} = Q_pt^r and Fil^1(B_cris)^{φ=1} = 0. All maps are G_K-equivariant.

**Hypotheses and scope.** B_cris ⊆ B_dR via R06.1/acris-embedding-injective.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1) is R06.1/bcris-twisted-frobenius-sequences (3) with r = 0.
2. (2) surjectivity of φ − 1 on B_cris: given b choose, by (1), x ∈ Fil^0 with (φ − 1)x = b.
3. (3) the 3×3 diagram of F-O Theorem 6.26 with rows (1) and (2): B_e/Q_p ≅ B_cris/(B_cris ∩ B_dR^+) ≅ B_dR/B_dR^+, the last because B_dR = B_cris + B_dR^+ (A_inf[1/p] ⊆ B_cris^+ surjects onto B_dR^+/t^n and t^{−n} ∈ B_cris).
4. (4) restrict (3) to Fil^{−r}; the φ = p^r eigenspace statement is (3) of R06.1/bcris-twisted-frobenius-sequences twisted by t^r.

**Checks.** The variant used by weak admissibility (B-C Lemma 9.3.7): for r > 0 the space (Fil^{−r}B_cris)^{φ=1} is infinite-dimensional over Q_p, since Fil^{−r}B_dR/B_dR^+ is an infinite-dimensional C-space. Kummer check: for u ∈ O_K^× not a root of unity and a compatible system of p-power roots, log_cris[ũ] ∈ B_cris^+ with φ(log[ũ]) = p log[ũ] (B-C Example 9.2.8), so log[ũ]/t ∈ B_e is a lift of the class of log(u)/t ∈ B_dR/B_dR^+.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/bcris-twisted-frobenius-sequences`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-bcris-twisted-frobenius-sequences), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/crystalline-period-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-crystalline-period-ring), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/bdr-filtration-and-graded`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-bdr-filtration-and-graded).

**Sources.** [J.-M. Fontaine and Y. Ouyang — Theory of p-adic Galois representations](https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/~jean-marc.fontaine/prepub/theory_padic.pdf), §6.2.3, Theorem 6.26 and Remark 6.27, p. 130. Statements (1)–(3) with proof. [O. Brinon and B. Conrad — CMI Summer School notes on p-adic Hodge theory](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/notes.pdf), Theorem 9.1.10, p. 134. Statement (1); B-C give no proof. [O. Brinon and B. Conrad — CMI Summer School notes on p-adic Hodge theory](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/notes.pdf), Proof of Lemma 9.3.7, display (9.3.1), p. 151. Variant (4); B-C cite the primary Colmez–Fontaine construction, F-O's proof is used.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-bmax-period-ring"></a>

### The rings A_max and B_max^+ and their embedding in B_dR^+

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/bmax-period-ring` (construction).

Let I = (p, ξ) ⊆ A_inf, A^0_max = A_inf[ξ/p] ⊆ A_inf[1/p] (the A_inf-subalgebra generated by p^{-1}I), A_max its p-adic completion and B_max^+ = A_max[1/p]; B_max = B_max^+[1/t]. For K/K_0 finite with uniformiser π_K, put A_{inf,K} = O_K ⊗_{W(k)} A_inf and let A_{max,K}, B_max,K^+ be the analogous completions for ([π̃_K] − π_K)/π_K (π̃_K ∈ O_C^♭ with π̃_K^♯ = π_K). Then: (1) the Witt Frobenius extends to A_max, B_max^+ and B_max; (2) the series Σ b_n(ξ/p)^n converge in B_dR^+, giving continuous G_K-equivariant maps B_max^+ → B_dR^+ and B_max,K^+ → B_dR^+, and B_max,K^+ ≅ K ⊗_{K_0} B_max^+; (3) A_cris maps continuously into A_max (γ_n(ξ) = (p^n/n!)(ξ/p)^n with p^n/n! ∈ Z_p), compatibly with the maps to B_dR^+, so j(A_cris)[1/p] ⊆ image(B_max^+) inside B_dR^+.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Only used as an auxiliary ring in the proof of R06.1/k-tensor-bcris-injective; Colmez's rings, specialised to the sympathetic algebra Λ = C.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Construction as in Colmez 2002 §8.5; φ preserves the ideal (p, ξ) since φ(ξ) ≡ ξ^p mod p, so φ(ξ/p) = ξ^p/p + w ∈ A^0_max.
2. (2) ξ/p ∈ Fil^1B_dR^+, so power series in ξ/p with p-adically null coefficients converge; K ⊗_{K_0} B_max^+ ≅ B_max,K^+ because ([π̃_K]/π_K)^e and [p^♭]/p differ by a unit of A_{inf,K} (Colmez Remark 8.13).
3. (3) the inclusion A^0_cris ⊆ A^0_max is p-adically continuous and extends to the completions; both maps to B_dR^+ restrict to the inclusion on A^0_cris ⊆ A_inf[1/p], so they agree by continuity.

**API.**

- `Amax` (data): A_max, the p-adic completion of A_inf[ξ/p] ⊆ A_inf[1/p].
- `BmaxPlus` (data): B_max^+ = A_max[1/p].
- `bmaxPlusToBdRPlus` (constructor): The continuous G_K-equivariant map B_max^+ → B_dR^+, Σ b_n(ξ/p)^n ↦ Σ b_n(ξ/p)^n.
- `acrisToAmax` (constructor): The continuous map A_cris → A_max extending A^0_cris ⊆ A^0_max.
- `acrisToAmax_comp` (compatibility): bmaxPlusToBdRPlus ∘ acrisToAmax = acrisToBdRPlus.
- `bmaxFrobenius` (constructor): The Frobenius on A_max and B_max^+ extending the Witt Frobenius.
- `bmaxPlusK_equiv` (equivalence): K ⊗_{K_0} B_max^+ ≅ B_max,K^+.

**Unit tests.**

- `Amax_xi_div_p` (computation): ξ/p ∈ A_max and (ξ/p)^n ∈ A_max for all n.
- `Amax_contains_ainf` (degenerate): A_inf ⊆ A_max.
- `acrisToAmax_divided_power` (compatibility): acrisToAmax(γ_n(ξ)) = (p^n/n!)(ξ/p)^n.
- `xi_mem_p_Amax_not_Acris` (non-example): ξ ∈ pA_max, but ξ ∉ pA_cris: modulo p, A_cris/p ≅ (O_C^♭/(p^♭)^p)[Y_0, Y_1, …]/(Y_i^p) and ξ maps to p^♭ ≠ 0.

**Uses.** Colmez 2002, Proposition 8.14: K ⊗_{K_0} B_max^+ → B_dR^+ is injective. PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/k-tensor-bcris-injective: B_cris^+ ⊆ B_max^+ transfers the injectivity to B_cris.

**Checks.** ξ^n/p^n ∈ A_max for all n, while A_cris only contains the divided powers ξ^n/n!; the map A_cris → A_max sends γ_n(ξ) to (p^n/n!)(ξ/p)^n.

**Prerequisites.** `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`, [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/de-rham-period-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-de-rham-period-ring), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/acris-embedding-into-bdr-plus`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-acris-embedding-into-bdr-plus), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/complete-algebraically-closed-bdr`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-complete-algebraically-closed-bdr), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/bdr-natural-topology`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-bdr-natural-topology), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/galois-action-on-cp`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-galois-action-on-cp), `mathlib:WittVector.frobenius`.

**Proof ingredients.** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/algebraic-closure-in-bdr-plus`; their statements and locators appear in the proof-ingredient index.

**Sources.** [Pierre Colmez — Espaces de Banach de dimension finie](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~pierre.colmez/jussieucorps.pdf), §8.5, definition of A_max and B_max^+, p. 61. The definition (Colmez's I is the ideal generated by p and ξ). [Pierre Colmez — Espaces de Banach de dimension finie](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~pierre.colmez/jussieucorps.pdf), Remarque 8.13, p. 62. Colmez Remark 8.13 gives the identification K ⊗_{K_0} B_max^+ ≅ B_max,K^+ (the formulas follow in the display).

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-k-tensor-bmax-injective"></a>

### Colmez: K ⊗_{K_0} B_max^+ → B_dR^+ is injective

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/k-tensor-bmax-injective` (theorem).

For K/Q_p finite, the natural map K ⊗_{K_0} B_max^+ ≅ B_max,K^+ → B_dR^+ is injective. In particular (K = K_0) B_max^+ → B_dR^+ is injective, and B_max^+ is identified with a subring of B_dR^+.

**Hypotheses and scope.** K/Q_p finite, v a generator of J_K = ker(θ on A_{inf,K}[1/π_K]).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Colmez §8.4: fix a continuous K-linear section s of θ and a generator v of J_K; the recursion a_0(x) = x, b_n(x) = θ(a_n(x)), a_{n+1}(x) = (a_n(x) − s(b_n(x)))/v defines a Q_p-linear topological isomorphism θ_v: B_dR^+ ≅ C[[X]], x ↦ Σ b_n(x)X^n (not a ring map).
2. With v = ([π̃_K] − π_K)/π_K (the element adjoined to A_{inf,K} to form A_{max,K}), the expansion restricts to isomorphisms A_max,K ≅ O_C{X} and B_max,K^+ ≅ C{X} (restricted power series) of topological O_K-modules.
3. The commutative square B_max,K^+ → C{X} ⊆ C[[X]] ← B_dR^+ (via θ_v) shows that B_max,K^+ → B_dR^+ is injective; K ⊗_{K_0} B_max^+ ≅ B_max,K^+ (R06.1/bmax-period-ring).

**Checks.** For K = K_0 the statement says that a p-adically convergent series Σ a_n(ξ/p)^n (a_n ∈ A_inf, a_n → 0) vanishing in B_dR^+ vanishes in B_max^+.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/bmax-period-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-bmax-period-ring), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/complete-algebraically-closed-bdr`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-complete-algebraically-closed-bdr), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/bdr-natural-topology`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-bdr-natural-topology).

**Sources.** [Pierre Colmez — Espaces de Banach de dimension finie](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~pierre.colmez/jussieucorps.pdf), §8.5, Proposition 8.14 with proof, p. 62. The statement (with the superscripts + lost in extraction). [Pierre Colmez — Espaces de Banach de dimension finie](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~pierre.colmez/jussieucorps.pdf), §8.4, the expansion θ_v, p. 60. The expansion isomorphism used in the proof (take Λ = C).

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-k-tensor-bcris-injective"></a>

### K ⊗_{K_0} B_cris → B_dR is injective and compatible with gradings

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/k-tensor-bcris-injective` (theorem).

For K/Q_p finite, the natural G_K-equivariant map K ⊗_{K_0} B_cris → B_dR is injective; giving K ⊗_{K_0} B_cris the subspace filtration, the induced map gr(K ⊗_{K_0} B_cris) → gr B_dR = B_HT is an isomorphism. Consequently K ⊗_{K_0} Frac(B_cris) → B_dR is injective.

**Hypotheses and scope.** B_cris^+ ⊆ B_dR^+ via R06.1/acris-embedding-injective.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Reduce to B_cris^+: K ⊗ B_cris = (K ⊗ B_cris^+)[1/t] and t is invertible in the field B_dR.
2. By R06.1/bmax-period-ring (3), B_cris^+ ⊆ B_max^+ inside B_dR^+; K is flat over K_0, so K ⊗_{K_0} B_cris^+ → K ⊗_{K_0} B_max^+ is injective, and K ⊗_{K_0} B_max^+ → B_dR^+ is injective by R06.1/k-tensor-bmax-injective.
3. Graded statement: t ∈ B_cris and A_cris surjects onto O_C, so each gr^i(K ⊗ B_cris) → C(i) is surjective; injectivity on gr is automatic for a subspace filtration (B-C proof of Theorem 9.1.5).
4. Fraction field: B_dR is a field, so a K-linear dependence in K ⊗ Frac(B_cris) clears denominators to one in K ⊗ B_cris.

**Checks.** For K = Q_p(p^{1/2}) the elements 1 ⊗ 1 and p^{1/2} ⊗ 1 stay K_0-linearly independent over B_cris inside B_dR.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/k-tensor-bmax-injective`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-k-tensor-bmax-injective), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/bmax-period-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-bmax-period-ring), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/crystalline-period-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-crystalline-period-ring), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/bdr-filtration-and-graded`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-bdr-filtration-and-graded), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`, [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/acris-embedding-into-bdr-plus`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-acris-embedding-into-bdr-plus), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/fontaine-element-t`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-fontaine-element-t), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/tilt-of-cp-and-special-elements`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-tilt-of-cp-and-special-elements).

**Proof ingredients.** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/t-in-acris`; their statements and locators appear in the proof-ingredient index.

**Sources.** [O. Brinon and B. Conrad — CMI Summer School notes on p-adic Hodge theory](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/notes.pdf), Theorem 9.1.5 with proof, p. 131. B-C state the theorem, note that Fontaine's proof is incomplete when e > 1 and omit the repair; the node repairs it with Colmez's Proposition 8.14. [Pierre Colmez — Espaces de Banach de dimension finie](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~pierre.colmez/jussieucorps.pdf), §8.5, after Proposition 8.14, p. 62. The identification used for the repair.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-crystalline-logarithm"></a>

### The crystalline logarithm λ: (O_C^♭)^× → B_cris^+ and its extension to (C^♭)^×

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/crystalline-logarithm` (construction).

(1) For x ∈ 1 + m_{O_C^♭}, the terms ([x] − 1)^n/n lie in A_cris for n ≫ 0 and tend to 0 p-adically, so log_cris[x] = Σ_{n≥1}(−1)^{n+1}([x] − 1)^n/n converges in B_cris^+; x ↦ log_cris[x] is a G_K-equivariant homomorphism with φ(log_cris[x]) = p log_cris[x]; extending by 0 on the Teichmüller lifts of k̄^× gives λ: (O_C^♭)^× → B_cris^+. (2) (Compatibility with log_dR.) If y ∈ (O_C^♭)^× and y^♯ ∈ K̄^× ∩ O_C^×, then log_cris[y] = log_dR([y]/y^♯) + log(y^♯) in B_dR^+, where log_dR is the logarithm on 1-units of B_dR^+ and log the p-adic logarithm on O_{K̄}^× (trivial on roots of unity). (3) log_cris[ε^a] = at for a ∈ Z_p.

**Hypotheses and scope.** A_cris ⊆ B_dR^+ as in R06.1/acris-embedding-injective.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1) θ(([x] − 1)^N) ∈ pO_C for N ≫ 0, so ([x] − 1)^N = pw_1 + ξw_2 has divided powers in A_cris; write n = Nq_n + r_n and use v_p(q_n!/n) → ∞ (B-C Lemma 9.2.2). Homomorphism, equivariance and φ-compatibility pass to the limit from finite sums.
2. (2) Both sides are additive in y and live in a torsion-free group, so replace y by y^N to reach y^♯ ∈ 1 + pO_{K'} for a finite K'/K; then compare the p-adically convergent series in O_{K'} ⊗_{W(k')} A_cris[1/p] with the Fil-adically convergent series in B_dR^+: the p-adic tail of Σ(−1)^{n+1}(p^n/n)v^n (θ̃(v) = 0) lies in Fil^i for n ≥ i (B-C Lemma 9.2.7).
3. (3) is R06.1/fontaine-element-t (3) in A_cris.

**API.**

- `logCris` (constructor): λ: (O_C^♭)^× → B_cris^+, x ↦ log_cris[x] on 1-units, 0 on Teichmüller lifts of k̄^×.
- `logCris_mul` (simp): λ(xy) = λ(x) + λ(y).
- `frobenius_logCris` (relation): φ(λ(x)) = pλ(x).
- `logCris_galois` (functoriality): λ(gx) = g λ(x).
- `logCris_epsilon` (simp): λ(ε^a) = a t.
- `logCris_eq_logDR` (compatibility): λ(y) = log_dR([y]/y^♯) + log(y^♯) when y^♯ ∈ O_{K̄}^×.

**Unit tests.**

- `logCris_one` (degenerate): λ(1) = 0.
- `logCris_epsilon_eq_t` (computation): λ(ε) = t.
- `logCris_compat_logDR_units` (compatibility): For y ∈ 1 + m_{O_C^♭} with y^♯ = 1, λ(y) = log_dR[y] (the B_dR^+ logarithm of R06.1/fontaine-element-t).
- `logCris_not_extend_nonunits` (non-example): λ does not extend to (C^♭)^× as a map into B_cris: λ(p^♭) would be u, which is transcendental over Frac(B_cris) (R06.1/log-p-flat-transcendental).

**Uses.** Brinon–Conrad Definition 9.2.3: B_st^+ is generated over B_cris^+ by adjoining the logarithms λ_st(y) of non-units. Brinon–Conrad Example 9.2.8: Kummer extensions of Q_p by Q_p(1) are crystalline, realised by t and log_cris[ũ]. PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/semistable-period-ring: the universal property of B_st^+ extends λ to (C^♭)^×.

**Checks.** λ(ε) = t; φ(λ(x)) = λ(x^p) = pλ(x).

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/crystalline-period-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-crystalline-period-ring), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`, [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/acris-embedding-into-bdr-plus`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-acris-embedding-into-bdr-plus), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/fontaine-element-t`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-fontaine-element-t), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/tilt-of-cp-and-special-elements`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-tilt-of-cp-and-special-elements), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/complete-algebraically-closed-bdr`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-complete-algebraically-closed-bdr), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/bdr-natural-topology`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-bdr-natural-topology), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/galois-action-on-cp`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-galois-action-on-cp), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/frobenius-on-acris`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-frobenius-on-acris).

**Proof ingredients.** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/t-in-acris`, `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/algebraic-closure-in-bdr-plus`; their statements and locators appear in the proof-ingredient index.

**Sources.** [O. Brinon and B. Conrad — CMI Summer School notes on p-adic Hodge theory](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/notes.pdf), Lemma 9.2.2, p. 137. Statement (1) (the φ-compatibility is the following display). [O. Brinon and B. Conrad — CMI Summer School notes on p-adic Hodge theory](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/notes.pdf), Lemma 9.2.7, p. 140. Statement (2).

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-semistable-period-ring"></a>

### The semistable period ring B_st with Frobenius, monodromy and Galois action

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/semistable-period-ring` (construction).

B_st^+ := Sym_Q((C^♭)^×) ⊗_{Sym_Q((O_C^♭)^×)} B_cris^+ (B-C Definition 9.2.3), the initial B_cris^+-algebra with a G_K-equivariant homomorphism λ_st: (C^♭)^× → B_st^+ extending λ of R06.1/crystalline-logarithm; B_st := B_st^+[1/t]. Choosing y_0 = p^♭ and u := λ_st(p^♭) gives B_st^+ = B_cris^+[u], B_st = B_cris[u], a polynomial ring in u. Structures: Frobenius φ(λ_st(y)) = pλ_st(y) (so φ(u) = pu), extending φ of B_cris; G_K acts by g(u) = u + c(g)t, where g(p^♭) = p^♭ε^{c(g)}; the monodromy operator N is the unique B_cris-linear derivation of B_st with N(λ_st(y)) = −v^♭(y) for y ∈ (C^♭)^× (normalisation v^♭(p^♭) = 1), i.e. N = −d/du. Then Nφ = pφN, N commutes with G_K, B_st^{N=0} = B_cris, and 0 → B_cris → B_st → B_st → 0 (last map N) is exact. Sign convention: this is Fontaine–Ouyang's N (N(log[ϖ]) = −1); Brinon–Conrad's operator is −N.

**Hypotheses and scope.** The normalisation of u and N: u = λ_st(p^♭) with (p^♭)^♯ = p, N = −d/du (Fontaine's convention as in Fontaine–Ouyang Definition 6.15).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Sym_Q((C^♭)^×) is a polynomial ring over Sym_Q((O_C^♭)^×) in one variable, because 1 → (O_C^♭)^× → (C^♭)^× → Q → 1 is exact (v^♭) (B-C (9.2.1)); so B_st^+ = B_cris^+[λ_st(y_0)] for any y_0 with v^♭(y_0) ≠ 0.
2. Changing y_0 to y_0w with w ∈ (O_C^♭)^× changes u by λ(w) ∈ B_cris^+, so d/du and hence N = −v^♭(y_0)d/dλ_st(y_0) do not depend on y_0 (B-C Remark 9.2.5).
3. g(p^♭) = p^♭ε^{c(g)} gives g(u) = u + λ(ε^{c(g)}) = u + c(g)t; φ is defined by φ(λ_st(y)) = λ_st(y^p) = pλ_st(y).
4. Nφ = pφN: both sides are derivations twisted by φ, agree on B_cris (zero) and on u: Nφ(u) = N(pu) = −p and pφN(u) = pφ(−1) = −p. N commutes with G_K because N(c(g)t) = 0.
5. Exactness: N = −d/du on B_cris[u] is surjective with kernel B_cris (F-O Proposition 6.16).

**API.**

- `Bst` (data): B_st = B_cris[u] (Polynomial Bcris), canonically Sym_Q((C^♭)^×) ⊗ B_cris.
- `Bst.u` (constructor): u = λ_st(p^♭) ∈ B_st.
- `Bst.logSt` (constructor): λ_st: (C^♭)^× → B_st, λ_st(y) = v^♭(y)u + λ(y/(p^♭)^{v^♭(y)}) (for y with rational valuation, using p-power roots of p^♭).
- `Bst.frobenius` (constructor): φ on B_st with φ(u) = pu, extending φ on B_cris.
- `Bst.monodromy` (constructor): N = −d/du, a B_cris-linear derivation.
- `Bst.monodromy_frobenius` (relation): N ∘ φ = p·φ ∘ N.
- `Bst.galois_u` (relation): g(u) = u + c(g)t with c the Kummer cocycle of p.
- `Bst.monodromy_galois` (relation): N(gb) = gN(b).
- `Bst.ker_monodromy` (characterisation): B_st^{N=0} = B_cris.
- `Bst.monodromy_surjective` (characterisation): N: B_st → B_st is surjective.
- `Bst.universal` (universal-property): (B_st^+, λ_st) is initial among B_cris^+-algebras S with a G_K-equivariant homomorphism (C^♭)^× → S extending λ.

**Unit tests.**

- `Bst_monodromy_u` (computation): N(u) = −1 and N(u^2) = −2u.
- `Bst_monodromy_bcris` (degenerate): N vanishes on B_cris ⊆ B_st.
- `Bst_frobenius_restrict` (compatibility): φ on B_st restricts to the Frobenius of B_cris (R06.1/frobenius-on-acris), and N is Polynomial.derivative up to sign.
- `Bst_not_bcris` (non-example): u ∉ B_cris: N(u) = −1 ≠ 0.
- `Bst_sign_convention` (characterisation): With B-C's normalisation N_BC = v^♭(y_0)·d/dλ_st(y_0) one has N_BC = −N.

**Uses.** Brinon–Conrad §9.2: D_st(V) = (B_st ⊗ V)^{G_K} is a filtered (φ,N)-module. PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/period-functors: semistable representations and D_st. PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3 (part D): potentially semistable representations and the Weil–Deligne parameter from (D_st, φ, N). CohomologyComparisons:CP.4: semistable comparison with the Hyodo–Kato structure uses B_st with the same N-normalisation.

**Checks.** N(u^2) = −2u; φ(u^2) = p^2u^2; B_st^{N=0, φ=1} ⊇ B_cris^{φ=1}. Tate curve: for q ∈ m_K, q̃ ∈ O_C^♭ with q̃^♯ = q, λ_st(q̃) = v_p(q)u + λ(unit) and g(λ_st(q̃)) = λ_st(q̃) + η(g)t realises V_p(E_q) inside B_st (B-C Example 9.2.9).

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/crystalline-logarithm`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-crystalline-logarithm), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/crystalline-period-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-crystalline-period-ring), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/tilt-of-cp-and-special-elements`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-tilt-of-cp-and-special-elements), `mathlib:Polynomial.derivative`.

**Sources.** [O. Brinon and B. Conrad — CMI Summer School notes on p-adic Hodge theory](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/notes.pdf), Definition 9.2.3 and Remark 9.2.5, pp. 138–139. The construction; B-C define N = v_0·d/dX, the negative of the convention used here. [J.-M. Fontaine and Y. Ouyang — Theory of p-adic Galois representations](https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/~jean-marc.fontaine/prepub/theory_padic.pdf), Definition 6.15 and Propositions 6.16–6.17, p. 122. Fontaine–Ouyang's normalisation N(log[ϖ]) = −1, with ϖ^{(0)} = −p. [J.-M. Fontaine and Y. Ouyang — Theory of p-adic Galois representations](https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/~jean-marc.fontaine/prepub/theory_padic.pdf), Proposition 6.17, p. 122. The commutation relation.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-bst-embedding-into-bdr"></a>

### The embedding B_st → B_dR attached to log p = 0

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/bst-embedding-into-bdr` (construction).

For a choice of log_K with log_K(p) ∈ K_0 (R06.1/log-extension-to-kbar), there is a unique G_K-equivariant B_cris-algebra homomorphism ι_{log}: B_st → B_dR with ι(λ_st(y)) = log_dR([y]/y^♯) + log_K(y^♯) for y ∈ (C^♭)^× with y^♯ ∈ Q̄_p^×; on u = λ_st(p^♭) it gives ι(u) = log_dR([p^♭]/p) + log_K(p) = Σ_{n≥1}(−1)^{n+1}ξ^n/(np^n) + log_K(p). The image ι(B_st) does not depend on the choice of log_K(p) ∈ K_0, and with Iwasawa's choice log_K(p) = 0 the map depends only on C. ι(B_st^+) ⊆ B_dR^+ and ι commutes with φ only on B_cris (B_dR has no Frobenius). K ⊗_{K_0} B_st inherits via ι the subspace filtration.

**Hypotheses and scope.** log_K(p) ∈ K_0; ι injective by R06.1/k-tensor-bst-injective.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Define the homomorphism (C^♭)^× → B_dR^+ on the subgroup {y : y^♯ ∈ Q̄_p^×} (which surjects onto (C^♭)^×/(O_C^♭)^×) by log_dR([y]/y^♯) + log_K(y^♯); [y]/y^♯ is a 1-unit of B_dR^+ since θ([y]) = y^♯ ∈ K̄ ⊆ B_dR^+ (R06.1/algebraic-closure-in-bdr-plus).
2. It extends λ on units by R06.1/crystalline-logarithm (2), so the universal property of B_st^+ (R06.1/semistable-period-ring) gives ι.
3. Changing log_K(p) by c ∈ K_0 changes ι(u) by c ∈ K_0 ⊆ B_cris, so the image is unchanged (B-C text before Theorem 9.2.10).

**API.**

- `bstToBdR` (constructor): ι: B_st →+* B_dR for Iwasawa's log (log p = 0).
- `bstToBdR_u` (simp): ι(u) = Σ_{n≥1}(−1)^{n+1}ξ^n/(np^n).
- `bstToBdR_bcris` (compatibility): ι restricted to B_cris is the inclusion B_cris ⊆ B_dR.
- `bstToBdR_galois` (functoriality): ι(gb) = gι(b).
- `bstToBdR_range_independent` (other): For any log_K(p) ∈ K_0 the image of B_st in B_dR is the same subring.
- `bstToBdR_fil` (structure): Fil^i(K ⊗_{K_0} B_st) := (K ⊗ B_st) ∩ Fil^iB_dR via ι.

**Unit tests.**

- `bstToBdR_u_mod_fil2` (computation): ι(u) − ξ/p ∈ Fil^2B_dR.
- `bstToBdR_one` (degenerate): ι(1) = 1.
- `bstToBdR_theta` (compatibility): θ_dR(ι(u)) = 0 = log_K(p) (Iwasawa's choice), and θ_dR(ι(b)) = θ_cris(b) for b ∈ A_cris.
- `bstToBdR_not_frobenius` (non-example): There is no Frobenius on B_dR making ι φ-equivariant: φ(u) = pu but the image of ξ ∈ Fil^1 would have to satisfy φ(ξ) ∉ Fil^1.

**Uses.** Brinon–Conrad §9.2: the filtration on D_st(V)_K comes from K ⊗ B_st ⊆ B_dR. PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/period-functors: K ⊗_{K_0} D_st(V) ⊆ D_dR(V).

**Checks.** ι(u) ∈ Fil^0 and θ_dR(ι(u)) = log_K(p) = 0 with Iwasawa's choice; ι(u) ≡ ξ/p mod Fil^2.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/semistable-period-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-semistable-period-ring), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/crystalline-logarithm`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-crystalline-logarithm), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/galois-action-on-cp`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-galois-action-on-cp), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/complete-algebraically-closed-bdr`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-complete-algebraically-closed-bdr), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/bdr-natural-topology`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-bdr-natural-topology), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/crystalline-period-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-crystalline-period-ring).

**Proof ingredients.** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/log-extension-to-kbar`, `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/algebraic-closure-in-bdr-plus`; their statements and locators appear in the proof-ingredient index.

**Sources.** [O. Brinon and B. Conrad — CMI Summer School notes on p-adic Hodge theory](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/notes.pdf), §9.2, text before Theorem 9.2.10, p. 143. Independence of the image. [J.-M. Fontaine and Y. Ouyang — Theory of p-adic Galois representations](https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/~jean-marc.fontaine/prepub/theory_padic.pdf), §6.1.2, display (6.9), p. 119. F-O's logarithm with log[ϖ] = log([ϖ]/(−p)).

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-log-p-flat-transcendental"></a>

### log([p^♭]/p) is transcendental over Frac(B_cris)

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/log-p-flat-transcendental` (theorem).

The element ι(u) = log_dR([p^♭]/p) ∈ B_dR^+ does not lie in Frac(B_cris) (fraction field inside B_dR), and it is transcendental over Frac(B_cris) and over Frac(K ⊗_{K_0} B_cris).

**Hypotheses and scope.** B_cris ⊆ B_dR (R06.1/acris-embedding-injective).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Put β=ξ/p and let S be the bounded A_inf-coefficient series ring in β inside B_dR^+. The inclusion A_cris⊆S gives Frac(B_cris)⊆Frac(S). Establish p-adic separation of this S. Compare residues of the truncations of α log_dR([p^flat]/p), for α≠0, to prove that this product cannot lie in S; the bounded-coefficient residue argument is Fontaine–Ouyang Lemma 6.12 and Fontaine §4.3.2.
2. Transcendence (F-O Proposition 6.11): if d ≥ 1 is the degree of the minimal polynomial of ι(u) over C_cris = Frac(B_cris), applying g ∈ G_{K_0} (g ι(u) = ι(u) + c(g)t) and uniqueness of the minimal polynomial gives c := c_{d−1} + dι(u) ∈ B_dR^{G_{K_0}} = K_0, so ι(u) ∈ C_cris, contradicting the lemma.
3. Over Frac(K ⊗ B_cris), a finite extension of C_cris by R06.1/k-tensor-bcris-injective, transcendence persists.

**Checks.** ι(u) ∉ B_cris although t ∈ B_cris and g(ι(u)) − ι(u) ∈ Z_pt.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/bst-embedding-into-bdr`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-bst-embedding-into-bdr), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/k-tensor-bmax-injective`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-k-tensor-bmax-injective), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/k-tensor-bcris-injective`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-k-tensor-bcris-injective), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/de-rham-invariants`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-de-rham-invariants), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/crystalline-period-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-crystalline-period-ring).

**Sources.** [J.-M. Fontaine and Y. Ouyang — Theory of p-adic Galois representations](https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/~jean-marc.fontaine/prepub/theory_padic.pdf), §6.1.3, Proposition 6.11 and Lemma 6.12 with proofs, pp. 119–121. The proof, including the unproved separatedness claim. [O. Brinon and B. Conrad — CMI Summer School notes on p-adic Hodge theory](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/notes.pdf), Proof sketch of Theorem 9.2.10, p. 143. B-C identify the separatedness as the key point and refer to [21, §4.3.2–4.3.3].

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-k-tensor-bst-injective"></a>

### K ⊗_{K_0} B_st → B_dR is injective

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/k-tensor-bst-injective` (theorem).

For every choice of log_K(p) ∈ K_0, the G_K-equivariant K ⊗_{K_0} B_cris-algebra map K ⊗_{K_0} B_st → B_dR induced by ι is injective; hence B_cris ⊆ B_st ⊆ B_dR, K ⊗_{K_0} B_st carries the subspace filtration, and gr(K ⊗ B_st) → gr B_dR is injective.

**Hypotheses and scope.** log_K(p) ∈ K_0.

**Construction or proof.**

1. K ⊗_{K_0} B_st = (K ⊗_{K_0} B_cris)[u]; K ⊗ B_cris ⊆ B_dR (R06.1/k-tensor-bcris-injective) and ι(u) is transcendental over Frac(K ⊗ B_cris) (R06.1/log-p-flat-transcendental), so the polynomial ring embeds (F-O Theorem 6.14(2), B-C Theorem 9.2.10).
2. Changing log_K(p) ∈ K_0 changes ι(u) by an element of K_0, preserving transcendence.

**Checks.** The images of 1, u, u^2 are K ⊗ B_cris-linearly independent in B_dR.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/k-tensor-bcris-injective`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-k-tensor-bcris-injective), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/log-p-flat-transcendental`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-log-p-flat-transcendental), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/bst-embedding-into-bdr`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-bst-embedding-into-bdr).

**Sources.** [O. Brinon and B. Conrad — CMI Summer School notes on p-adic Hodge theory](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/notes.pdf), Theorem 9.2.10, p. 143. The statement (superscripts + dropped). [J.-M. Fontaine and Y. Ouyang — Theory of p-adic Galois representations](https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/~jean-marc.fontaine/prepub/theory_padic.pdf), Theorem 6.14(2) with proof, p. 121. F-O's proof, which presupposes injectivity of K ⊗ B_cris → B_dR (supplied here by R06.1/k-tensor-bcris-injective).

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-crystalline-semistable-invariants"></a>

### Galois invariants: (B_cris^+)^{G_K} = B_cris^{G_K} = B_st^{G_K} = Frac(B_st)^{G_K} = K_0

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/crystalline-semistable-invariants` (theorem).

For K/Q_p finite with maximal unramified subfield K_0 = W(k)[1/p]: K_0 = (B_cris^+)^{G_K} = B_cris^{G_K} = B_st^{G_K} = Frac(B_cris)^{G_K} = Frac(B_st)^{G_K}. More generally for any complete discretely valued K' ⊆ C, B_st^{G_{K'}} = K'_0 = W(k')[1/p].

**Hypotheses and scope.** log_K(p) ∈ K_0 (the invariants do not depend on it).

**Construction or proof.**

1. K_0 = W(k)[1/p] = (A_inf[1/p])^{G_K} ⊆ (B_cris^+)^{G_K} ⊆ … ⊆ Frac(B_st)^{G_K} (W(O_C^♭)^{G_K} = W((O_C^♭)^{G_K}) = W(k)).
2. By R06.1/k-tensor-bst-injective, K ⊗_{K_0} Frac(B_st)^{G_K} ⊆ B_dR^{G_K} = K (R06.1/de-rham-invariants); comparing K_0-dimensions forces Frac(B_st)^{G_K} = K_0 (F-O Theorem 6.14(1)).

**Checks.** B_cris^{G_{Q_p}} = Q_p; for K = Q_p(p^{1/2}), B_cris^{G_K} = Q_p ≠ K.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/k-tensor-bst-injective`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-k-tensor-bst-injective), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/de-rham-invariants`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-de-rham-invariants), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/semistable-period-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-semistable-period-ring).

**Sources.** [J.-M. Fontaine and Y. Ouyang — Theory of p-adic Galois representations](https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/~jean-marc.fontaine/prepub/theory_padic.pdf), Theorem 6.14(1) with proof, p. 121. The invariants follow from the injectivity K ⊗ B_st ↪ B_dR. [O. Brinon and B. Conrad — CMI Summer School notes on p-adic Hodge theory](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/notes.pdf), §8, introduction, p. 101. The same argument for B_cris.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-period-ring-invariants"></a>

### Galois invariants of the period rings

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/period-ring-invariants` (theorem).

Let K/Q_p be finite, K_0 its maximal unramified subfield. Then: (1) C^{G_K} = K and C(i)^{G_K} = 0 for i ≠ 0 (Tate); (2) B_HT^{G_K} = Frac(B_HT)^{G_K} = K; (3) (B_dR^+)^{G_K} = B_dR^{G_K} = K; (4) (B_cris^+)^{G_K} = B_cris^{G_K} = Frac(B_cris)^{G_K} = K_0 and B_st^{G_K} = Frac(B_st)^{G_K} = K_0; (5) (Fil^0B_cris)^{φ=1} = Q_p. The same holds with K replaced by any finite extension K' ⊆ K̄ (with K'_0) or by K̂^{ur} (with K̂_0^{ur}).

**Hypotheses and scope.** K/Q_p finite; the rings of R06.1.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): R06.1/tate-sen-theorem. (2): R06.1/hodge-tate-period-ring. (3): R06.1/de-rham-invariants. (4): R06.1/crystalline-semistable-invariants. (5): R06.1/fundamental-exact-sequence.
2. The rings depend only on C, so replacing K by K' or K̂^{ur} changes only the group (B-C Remark 4.4.9).

**Checks.** CohomologyComparisons CP.2 and MordellLawrenceVenkatesh LV.4 use B_cris^{G_K} = W(k)[1/p]: for K = Q_p this is Q_p. C(1)^{G_K} = 0: t̄ ∈ gr^1B_dR is not invariant since g(t) = χ(g)t.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/tate-sen-theorem`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-tate-sen-theorem), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/hodge-tate-period-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-hodge-tate-period-ring), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/de-rham-invariants`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-de-rham-invariants), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/crystalline-semistable-invariants`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-crystalline-semistable-invariants), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/fundamental-exact-sequence`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-fundamental-exact-sequence).

**Sources.** [J.-M. Fontaine and Y. Ouyang — Theory of p-adic Galois representations](https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/~jean-marc.fontaine/prepub/theory_padic.pdf), Proposition 6.28(2), p. 131. The crystalline and semistable invariants (superscripts G_K lost in extraction). [O. Brinon and B. Conrad — CMI Summer School notes on p-adic Hodge theory](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/notes.pdf), Example 5.1.3, p. 67. The de Rham invariants, including the fraction field.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-arithmetic-and-perfectoid-constructions-agree"></a>

### Fontaine's arithmetic construction of the period rings agrees with the perfectoid/Mathlib construction

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/arithmetic-and-perfectoid-constructions-agree` (comparison).

Let R_F = lim_{x↦x^p} O_{K̄}/p (Fontaine's ring R, built from the arithmetic object O_{K̄}) and let θ_F: W(R_F) → O_C, Σ[c_n]p^n ↦ Σ c_n^{(0)}p^n, be Fontaine's map. Then: (1) the reduction map O_{K̄}/p → O_C/p is an isomorphism and induces a G_K-equivariant ring isomorphism R_F ≅ PreTilt O_C p = O_C^♭ matching x ↦ x^{(0)} with PreTilt.untilt; (2) under W of this isomorphism θ_F corresponds to Mathlib's fontaineTheta (both are ring maps agreeing on Teichmüller lifts and p-adically continuous); (3) Fontaine's B_dR^+ = lim W(R_F)[1/p]/(ker θ_{F,Q})^j is G_K-equivariantly and filtered isomorphic to BDeRhamPlus 𝓞_ℂ_[p] p (R06.1/de-rham-period-ring) and to Scholze's B_dR^+(C, O_C) (R06.1/bdr-plus-of-perfectoid-affinoid-algebras), compatibly with θ; (4) Fontaine's A_cris (the p-adic completion of W(R_F)[ξ^m/m!]) is isomorphic to the p-completed PD envelope of (A_inf, ker θ) of CrystallineCohomology:CR.0, compatibly with θ, Frobenius and G_K; hence B_cris, B_st and their structures built from either presentation agree.

**Hypotheses and scope.** All identifications are G_K-equivariant; K enters only through G_K.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1) O_{K̄} is dense in O_C, so O_{K̄}/p = O_C/p; R(−) is functorial (B-C Proposition 4.3.1: R(O/pO) ≅ lim_{x↦x^p} O for p-adically complete O).
2. (2) Mathlib's fontaineTheta_teichmuller: θ([x]) = x.untilt; Fontaine's θ_F([x]) = x^{(0)}; both are ring maps W(R) → O_C, continuous for the p-adic topology, and W(R) is generated topologically by Teichmüller lifts over Z_p (every element is Σ p^n[x_n]).
3. (3) the two completions are the completion of the same localised ring along the same ideal (Localization.Away p and W(R)[1/p] agree); for Scholze's ring with (R, R^+) = (C, O_C) the definitions coincide literally (decomposition node, acceptance).
4. (4) A^0_cris = A_inf[ξ^m/m!] is the PD envelope of the regular principal ideal ξA_inf in the p-torsion free ring A_inf (the explicit envelope for regular principal ideals exported by CR.0; B-C Exercise 9.4.1(1)); p-adic completions agree; the Frobenius lifts agree because both extend the Witt Frobenius.

**Checks.** θ_F([p^♭]) = p = fontaineTheta([p^♭]); both kernels are generated by ξ = [p^♭] − p.

Conrad — CMI Summer School notes on p-adic Hodge theory](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/notes.pdf), §4.4, definition of θ, p. 56. Conrad — CMI Summer School notes on p-adic Hodge theory](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/notes.pdf), Exercise 9.4.1(1), p. 153. The PD envelope of (A_inf, ker θ) as A_inf[X^n/n!]/(X − ξ).

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-complete-algebraically-closed-bdr"></a>

### De Rham completion over an algebraically closed field

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/complete-algebraically-closed-bdr` (theorem).

Let C be a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field of mixed characteristic (0,p), with rank-one valuation and 0<|p|<1. On the existing carrier BDeRhamPlus(O_C,p), θ extends to a surjective map θ_dR:B_dR^+(C)→C. Its kernel is generated by the image of any generator ξ of ker(θ:A_inf(C)[1/p]→C). The ring is a complete DVR for this ideal, its residue field is C, and BDeRham(O_C,p) is canonically its fraction field. For C=ℂ_p the maps coincide with Mathlib’s fontaineTheta and its localization. The natural topology is the inverse-limit topology of the Banach quotients; it is distinguished from the discrete valuation topology.

**Hypotheses and scope.** C as above; O_C is the valuation ring, with the shared tilt and θ map; p-adic completeness refers to O_C, not to C.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Import principal-kernel and regular-generator properties of θ from AI.0:integral. Apply completion to A_inf[1/p], identify every ξ-adic quotient and its residue map, and prove separation and regularity. Use the associated graded C[ξ] to show that every nonzero element is a unit times a power of ξ. Identify Mathlib’s localization at all generators with localization at ξ, hence with the fraction field.

**Checks.** The residue is C rather than O_C; ξ is a nonunit in the completed ring although p is a unit. The statement applies to C beyond the completed algebraic closure of a finite extension of Q_p; no G_K-action is asserted without an action on C.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:BDeRhamPlus`, `mathlib:BDeRham`, `mathlib:fontaineThetaInvertP`, `mathlib:WittVector.fontaineTheta`, `AInfCohomology:AI.0:integral`.

**Sources.** [Peter Scholze — p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.3463v2), Definition 6.1, Lemma 6.3, Corollary 6.4, printed pp.35–36 (arXiv v2). The perfectoid completion and its principal residue ideal specialize at any complete algebraically closed field. [Jean-Marc Fontaine — Le corps des périodes p-adiques](https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_1994__223__59_0.pdf), §1.5–§1.6, pp.66–69. The residue map and discrete valuation structure follow from the principal regular kernel.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-breuil-completed-semistable-rings"></a>

### Breuil’s completed semistable periods

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/breuil-completed-semistable-rings` (construction).

For K a complete discretely valued field of mixed characteristic with perfect residue k and uniformizer π, put W=W(k), K_0=W[1/p]. Let R_l be the PD envelope of W[t]/p^l→O_K/p^l, t↦π, compatible with the canonical divided powers of p. Let P_l be H^0_log-cris((Spec(O_Kbar/p),O_Kbar∖{0})/(Spec R_l,N→R_l,1↦t)). Define S^min_0=lim_l R_l, 𝒦=S^min_0[1/p], Â_st=lim_l P_l and B̂_st^+=Â_st[1/p]. For compatible p-power roots of π, Â_st identifies with the p-adic completion of A_cris⟨X⟩. In these coordinates φ(X)=(1+X)^p−1, N(X)=1+X, g(X)=[ε_π(g)](1+X)−1, and the structural image of t is [π^flat](1+X)^−1. Thus N(t)=−t and φ(t)=t^p. This N convention gives Nφ=pφN; replacing the sign requires replacing it everywhere, including the B_st embedding.

**Hypotheses and scope.** All divided powers are compatible with those on p; P_l uses logarithmic crystalline cohomology from CR.6. The name t in R_l is a polynomial variable; Fontaine’s period is denoted t_Fontaine when both occur.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Use the universal PD and log-crystalline objects supplied by CR.0 and CR.6. Compute P_l after choosing roots of π as W_l(O_Kbar/p)^DP⟨X⟩ with the transition maps specified by Frobenius on Witt coordinates. Pass to inverse limits, then invert p. Transport the canonical operators and check independence of the chosen roots by the coordinate change X↦[ε]^{-1}(1+X′)−1.

**API.**

- `BreuilPeriods.transition` (data): Reduction P_{l+1}→P_l respects the structural R_{l+1}→R_l map.
- `BreuilPeriods.coordinate_change` (compatibility): The coordinate change attached to a different root system intertwines φ,N and G_K.
- `BreuilPeriods.phi_monodromy` (relation): Nφ=pφN on both 𝒦 and B̂_st^+.
- `BreuilPeriods.specialize_zero` (projection): The map 𝒦→K_0 sends the structural polynomial variable to 0 and commutes with φ.
- `BreuilPeriods.invariants` (characterisation): (B̂_st^+)^{G_K}=𝒦 via the structural embedding.

**Unit tests.**

- `BreuilPeriods.base_variable` (computation): For u=[π^flat]/(1+X), N(u)=−u and φ(u)=u^p; u is G_K-invariant.
- `BreuilPeriods.monodromy_constant` (degenerate): N vanishes on A_cris but N(X)=1+X, so it is not zero on Â_st.
- `BreuilPeriods.pd_coordinate` (non-example): X^{[p]} is present integrally; the ordinary polynomial algebra A_cris[X] is not the completed PD carrier.
- `BreuilPeriods.roots` (compatibility): A changed root system gives the displayed affine coordinate transformation and leaves u unchanged.

**Uses.** Disegni–Liu Lemmas B.13–B.14: Computes the coefficient ring, invariant sections and two connecting homomorphisms.. Breuil Theorem 3.3: Compares semistable representations with completed semistable periods..

**Checks.** Changing roots transports the ring and all operators; it does not change its isomorphism class.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/crystalline-period-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-crystalline-period-ring), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.6`.

**Sources.** [Christophe Breuil — Représentations p-adiques semi-stables et transversalité de Griffiths](https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/~christophe.breuil/PUBLICATIONS/Griffiths.pdf), §2, pp.3–6; §4.1, pp.8–9 in author copy. Defines the log-crystalline inverse limit, the PD coordinates, and the invariant base ring. [Daniel Disegni and Yifeng Liu — A p-adic arithmetic inner product formula](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2204.09239), §B.5 preceding Lemma B.13, pp.91–92 in arXiv copy. Uses these inverse limits as the period rings for monodromy edge maps.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-breuil-nilpotent-period-comparison"></a>

### Nilpotent and completed semistable periods

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/breuil-nilpotent-period-comparison` (theorem).

With these rings, B_st^+ identifies canonically with the elements of B̂_st^+ killed by some power of N. The ring B̂_st^+ is flat over 𝒦, N:B̂_st^+→B̂_st^+ is surjective, and its G_K-invariants are 𝒦. For a finite-dimensional (φ,N)-module D with nilpotent N, the diagonal-monodromy sequences 0→(D⊗B_st^+)^{N=0}→D⊗B_st^+→D⊗B_st^+→0 and 0→(D⊗B̂_st^+)^{N=0}→D⊗B̂_st^+→D⊗B̂_st^+→0 are exact and their left terms agree.

**Hypotheses and scope.** K,π and compatible period embeddings as in the construction; N on D is nilpotent.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Identify the N-nilpotent coordinate subring with polynomials in log(1+X), then compare with the chosen B_st^+ coordinate. Use the flatness theorem for completed log-crystalline periods. Derive surjectivity by solving N at each P_l and proving R^1lim ker N_l=0. Apply exp(−log(1+X)N_D) to reduce the tensor-monodromy statement to scalar periods.

**Checks.** For D=K_0 and N=0 the two kernels are B_cris^+. Flatness and the inverse-limit vanishing are required; pointwise surjectivity alone is insufficient.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/breuil-completed-semistable-rings`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-breuil-completed-semistable-rings), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/semistable-period-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-semistable-period-ring).

**Sources.** [Daniel Disegni and Yifeng Liu — A p-adic arithmetic inner product formula](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2204.09239), Lemma B.13 and following diagram, pp.91–92. States the nilpotent-part comparison, flatness and surjectivity, then derives the two exact rows. [Christophe Breuil — Représentations p-adiques semi-stables et transversalité de Griffiths](https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/~christophe.breuil/PUBLICATIONS/Griffiths.pdf), §2 and Corollary 4.1.3, pp.3–6,9. Supplies coordinates and identifies the invariant coefficient ring.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-breuil-frobenius-edge-factorization"></a>

### Frobenius-isotypic monodromy edge maps

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/breuil-frobenius-edge-factorization` (theorem).

For every integer r and nilpotent finite-dimensional (φ,N)-module D, the edge map ((D⊗_{K_0}𝒦)/N(D⊗𝒦))^{φ=p^r}→H^1(G_K,(D⊗B_st^+)^{N=0}) coming from the completed-monodromy row factors through specialization t↦0 to D/ND. The map is compared with the edge map of the B_st^+ row through the common N=0 term. No factorization of an unrestricted monodromy cokernel, and no equality of invariant images of N, is asserted.

**Hypotheses and scope.** The period embedding and sign convention of the completed-period comparison are fixed.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Take continuous G_K-cohomology of the two exact rows and compare their connecting maps by naturality. Restrict to φ=p^r. Apply the specialization computation in Lemma B.14; the restriction is essential.

**Checks.** The case D=K_0,r=0 includes constants but does not identify ker(𝒦→K_0) with N of invariant completed periods.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/breuil-nilpotent-period-comparison`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-breuil-nilpotent-period-comparison), `ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.1`.

**Sources.** [Daniel Disegni and Yifeng Liu — A p-adic arithmetic inner product formula](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2204.09239), Lemma B.14 and Remark B.15, p.92. Proves the restricted factorization and explicitly leaves the stronger invariant-image question open.

### Worked example — Two different uniformizers

In B_dR^+(C), the scalar p is a unit because the construction completes A_inf[1/p]. A generator ξ of ker θ remains a nonunit, and its quotient is C. After choosing ε, t=log[ε] generates the same ideal: t/ξ is a unit. Consequently gr^i B_dR≅C(i), with Galois action g(t)=χ_p(g)t. On the crystalline subring φ(t)=pt. In B_st=B_cris[u], choose N(u)=−1 and φ(u)=pu; then Nφ(u)=−p=pφN(u). The map u↦log_dR([p^flat]/p) depends on the chosen logarithm convention, while its algebraic independence supplies the embedding. These computations distinguish p-adic completion of integral periods from θ-adic completion after rationalization.


<a id="layer-p7-annulus-foundations"></a>

## P7:annulus-foundations — Analytic coefficient rings

Use bilateral Laurent series on specified radius intervals. Restriction, coefficient extension and localization preserve the convergence conditions and the endpoint topology. The Robba ring is a germ near the outer boundary, whereas the Amice ring allows a different negative-tail convergence condition. Neither is supplied by a one-sided formal power series carrier.

**Landmarks:** Ring of analytic functions on an annulus; Robba ring; Amice ring; Overconvergent cyclotomic rings; Cyclotomic Frobenius; Cyclotomic Gamma-action.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p7-annulus-foundations-plan-annulus-laurent-ring"></a>

### The ring O_K(I) of Laurent series convergent on an annulus

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/plan/annulus-laurent-ring` (definition).

For K as in the hypotheses and a nonempty interval I in (0, infinity), O_K(I) is the set of two-sided coefficient families a : Z -> K such that |a_n| rho^n -> 0 as |n| -> infinity for every rho in I (the Laurent series sum_{n in Z} a_n T^n converging on the annulus {|T| in I}). It is a K-submodule of the K-module of all families Z -> K, and a commutative K-algebra under the Cauchy product (fg)_n = sum_{i+j=n} a_i b_j, each such sum converging absolutely in K. It contains the Laurent polynomials K[T, T^{-1}] as a K-subalgebra, and T is a unit with inverse T^{-1}. For an annulus with centre e in K (ColemanIntegration's A(e; r, s) with 0 <= r < s <= infinity) one takes I = (r, s) and reads T as z - e; the ring does not depend on e.

**Hypotheses and scope.** K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| (Kedlaya–Liu's 'analytic field'); O_K = {|x| <= 1}, m_K = {|x| < 1}, k = O_K/m_K. Characteristic 0 is assumed only where stated. I is a nonempty interval contained in (0, +infinity): open, closed or half-open, possibly a single point, possibly unbounded above. The radius variable rho ranges over I. No condition relates I to the value group |K^x|; for closed endpoints outside the divisible hull of |K^x| the ring is still defined (Berkovich's convention, Kedlaya overview Remark 3.2.4).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Submodule: the condition is preserved by sums (ultrametric inequality |a_n + b_n| rho^n <= max) and scalar multiples.
2. Convergence of the Cauchy product: for fixed n and rho in I, |a_i b_{n-i}| = (|a_i| rho^i)(|b_{n-i}| rho^{n-i}) rho^{-n} tends to 0 as |i| -> infinity, so the sum converges in the complete field K (Lazard 1962, Proposition 1 and (2.3)-(2.4)).
3. Closure: |c_n| rho^n <= sup_i (|a_i| rho^i)(|b_{n-i}| rho^{n-i}), and for |n| large at least one of |i|, |n - i| is large, so |c_n| rho^n -> 0.
4. Ring axioms: associativity, commutativity and distributivity are identities of absolutely convergent double sums in a complete nonarchimedean field (Mathlib's DiscreteConvolution.ringConvolution API, additive version, and the Tau Ceti convolution lemmas for two-sided restricted families).
5. T and T^{-1} are the families concentrated in degree 1 and -1; their product is the unit family.

**API.**

- `annulusCoeffs` (constructor): The K-submodule of Z -> K of families with |a_n| rho^n -> 0 along the cofinite filter of Z for every rho in I.
- `AnnulusRing` (data): The type O_K(I) of elements of annulusCoeffs K I.
- `AnnulusRing.coeff` (projection): The coefficient family f -> (a_n)_{n in Z}.
- `AnnulusRing.ext` (extensionality): Two elements with the same coefficients are equal.
- `AnnulusRing.instCommRing` (instance): Commutative ring structure with the Cauchy product; K-algebra structure through constants.
- `AnnulusRing.coeff_mul` (simp): coeff (f * g) n = sum over i + j = n of coeff f i * coeff g j (an absolutely convergent sum).
- `AnnulusRing.T` (constructor): The coordinate T (coefficient family Pi.single 1 1).
- `AnnulusRing.T_isUnit` (characterisation): T is a unit with inverse the family Pi.single (-1) 1.
- `AnnulusRing.C` (constructor): Constants c in K (family Pi.single 0 c); C is the algebra map.
- `AnnulusRing.ofLaurentPolynomial` (coercion): The injective K-algebra map K[T, T^{-1}] -> O_K(I) (Mathlib LaurentPolynomial).
- `AnnulusRing.annulusCoeffs_antitone` (relation): If I is contained in J then annulusCoeffs K J <= annulusCoeffs K I.
- `AnnulusRing.annulusCoeffs_one_eq_twoSidedRestricted` (compatibility): annulusCoeffs K {1} = TauCeti.Huber.twoSidedRestrictedSubmodule K K, and the product is twoSidedRestrictedMul.

**Unit tests.**

- `AnnulusRing.test_T_mul_Tinv` (computation): In O_K(I), T * T^{-1} = 1, i.e. Pi.single 1 1 convolved with Pi.single (-1) 1 is Pi.single 0 1.
- `AnnulusRing.test_geometric` (computation): In O_K((0,1)) the family a_n = 1 (n >= 0), 0 (n < 0) lies in the ring and (1 - T) times it equals 1.
- `AnnulusRing.test_geometric_not_mem` (non-example): The family a_n = 1 (n >= 0), 0 (n < 0) does not lie in O_K({1}): its coefficients do not tend to 0. A definition requiring convergence only as n -> +infinity fails this.
- `AnnulusRing.test_unit_circle` (compatibility): annulusCoeffs K {1} equals TauCeti.Huber.twoSidedRestrictedSubmodule K K.
- `AnnulusRing.test_polynomial_mem` (degenerate): Every Laurent polynomial (finitely supported family) lies in annulusCoeffs K I for every I.

**Uses.** ColemanIntegration:L0/annulus-residue: the carrier O_K(A(e; r, s)) whose T^{-1}-coefficient is the residue. ColemanIntegration:L0/annulus-exact-iff-residue-zero: termwise integration inside O_K(I). PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/robba-ring: the rings of functions on annuli whose union is the Robba ring, compared with Kedlaya analytic rings. Berger 2002, Section 2 (H_F^alpha) and Proposition 2.31: B^{dagger,r}_{rig,K} is identified with such a ring in the variable pi_K. Kedlaya–Liu, Definition 4.1.2: R^r_K is O_K([omega^r, 1)).

**Checks.** For rho = 1 the coefficient submodule of O_K({1}) equals Tau Ceti's twoSidedRestrictedSubmodule K K and the product equals twoSidedRestrictedMul. In O_K((0,1)): (1 - T) * sum_{n >= 0} T^n = 1, while sum_{n >= 0} T^n is not in O_K({1}).

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:DiscreteConvolution.ringConvolution`, `mathlib:LaurentPolynomial`, `mathlib:IsUltrametricDist`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.twoSidedRestrictedSubmodule`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.twoSidedRestrictedMul`.

**Sources.** [K. Kedlaya and R. Liu — Relative p-adic Hodge theory: Foundations](https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.0792v5), Definition 4.1.2, p. 103. Kedlaya–Liu's R^r_K is O_K([omega^r, 1)) in this notation. [K. Kedlaya and R. Liu — Relative p-adic Hodge theory: Foundations](https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.0792v5), Definition 4.1.2, p. 103. The ring structure by formal (Cauchy) multiplication. [K. S. Kedlaya — Local monodromy of p-adic differential equations: an overview](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0501361v2), Definition 3.2.1, p. 10. Rings of functions on annuli A(I) as Laurent series. [M. Lazard — Les zéros des fonctions analytiques d’une variable sur un corps valué complet](http://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1962__14__47_0/), Proposition 1, p. 50 (numdam OCR layer). Lazard's L_K I is O_K(I) written in the valuation variable mu = -log rho; Proposition 1 makes it a ring (integral domain).

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p7-annulus-foundations-plan-gauss-norm"></a>

### The rho-Gauss norm |.|_rho

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/plan/gauss-norm` (definition).

For rho > 0 and a coefficient family a : Z -> K put |a|_rho = sup_n |a_n| rho^n in [0, infinity]. For f in O_K(I) and rho in I, |f|_rho is finite, for f≠0 the supremum is a maximum attained on a nonempty finite set of indices (the dominant indices D(f, rho), with least element n(f, rho) and greatest element N(f, rho)), and |.|_rho is a norm on the K-vector space O_K(I): |f|_rho = 0 iff f = 0, |f + g|_rho <= max(|f|_rho, |g|_rho), |c f|_rho = |c| |f|_rho, and |a_n| rho^n <= |f|_rho (Cauchy inequality); |T^n|_rho = rho^n.

**Hypotheses and scope.** K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| (Kedlaya–Liu's 'analytic field'); O_K = {|x| <= 1}, m_K = {|x| < 1}, k = O_K/m_K. Characteristic 0 is assumed only where stated. I is a nonempty interval contained in (0, +infinity): open, closed or half-open, possibly a single point, possibly unbounded above. The radius variable rho ranges over I.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Finiteness and attainment: |a_n| rho^n -> 0 as |n| -> infinity, so only finitely many n have |a_n| rho^n >= |f|_rho / 2 when f != 0; the supremum over this finite set is attained.
2. Norm axioms are coefficientwise consequences of the ultrametric inequality in K.
3. For f supported in n >= 0 the value agrees with Mathlib's PowerSeries.gaussNorm (norm, rho) of the corresponding power series (PowerSeries.gaussNorm_eq).

**API.**

- `gaussNorm` (data): |a|_rho = iSup over n of |a n| * rho^n.
- `gaussNorm_nonneg` (other): 0 <= |f|_rho.
- `AnnulusRing.gaussNorm_eq_zero_iff` (characterisation): For rho in I and f in O_K(I): |f|_rho = 0 iff f = 0.
- `AnnulusRing.gaussNorm_add_le` (relation): |f + g|_rho <= max(|f|_rho, |g|_rho).
- `AnnulusRing.gaussNorm_smul` (simp): |c f|_rho = |c| |f|_rho.
- `AnnulusRing.gaussNorm_T_zpow` (simp): |T^n|_rho = rho^n for n in Z.
- `AnnulusRing.norm_coeff_mul_le_gaussNorm` (relation): |a_n| rho^n <= |f|_rho (Cauchy inequality).
- `AnnulusRing.exists_dominant` (characterisation): For f != 0 and rho in I the set of n with |a_n| rho^n = |f|_rho is finite and nonempty.
- `AnnulusRing.gaussNorm_eq_powerSeries_gaussNorm` (compatibility): For f with a_n = 0 for n < 0, |f|_rho = PowerSeries.gaussNorm (fun x => |x|) rho f.

**Unit tests.**

- `gaussNorm.test_one_add_T` (computation): |1 + T|_rho = max(1, rho).
- `gaussNorm.test_constant` (degenerate): |C c|_rho = |c| for every rho.
- `gaussNorm.test_not_pointwise` (non-example): If varpi in K has |varpi| = rho, then |varpi - T|_rho = rho > 0 although the series vanishes at T = varpi: the Gauss norm is not the absolute value at a point.
- `gaussNorm.test_powerSeries` (compatibility): For a power series f (no negative coefficients), gaussNorm rho f = PowerSeries.gaussNorm (fun x => |x|) rho f.
- `gaussNorm.zero_dominance` (non-example): The zero series has norm zero, and every integer is a maximizing index; the finite nonempty dominant set assertion requires f≠0.

**Uses.** ColemanIntegration:L0/annulus-log-transcendence: Gauss norms detect the dominant monomial on a sub-annulus. PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/robba-ring: w_s(f) = -log_{|pi|} |f|_{|pi|^s} compares Kedlaya's partial valuations with the Gauss norm. Berger 2002, Section 2.1 (valuations V_I): the norms defining the Frechet topology of B^{dagger,r}_{rig}.

**Checks.** |1 + T|_rho = max(1, rho); for |varpi| = rho < 1, |varpi - T|_rho = rho although varpi - T vanishes at T = varpi.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/plan/annulus-laurent-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-annulus-foundations-plan-annulus-laurent-ring), `mathlib:PowerSeries.gaussNorm`, `mathlib:IsUltrametricDist`.

**Sources.** [K. S. Kedlaya — Local monodromy of p-adic differential equations: an overview](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0501361v2), Definition 3.2.1, p. 10. Lazard — Les zéros des fonctions analytiques d’une variable sur un corps valué complet](http://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1962__14__47_0/), (1.7), p. 49 (numdam OCR).
