<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p7-annulus-foundations-plan-cyclotomic-log-robba-ring"></a>

### The logarithmic Robba ring B^dagger_{log,F} = B^dagger_{rig,F}[log pi]

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/plan/cyclotomic-log-robba-ring` (construction).

B^dagger_{log,F} = B^dagger_{rig,F}[l] is the polynomial ring in one variable l = 'log pi', with: phi extended by phi(l) = p l + log(phi(pi)/pi^p), where phi(pi)/pi^p - 1 has Gauss norm < 1 on (p^{-1/(p-1)}, 1) so the logarithm lies in B^{dagger,r}_F for r > p - 1; gamma_a extended by gamma_a(l) = l + log(gamma_a(pi)/pi) with log(gamma_a(pi)/pi) = log_p(a) + log(1 + h_a) in B^+_{rig,F} (log_p the Iwasawa logarithm on Z_p^x, h_a as in cyclotomic-gamma-action); partial extended by partial(l) = (1+pi)/pi; and the monodromy operator N = -(p/(p-1)) d/dl, the B^dagger_{rig,F}-linear derivation with N(l) = -p/(p-1). These satisfy N phi = p phi N, N gamma_a = gamma_a N, N partial = partial N, gamma_a gamma_b = gamma_{ab}, gamma_a phi = phi gamma_a, partial phi = p phi partial, and ker N = B^dagger_{rig,F}.

**Hypotheses and scope.** p is a prime, k a perfect field of characteristic p, F = W(k)[1/p] with |p| = p^{-1} and sigma its Witt vector Frobenius (an isometric automorphism of F); pi is a variable. zeta_{p^n} (n >= 1) is a compatible system of primitive p^n-th roots of unity in a fixed algebraic closure of F (the epsilon of the shared conventions), F_n = F(zeta_{p^n}), F_infinity = union of the F_n, and chi : Gal(F_infinity/F) -> Z_p^x the cyclotomic character, an isomorphism since F/Q_p is unramified. Berger's radius convention: for r > 0, C[r;1[ = {z : p^{-1/r} <= |z| < 1}; r_n = p^{n-1}(p-1), so that |zeta_{p^n} - 1| = p^{-1/r_n}. Normalisation: Berger 2002 uses N = -d/dl; Berger 2008 Appendix B corrects it to N(l) = -p/(p-1) so that the comparison with Fontaine's N = -d/du on B_st (u = log[p~], p~^{(0)} = p) holds; this node uses the corrected normalisation. If R06.1 normalises u differently, the scalar changes accordingly (PadicHodgeTheory:P7/plan/berger-dcris-dst-dictionary).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Convergence: phi(pi)/pi^p = 1 + h with h = sum_{i=1}^{p-1} binom(p,i) pi^{i-p}, |h|_rho = p^{-1} rho^{1-p} < 1 for rho > p^{-1/(p-1)} and bounded by a constant < 1 on [rho_0, 1); log(1+h) = sum (-1)^{k-1} h^k/k converges and is bounded (gauss-norm-maximum-principle, frechet-topology). For gamma_a: |h_a|_rho <= rho, so log(1 + h_a) converges on the open unit disc.
2. Well defined ring endomorphisms: extension of ring maps to a polynomial ring by choosing the image of l. Cocycle identities: gamma_a gamma_b(l) = gamma_{ab}(l) because gamma_{ab}(pi)/pi = gamma_a(gamma_b(pi)/pi) gamma_a(pi)/pi and log is a homomorphism on these units; gamma_a phi(l) = phi gamma_a(l) similarly.
3. N phi = p phi N: N(phi(l)) = p N(l) = -p^2/(p-1) = p phi(N(l)); the other relations are checked on l and on B^dagger_{rig,F} (where N = 0).
4. partial extended by partial(l) = (1+pi)/pi is compatible with phi: partial(phi(l)) = p (1+pi)^p/((1+pi)^p - 1) = p phi((1+pi)/pi).

**API.**

- `CycRing.LogRing` (data): B^dagger_{log,F} = Polynomial (B^dagger_{rig,F}), with l = X.
- `CycRing.logPhi` (constructor): phi on B^dagger_{log,F} with phi(l) = p l + log(phi(pi)/pi^p).
- `CycRing.logGamma` (constructor): gamma_a on B^dagger_{log,F} with gamma_a(l) = l + log(gamma_a(pi)/pi).
- `CycRing.monodromyN` (constructor): N = -(p/(p-1)) d/dl, a B^dagger_{rig,F}-linear derivation.
- `CycRing.monodromyN_phi` (relation): N o phi = p phi o N.
- `CycRing.monodromyN_gamma` (relation): N o gamma_a = gamma_a o N.
- `CycRing.ker_monodromyN` (characterisation): ker N = B^dagger_{rig,F}.
- `CycRing.logPartial` (constructor): partial extended by partial(l) = (1+pi)/pi, commuting with N.

**Unit tests.**

- `log.test_N_phi` (computation): N(phi(l)) = p phi(N(l)) = -p^2/(p-1).
- `log.test_gamma_cocycle` (computation): gamma_a(gamma_b(l)) = gamma_{ab}(l).
- `log.test_ker_N` (degenerate): N vanishes exactly on B^dagger_{rig,F} (degree 0 polynomials).
- `log.test_not_in_Brig` (non-example): No element f of B^dagger_{rig,F} satisfies partial f = (1+pi)/pi, so l must be adjoined as a new variable.
- `log.test_kedlaya` (compatibility): With u = pi and q = p, phi(l) = q l + log(phi(u)/u^q) is the Frobenius of RD.2/log-robba-ring.

**Uses.** PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/berger-form-of-local-monodromy: B^dagger_{log,K} = B^dagger_{rig,K}[log pi], the solution ring of the monodromy theorem. PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/log-robba-ring: Kedlaya's R_log = R[log u] with u = pi and q = p is this ring (same phi, derivation and N up to the scalar p/(p-1)). PadicHodgeTheory:P7/plan/berger-dcris-dst-dictionary: D_st(V) = (D^dagger_log(V)[1/t])^{Gamma_K}. PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/plan/p-adic-monodromy-theorem: quasi-unipotence is solved in B^dagger_{log,L}.

**Checks.** N(l) = -p/(p-1), N(phi(l)) = -p^2/(p-1) = p phi(N(l)).

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/plan/overconvergent-cyclotomic-rings`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-annulus-foundations-plan-overconvergent-cyclotomic-rings), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/plan/cyclotomic-frobenius`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-annulus-foundations-plan-cyclotomic-frobenius), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/plan/cyclotomic-gamma-action`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-annulus-foundations-plan-cyclotomic-gamma-action), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/plan/cyclotomic-derivation`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-annulus-foundations-plan-cyclotomic-derivation), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/plan/gauss-norm`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-annulus-foundations-plan-gauss-norm), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/plan/frechet-topology`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-annulus-foundations-plan-frechet-topology), `mathlib:Polynomial`, `mathlib:Derivation`.

**Proof ingredients.** `PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/gauss-norm-maximum-principle`; their statements and locators appear in the proof-ingredient index.

**Sources.** [L. Berger — Représentations p-adiques et équations différentielles](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0102179v3), Section 2.6, p. 29. Definition of B^dagger_{log,K}. [L. Berger — Représentations p-adiques et équations différentielles](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0102179v3), Section 2.6, p. 29. phi(log pi) = p log pi + log(phi(pi)/pi^p) and gamma(log pi) = log pi + log(gamma(pi)/pi). [L. Berger — Équations différentielles p-adiques et (φ,N)-modules filtrés](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0406601v1), Appendice B, Erratum à [Ber02], p. 27. The corrected normalisation of N.

### Worked example — Endpoint and dominant-term tests

For 0<ρ<1, f(T)=T^{−1}+p has |f|_ρ=max(ρ^{−1},|p|)=ρ^{−1}. The negative exponent must contribute: a one-sided series model cannot represent f. The zero series has norm zero and every integer maximizes its coefficient contribution, so a finite nonempty set of dominant exponents is asserted only for f≠0. The series Σ_{n≥0}T^n converges at every radius below one and gives (1−T)^{−1}, but its terms do not tend to zero at radius one. Thus convergence on an open annulus is different from convergence on a closed annulus containing that endpoint. Under cyclotomic Frobenius T↦(1+T)^p−1, the period log(1+T) becomes p log(1+T); the localization at the n-th root tower therefore sends it to t/p^n.


<a id="layer-r06-2"></a>

## R06.2 — Period functors and admissibility

Give the admissible period functors their exact tensor and filtration theory, including perfect residue fields beyond finite local fields. The analytic Colmez–Fontaine construction supplies weak admissibility versus admissibility independently of the differential monodromy theorem. Coefficient characters, regular ordinary flags, reductive fiber functors and almost C-period realizations use the same conventions.

**Landmarks:** Fontaine's period functors; Hodge–Tate decomposition; Filtered (φ,N)-modules; Fundamental period complex; Colmez–Fontaine theorem; Regular ordinary flags.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-regular-period-ring"></a>

### (F, G)-regular rings

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/regular-period-ring` (definition).

Let F be a field, G a group, and B an F-algebra which is a domain with an action of G by F-algebra automorphisms such that E := B^G is a field; let C = Frac(B) with the induced G-action. B is (F, G)-regular if (i) C^G = B^G, and (ii) every nonzero b ∈ B such that the F-line Fb is G-stable is a unit of B.

**Hypotheses and scope.** No topology on F, G or B is required (B-C §5.1).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Definition; the G-action extends to C by g(b_1/b_2) = g(b_1)/g(b_2).

**API.**

- `IsRegularPeriodRing` (structure): The predicate: B a domain, (Frac B)^G = B^G, and nonzero b spanning a G-stable F-line is a unit.
- `IsRegularPeriodRing.of_isField` (instance): A field with G-action is regular.
- `IsRegularPeriodRing.invariants_isField` (characterisation): If B is regular then B^G is a field (hypothesis) equal to (Frac B)^G.
- `IsRegularPeriodRing.unit_of_stable_line` (projection): The unit property for stable lines.
- `IsRegularPeriodRing.character_of_stable_line` (other): A G-stable F-line Fb defines a character η: G → F^× with g(b) = η(g)b.

**Unit tests.**

- `isRegularPeriodRing_field` (degenerate): A field L with a G-action by F-algebra automorphisms is (F, G)-regular.
- `isRegularPeriodRing_BdR` (compatibility): B_dR = BDeRham 𝓞_ℂ_[p] p with the G_K-action is (Q_p, G_K)-regular (it is a field).
- `not_isRegularPeriodRing_BdRPlus` (non-example): B_dR^+ with the G_K-action is not (Q_p, G_K)-regular: t is a non-unit spanning a stable line.
- `isRegularPeriodRing_polynomial_trivial` (computation): F[X] with trivial G-action is not regular (X spans a stable line and is not a unit), while F(X) is.

**Uses.** Brinon–Conrad Theorem 5.2.1: the admissibility formalism requires B regular. PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/period-rings-are-regular: B_HT, B_dR, B_cris, B_st are regular. PadicHodgeRegulators:L0: realisations of Galois representations in regular period rings.

**Checks.** Every field with a G-action is (F, G)-regular. B_dR^+ is not (Q_p, G_K)-regular: t spans a G_K-stable Q_p-line but is not a unit (B-C Example 5.1.3).

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:IsDomain`, `mathlib:FractionRing`.

**Sources.** [O. Brinon and B. Conrad — CMI Summer School notes on p-adic Hodge theory](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/notes.pdf), §5.1, Definition 5.1.1, p. 66. The definition. [J.-M. Fontaine and Y. Ouyang — Theory of p-adic Galois representations](https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/~jean-marc.fontaine/prepub/theory_padic.pdf), §2.1.2, Definition 2.8, p. 21. Same definition in F-O.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-admissibility-dimension-bound"></a>

### The comparison map α_V is injective and dim_E D_B(V) ≤ dim_F V

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/admissibility-dimension-bound` (theorem).

Let B be (F, G)-regular with E = B^G, V a finite-dimensional F-linear representation of G, and D_B(V) = (B ⊗_F V)^G. Then the B-linear G-equivariant map α_V: B ⊗_E D_B(V) → B ⊗_F V is injective, dim_E D_B(V) ≤ dim_F V, and equality holds if and only if α_V is an isomorphism (V is then called B-admissible). Equivalently V is B-admissible iff B ⊗_F V ≅ B^{dim V} compatibly with the B-module structure and the G-action.

**Hypotheses and scope.** B (F, G)-regular (R06.2/regular-period-ring).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Injectivity: reduce to C = Frac(B) (flat over B) since D_B(V) ⊆ D_C(V) and E = C^G; for B a field, G-invariant E-linearly independent x_i are B-linearly independent: a minimal relation x_r = Σ_{i<r} b_i x_i is G-stable, so b_i ∈ B^G = E.
2. Dimension bound: compare C-dimensions after the flat base change.
3. Equality ⇒ isomorphism: the determinant of α_V in bases spans a G-stable F-line (G acts on det through det V^{-1}), hence is a unit by regularity (B-C Theorem 5.2.1(1)).
4. Alternative description: B-C Remark 5.2.3.

**Checks.** V = F (trivial): D_B(F) = E and α is the identity.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/regular-period-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-regular-period-ring), `mathlib:Representation.invariants`, `mathlib:Representation.tprod`.

**Sources.** [O. Brinon and B. Conrad — CMI Summer School notes on p-adic Hodge theory](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/notes.pdf), Theorem 5.2.1(1) with proof, pp. 68–70. The statement. [J.-M. Fontaine and Y. Ouyang — Theory of p-adic Galois representations](https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/~jean-marc.fontaine/prepub/theory_padic.pdf), §2.1.2, Theorem 2.13, p. 22. F-O's version of the same formalism.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-admissible-category-tannakian"></a>

### B-admissible representations form a Tannakian subcategory on which D_B is exact, faithful and tensor

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/admissible-category-tannakian` (theorem).

For B (F, G)-regular: (1) D_B restricted to B-admissible representations is exact and faithful into finite-dimensional E-vector spaces; subrepresentations and quotients of B-admissible representations are B-admissible. (2) If V_1, V_2 are B-admissible, D_B(V_1) ⊗_E D_B(V_2) ≅ D_B(V_1 ⊗ V_2), so V_1 ⊗ V_2 is B-admissible; V^∨ is B-admissible and D_B(V) ⊗ D_B(V^∨) → D_B(F) = E is a perfect pairing; exterior and symmetric powers are B-admissible and D_B commutes with them; in particular D_B(det V) = det D_B(V).

**Hypotheses and scope.** B (F, G)-regular.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1) α_V is an isomorphism for admissible V, so exactness can be tested after B ⊗_E −; a short exact sequence gives dim D_B(V) ≤ dim D_B(V') + dim D_B(V'') ≤ dim V' + dim V'' = dim V, forcing equalities.
2. (2) The natural map D_B(V_1) ⊗ D_B(V_2) → D_B(V_1 ⊗ V_2) composed with the inclusion into B ⊗ (V_1 ⊗ V_2) equals α_{V_1} ⊗_B α_{V_2} restricted, hence injective; dimensions force isomorphism. Exterior/symmetric powers are quotients of tensor powers. Duality: reduce to det V via det(V^∨) ⊗ ∧^{d−1}V ≅ V^∨; for dim 1, D_B(V) = E(b ⊗ v_0) with b ∈ B^× and b^{-1} ⊗ v_0^∨ ∈ D_B(V^∨) (B-C Theorem 5.2.1(2)(3)).

**Checks.** D_B(F) = E; D_B(V ⊕ W) = D_B(V) ⊕ D_B(W).

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/admissibility-dimension-bound`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-admissibility-dimension-bound).

**Sources.** [O. Brinon and B. Conrad — CMI Summer School notes on p-adic Hodge theory](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/notes.pdf), Theorem 5.2.1(2)–(3), p. 68. Statement (1); (3) is the tensor/dual statement.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-period-rings-are-regular"></a>

### B_HT, B_dR, B_cris and B_st are (Q_p, G_K)-regular

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/period-rings-are-regular` (theorem).

For K/Q_p finite: (1) B_HT is (Q_p, G_K)-regular with B_HT^{G_K} = K; (2) B_dR is (Q_p, G_K)-regular with B_dR^{G_K} = K; (3) B_cris and B_st are (Q_p, G_K)-regular with B_cris^{G_K} = B_st^{G_K} = K_0. More precisely, if b ∈ B_dR is nonzero and Q_p b is G_K-stable then b ∈ K̄·t^i for some i ∈ Z, and b ∈ B_st forces b ∈ K̂_0^{ur}·t^i ⊆ B_cris^×.

**Hypotheses and scope.** log_K(p) = 0 for the embedding B_st ⊆ B_dR (the statement is independent of the choice).

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1) Invariants of B_HT and C(t) by Tate–Sen (R06.1/hodge-tate-period-ring); a stable line Q_p b with b = Σ c_jt^j has character ψ with each c_j ∈ C(ψ^{-1}χ^j)^{G_K}, so at most one j occurs since χ has infinite image on inertia; b = ct^j is a unit (B-C Example 5.1.2).
2. (2) B_dR is a field with B_dR^{G_K} = K (R06.1/de-rham-invariants).
3. (3) (F-O Proposition 6.28) Domains and invariants by R06.1/period-ring-invariants. Stable line Q_p b ⊆ B_dR: after multiplying by t^{-i}, b ∈ B_dR^+ ∖ Fil^1; its residue b̄ ∈ C spans a stable line, so by Tate–Sen the character η has η(I_K) finite and b̄ is algebraic over K̂_0^{ur}; its Hensel lift β ∈ K̄ ⊆ B_dR^+ has the same character, and b − β, if nonzero, would give an invariant in C(χ^rη) with r ≥ 1, impossible; so b = β ∈ K̄. Finally K̄ ∩ B_st = K̂_0^{ur} ∩ K̄ ⊆ B_cris^×: a finite extension L of K̂_0^{ur} inside B_st satisfies L ⊗ … ⊆ B_st^{G_L} = L_0 = K̂_0^{ur} by R06.1/period-ring-invariants applied to L.

**Checks.** t ∈ B_cris^× and every G_K-stable line in B_cris is K̂_0^{ur}t^i-type. B_dR^+ and B_cris^+ are not regular (t is not a unit there).

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/regular-period-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-regular-period-ring), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/period-ring-invariants`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-period-ring-invariants), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/tate-sen-theorem`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-tate-sen-theorem), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/hodge-tate-period-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-hodge-tate-period-ring), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/complete-algebraically-closed-bdr`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-complete-algebraically-closed-bdr), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/bdr-natural-topology`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-bdr-natural-topology), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/galois-action-on-cp`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-galois-action-on-cp), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/k-tensor-bst-injective`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-k-tensor-bst-injective).

**Proof ingredients.** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/algebraic-closure-in-bdr-plus`; their statements and locators appear in the proof-ingredient index.

**Sources.** [J.-M. Fontaine and Y. Ouyang — Theory of p-adic Galois representations](https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/~jean-marc.fontaine/prepub/theory_padic.pdf), Proposition 6.28 with proof, p. 131. Regularity of B_cris and B_st. [O. Brinon and B. Conrad — CMI Summer School notes on p-adic Hodge theory](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/notes.pdf), Example 5.1.2, p. 66. Regularity of B_HT. [O. Brinon and B. Conrad — CMI Summer School notes on p-adic Hodge theory](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/notes.pdf), Proposition 9.1.6, p. 131. B-C's statement for B_cris (its proof relies on Theorem 9.1.5).

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-filtered-vector-spaces"></a>

### The category Fil_F of finite-dimensional filtered vector spaces

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/filtered-vector-spaces` (definition).

For a field F, an object of Fil_F is a finite-dimensional F-vector space D with a decreasing Z-indexed filtration by subspaces Fil^iD that is exhaustive (Fil^iD = D for i ≪ 0) and separated (Fil^iD = 0 for i ≫ 0); morphisms are linear maps T with T(Fil^iD') ⊆ Fil^iD. Kernels carry the subspace filtration and cokernels the quotient filtration; T is strict if the quotient and subspace filtrations on T(D') agree (coim T ≅ im T). A short exact sequence is one that is exact with D' ⊆ D carrying the subspace filtration and D'' the quotient filtration, equivalently 0 → Fil^iD' → Fil^iD → Fil^iD'' → 0 exact for all i. Tensor product: Fil^n(D ⊗ D') = Σ_{p+q=n} Fil^pD ⊗ Fil^qD'; dual: Fil^i(D^∨) = (Fil^{1−i}D)^⊥; unit F[0] (Fil^0 = F, Fil^1 = 0); shift D[n] with Fil^i(D[n]) = Fil^{i+n}D; gr^i D = Fil^iD/Fil^{i+1}D; Hom-filtration Fil^i Hom(D', D) = {T : T(Fil^jD') ⊆ Fil^{i+j}D}. Fil_F is additive but not abelian.

**Hypotheses and scope.** F any field (F = K for D_dR, F = K' for descent).

**Definitions on existing carriers.**

- `filtrationShift`: For F:Z→Submodule K V define filtrationShift(F,n)(i)=F(i+n).
- `dualFiltration`: Define dualFiltration(F)(i)=(F(1−i)).dualAnnihilator on the algebraic dual.
- `singleJumpFiltration`: Define singleJumpFiltration(w)(i)=V for i≤w and 0 for i>w.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Definitions; exhaustiveness/separatedness of ⊗ and dual are checked with bases adapted to the filtrations; gr is exact on short exact sequences and gr(D ⊗ D') ≅ gr D ⊗ gr D' (B-C §6.2).

**API.**

- `FilteredSpace` (structure): A finite-dimensional F-space D with an antitone family fil: Z → Submodule F D, exhaustive and separated.
- `FilteredSpace.Hom` (structure): Filtration-preserving linear maps.
- `FilteredSpace.IsStrict` (other): T is strict: T(Fil^iD') = Fil^iD ∩ T(D') for all i.
- `FilteredSpace.tensor` (constructor): Fil^n(D ⊗ D') = Σ_{p+q=n} Fil^p ⊗ Fil^q.
- `FilteredSpace.dual` (constructor): Fil^i D^∨ = (Fil^{1−i}D)^⊥.
- `FilteredSpace.shift` (constructor): D[n] with Fil^i(D[n]) = Fil^{i+n}D.
- `FilteredSpace.gr` (projection): gr^i D = Fil^i/Fil^{i+1}; Σ_i dim gr^i D = dim D.
- `FilteredSpace.unit` (constructor): F[0].
- `FilteredSpace.ShortExact` (structure): Short exact sequences (strict at both ends).
- `FilteredSpace.isIso_iff_gr` (characterisation): A morphism is an isomorphism iff it is bijective and strict iff gr of it is an isomorphism.
- `FilteredSpace.isModuleFiltration` (compatibility): fil is an IsModuleFiltration over the trivially filtered ring F in Mathlib's sense.
- `Filtration.shift_antitone` (relation): If F is antitone, so is filtrationShift(F,n).
- `Filtration.shift_add` (relation): Shifting by n then m equals shifting by n+m.
- `Filtration.dual_antitone` (relation): If F is antitone, then dualFiltration(F) is antitone.
- `Filtration.dual_membership` (relation): f belongs to the i-th dual piece iff f(v)=0 for every v in F(1−i).
- `Filtration.dual_dual` (relation): The inverse image under evaluation V→V** of the i-th double-dual piece is F(i).
- `Filtration.dual_shift` (relation): Dualizing shift n gives the dual filtration shifted by −n.
- `Filtration.single_jump_antitone` (relation): singleJumpFiltration(w) is antitone.
- `Filtration.single_jump_shift` (relation): Shifting jump w by n gives jump w−n.
- `Filtration.single_jump_dual` (relation): Dualizing jump w gives jump −w.

**Unit tests.**

- `filteredSpace_unit_dual` (degenerate): F[0]^∨ ≅ F[0] (the 1 − i in the dual filtration).
- `filteredSpace_bijective_not_iso` (non-example): id: (F^2, jump at 0) → (F^2, jump at 4) is a bijective morphism but not an isomorphism.
- `filteredSpace_gr_dim` (computation): For D = F^2 with Fil^0 = D, Fil^1 = F·e_1, Fil^2 = 0: dim gr^0 = dim gr^1 = 1.
- `filteredSpace_mathlib_filtration` (compatibility): fil is antitone and gives Mathlib's IsModuleFiltration for the ring filtration of F concentrated in degrees ≤ 0.
- `Filtration.shift_zero` (computation): filtrationShift(F,0)=F.
- `Filtration.shift_tate` (computation): Shift 1 sends the jump-zero filtration to the jump-minus-one filtration.
- `Filtration.shift_inverse` (computation): Shifting by n and then −n recovers F.
- `Filtration.dual_unit_zero` (computation): The degree-zero dual piece of the jump-zero filtration is the whole dual.
- `Filtration.dual_unit_one` (computation): The degree-one dual piece of the jump-zero filtration is zero.
- `Filtration.dual_weight` (computation): The dual of a jump-minus-one filtration has jump one.
- `Filtration.single_jump_at` (computation): The piece at the jump w is all of V.
- `Filtration.single_jump_after` (computation): The piece at w+1 is zero.
- `Filtration.single_jump_negative` (computation): For jump −2, the piece at −1 is zero.

**Uses.** Brinon–Conrad §6.3: D_dR takes values in Fil_K. PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/filtered-phi-n-modules: the filtration on D_K. MordellLawrenceVenkatesh LV.1/filtration-weight: weight of a filtered space t_H(D)/dim D.

**Checks.** The identity map from D with the trivial filtration (jump at 0) to D with jump at 4 is a bijective morphism that is not an isomorphism (B-C Example 6.2.1).

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:IsModuleFiltration`, `mathlib:Submodule`.

**Sources.** [O. Brinon and B. Conrad — CMI Summer School notes on p-adic Hodge theory](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/notes.pdf), §6.2, p. 74. The category. [O. Brinon and B. Conrad — CMI Summer School notes on p-adic Hodge theory](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/notes.pdf), Definition 6.2.5, p. 75. Strictness.

### Fontaine's period functors D_HT, D_dR, D_cris, D_st and their comparison maps

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/period-functors` (definition).

For a p-adic representation V of G_K (finite-dimensional Q_p-vector space with continuous linear G_K-action) put D_B(V) = (B ⊗_{Q_p} V)^{G_K} for B ∈ {B_HT, B_dR, B_cris, B_st}. Structures: D_HT(V) is a finite-dimensional graded K-vector space (grading from B_HT); D_dR(V) is a finite-dimensional K-vector space with the exhaustive separated filtration Fil^iD_dR(V) = (t^iB_dR^+ ⊗ V)^{G_K}; D_cris(V) is a finite-dimensional K_0-vector space with the σ-semilinear Frobenius φ ⊗ 1 and the filtration on D_cris(V)_K = K ⊗_{K_0} D_cris(V) ⊆ D_dR(V) induced from D_dR(V); D_st(V) is a finite-dimensional K_0-vector space with φ, monodromy N ⊗ 1 and the induced filtration on D_st(V)_K ⊆ D_dR(V) (via Iwasawa's log p = 0). The comparison maps α_V: B ⊗_{B^{G_K}} D_B(V) → B ⊗_{Q_p} V are B-linear, G_K-equivariant and compatible with all structures. Contravariant versions D*_B(V) = Hom_{Q_p[G_K]}(V, B) = D_B(V^∨); inverse functors V_cris(D) = Fil^0(B_cris ⊗_{K_0} D)^{φ=1} and V_st(D) = Fil^0(B_st ⊗_{K_0} D)^{φ=1, N=0}. Hodge–Tate weight convention (pinned): h ∈ Z is a Hodge–Tate weight of V with multiplicity dim_K gr^{−h}D_dR(V) = dim_K (C(−h) ⊗ V)^{G_K}; thus Q_p(1) has Hodge–Tate weight +1 (HT(χ) = +1), which is the negative of Brinon–Conrad's convention (their weights are the degrees of D_HT, and C(q) has B-C weight −q).

**Hypotheses and scope.** V a continuous Q_p-representation of G_K on a finite-dimensional space; K ⊗_{K_0} D_st(V) ⊆ D_dR(V) by R06.1/k-tensor-bst-injective.

**Construction or proof.**

1. D_B(V) are E-vector spaces (E = B^{G_K}) of dimension ≤ dim V by R06.2/admissibility-dimension-bound and R06.2/period-rings-are-regular.
2. The filtration on D_dR(V) is exhaustive and separated because D_dR(V) is finite-dimensional and Fil^• B_dR is exhaustive and separated.
3. φ on D_cris(V) and D_st(V) is bijective for crystalline/semistable V by R06.2/dcris-dst-filtered-phi-n-modules; for arbitrary V it is an injective σ-semilinear map of a finite-dimensional space.
4. K ⊗_{K_0} D_st(V) = ((K ⊗ B_st) ⊗ V)^{G_K} ⊆ D_dR(V) by exactness of K ⊗_{K_0} − and injectivity of K ⊗ B_st → B_dR.

**API.**

- `DHT` (constructor): D_HT(V) = (B_HT ⊗ V)^{G_K} as a graded K-vector space.
- `DdR` (constructor): D_dR(V) = (B_dR ⊗ V)^{G_K} with its filtration Fil^iD_dR(V) = (t^iB_dR^+ ⊗ V)^{G_K}.
- `Dcris` (constructor): D_cris(V) = (B_cris ⊗ V)^{G_K} with φ and the filtration on K ⊗_{K_0} D_cris(V).
- `Dst` (constructor): D_st(V) = (B_st ⊗ V)^{G_K} with φ, N and filtration.
- `comparisonMap` (data): α_V: B ⊗_{B^{G_K}} D_B(V) → B ⊗ V.
- `Dcris_eq_Dst_ker_monodromy` (characterisation): D_cris(V) = D_st(V)^{N=0}.
- `Dst_to_DdR` (coercion): K ⊗_{K_0} D_st(V) → D_dR(V) is injective and strict for the filtrations.
- `DB_map` (functoriality): D_B is a functor: D_B(f∘g) = D_B(f)∘D_B(g), D_B(id) = id.
- `DdR_twist` (relation): D_dR(V(n)) = t^{−n}D_dR(V) ⊗ e_n with Fil^i D_dR(V(n)) = Fil^{i+n}D_dR(V) (shift).
- `Vcris` (constructor): V_cris(D) = Fil^0(B_cris ⊗_{K_0} D)^{φ=1} for D ∈ MF^φ_K.
- `Vst` (constructor): V_st(D) = Fil^0(B_st ⊗_{K_0} D)^{φ=1, N=0}.
- `DdR_contravariant` (equivalence): D*_dR(V) := Hom_{Q_p[G_K]}(V, B_dR) ≅ D_dR(V^∨).
- `hodgeTateMultiplicity` (data): m_h(V) = dim_K gr^{−h}D_dR(V) (convention HT(χ) = +1).
- `hodgeTateMultiplicity_eq_BC` (compatibility): m_h(V) equals Brinon–Conrad's multiplicity of the weight −h, i.e. dim_K (C(−h) ⊗ V)^{G_K} = dim D_HT(V)_{−h}.

**Unit tests.**

- `DdR_trivial` (degenerate): D_dR(Q_p) = K with Fil^0 = K and Fil^1 = 0.
- `DdR_tate_twist` (computation): D_dR(Q_p(1)) = K·t^{−1} ⊗ e_1 with gr^{−1} ≠ 0; hodgeTateMultiplicity 1 (Q_p(1)) = 1.
- `Dcris_trivial_compat_isocrystal` (compatibility): D_cris(Q_p) with its Frobenius is the unit isocrystal: Mathlib's StandardOneDimIsocrystal of slope 0 over K_0 = K(p, k).
- `DHT_nonHT_character` (non-example): For p odd, K = Q_p and η = ⟨χ⟩^s with s ∈ Z_p ∖ Z, D_HT(Q_p(η)) = 0.
- `Dcris_ne_DdR_ramified` (non-example): For K/K_0 ramified and V = Q_p, D_cris(V) = K_0 while D_dR(V) = K (different base fields).

**Uses.** Brinon–Conrad §§2.4, 6, 8, 9: the functors and their comparison isomorphisms. MordellLawrenceVenkatesh LV.1, LV.4, LV.6, LV.7: D_dR with its filtration and D_cris ∈ MF^φ_K of local Galois representations. CohomologyComparisons CP.2, CP.5: D_cris(H^i_ét) = H^i_cris[1/p] and D_dR(V) ⊗ B_dR^+ lattices. FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems R28.2: Hodge–Tate decomposition of Tate modules. PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3 (part D): D_pst and the Weil–Deligne parameter. PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4 (part D): the Hodge–Tate weight convention HT(χ_p) = +1. FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4: comparison of Wach modules with D_cris. PadicHodgeRegulators:L0: realisations imported with no second carrier.

**Checks.** D_dR(Q_p(n)) = Kt^{−n} with unique jump at −n; Q_p(n) has Hodge–Tate weight n (R06.2/ddr-of-tate-twists). D_cris(Q_p) = K_0 with φ = σ and trivial filtration.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/de-rham-period-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-de-rham-period-ring), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/hodge-tate-period-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-hodge-tate-period-ring), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/crystalline-period-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-crystalline-period-ring), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/semistable-period-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-semistable-period-ring), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/bst-embedding-into-bdr`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-bst-embedding-into-bdr), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/k-tensor-bst-injective`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-k-tensor-bst-injective), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/admissibility-dimension-bound`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-admissibility-dimension-bound), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/period-rings-are-regular`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-period-rings-are-regular), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/filtered-vector-spaces`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-filtered-vector-spaces), `mathlib:Representation.invariants`, `mathlib:Representation.tprod`, `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1`.

**Sources.** [O. Brinon and B. Conrad — CMI Summer School notes on p-adic Hodge theory](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/notes.pdf), §6.1, definition of D_dR, p. 73. D_dR; D_HT is Definition 2.4.12, D_cris §8 intro, D_st §9.2. [O. Brinon and B. Conrad — CMI Summer School notes on p-adic Hodge theory](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/notes.pdf), §6.3, Example 6.3.1 and the discussion of Hodge–Tate weights, p. 76. B-C's convention, of which ours is the negative (with the indicated sign translation). [Laurent Berger — An introduction to the theory of p-adic representations](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0210184v1), §II.2.3, p. 12. Berger's convention, which is ours (V_p E has weights 0 and 1).
