### Wach modules recover the filtered phi-module D_cris(V)

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P7/plan/wach-dcris-comparison` (theorem).

Equip N(V) with the filtration Fil^i N(V) = {x in N(V) : phi(x) in q^i N(V)} (for V with weights <= 0; in general N(V) = pi^{-b} N(V(-b)) and the filtration is transported). Then the map lambda : D_cris(V) -> N(V)/pi N(V), obtained from the inclusion D_cris(V) in B^+_{rig,F} tensor_{B^+_F} N(V) (the R07.4 integral Wach interface: D_cris(V) = (B^+_{rig,F} tensor N(V))^{Gamma_F}), is an isomorphism of filtered phi-modules over F, where N(V)/pi N(V) carries the image filtration and D_cris(V) its Hodge filtration (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/filtered-phi-n-modules, Fil^i D_cris(V) = Fil^i D_dR(V) cap D_cris(V)).

**Hypotheses and scope.** K = F = W(k)[1/p] is absolutely unramified (Wach modules are only claimed over unramified bases). T is a G_F-stable Z_p-lattice in a crystalline representation V of dimension d, with Hodge–Tate weights in [a, b] for the convention HT(chi) = +1 (Berger writes r_j = -(weights) and calls V positive when all weights are <= 0). N(T) and N(V) = B^+_F tensor N(T) are the Wach modules imported from R07.4’s integral Wach interface (a Wach module over B^+_F must include the condition that B_F tensor N is an etale (phi, Gamma)-module, Berger errata 2026 for Definition III.4.1); q = phi(pi)/pi. V is a p-adic representation of G_K of dimension d; D_st, D_cris, D_dR are the period functors of PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/period-functors with Fontaine's normalisations (u = log[p~], N = -d/du, N phi = p phi N); HT(chi) = +1, so 'positive' in Berger's sense means Hodge–Tate weights <= 0.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Bijectivity: by dimension it suffices that pi B^+_{rig,F} tensor N(V) meets D_cris(V) in 0. Show by induction on j >= 1 that this intersection lies in pi^j B^+_{rig,F} tensor N(V): for x = pi^j y there, gamma(x) - chi(gamma)^j x lies in pi^{j+1} B^+_{rig,F} tensor N(V) (gamma(pi) = chi(gamma) pi mod pi^2 and Gamma_F acts trivially on N(V)/pi N(V)); if x is Gamma_F-fixed and chi(gamma)^j != 1 this forces x into pi^{j+1}(...) (Berger 2004 Theoreme III.4.4 proof, using the exponent +j in the leading-term character). An element divisible by every power of pi is 0. lambda is phi-equivariant by construction.
2. Filtrations: for V with weights <= 0, D_cris(V) = (B~^+_{rig} tensor V)^{G_F} and Fil^i D_cris(V) = (Fil^i B~^+_{rig} tensor V)^{G_F}; Fil^i B~^+_{rig} = Fil^i B^+_max cap B~^+_{rig} = (pi/pi_1)^i B^+_max cap B~^+_{rig}, and x lies in it iff phi(x) in q^i B~^+_{rig} (q = phi(pi/pi_1)) (R06.1/crystalline-period-ring, P7/extended-robba-ring-with-galois-action).
3. Compare inside B~^+_{rig}[1/pi] tensor V = B~^+_{rig}[1/pi] tensor N(V) (the R07.4 integral Wach interface, Berger 2004 Theoreme III.3.1): q^i(B~^+_{rig} tensor V) cap (B^+_{rig,F} tensor N(V)) = q^i B^+_{rig,F} tensor N(V); this gives lambda(Fil^i D_cris(V)) contained in the image of Fil^i N(V).
4. Reverse inclusion (completing Berger 2004, whose proof omits this step; Berger errata 2026, section 2): if y in D_cris(V) has image in Fil^i N(V)/pi N(V), a priori only y in Fil^i N(V) + pi N(V); for gamma non-torsion and j >= 1, gamma - chi(gamma)^j multiplies y by a nonzero scalar and maps Fil^i N(V) + pi^j N(V) into Fil^i N(V) + pi^{j+1} N(V); applying this for j = 1, ..., i - 1 gives y in Fil^i N(V), hence y in Fil^i D_cris(V) (Corollaire III.4.5 for general V by twisting).

**Checks.** Supersingular example (Berger introduction V.1.1): N(T) = A^+_F e + A^+_F f with phi(e) = q f, phi(f) = e; Fil^1 N(V) = {a e + b f : phi(b) in q B^+_F} = {b in pi B^+_F}, so Fil^1 (N/pi N) = F e-bar, and phi(e-bar) = p f-bar (q is congruent to p mod pi), phi(f-bar) = e-bar: the filtered phi-module with Fil^0 = D, Fil^1 = F e, Fil^2 = 0; t_N = v_p(det) = v_p(-p) = 1 = t_H (checked with PARI/GP).

**Prerequisites.** `FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4`, [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/filtered-phi-n-modules`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-filtered-phi-n-modules), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/period-functors`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-period-functors), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/crystalline-period-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-crystalline-period-ring), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/plan/extended-robba-ring-with-galois-action`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-plan-extended-robba-ring-with-galois-action), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/plan/berger-dcris-dst-dictionary`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-plan-berger-dcris-dst-dictionary), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/plan/overconvergent-cyclotomic-rings`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-annulus-foundations-plan-overconvergent-cyclotomic-rings), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/plan/cyclotomic-frobenius`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-annulus-foundations-plan-cyclotomic-frobenius).

**Sources.** [L. Berger — Limites de représentations cristallines](https://perso.ens-lyon.fr/laurent.berger/articles/article06.pdf), Théorème III.4.4, p. 22. The filtration on the Wach module. [L. Berger — Limites de représentations cristallines](https://perso.ens-lyon.fr/laurent.berger/articles/article06.pdf), Théorème III.4.4, p. 22. The comparison map lambda, an isomorphism of filtered phi-modules. [Laurent Berger — An introduction to the theory of p-adic representations](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0210184v1), V.1.1, p. 33. The phi-module statement. [L. Berger — Limites de représentations cristallines](https://perso.ens-lyon.fr/laurent.berger/articles/article06.pdf), Introduction, Théorème 3, p. 4. Theorem 3 of the introduction. [L. Berger — Errata for my articles](https://perso.ens-lyon.fr/laurent.berger/articles/errata.pdf), Section 2, Theorem III.4.4 (errata dated May 5, 2026). The missing step, supplied in proof step 4.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p7-plan-integral-dcris-lattice"></a>

### The integral lattice D_cris(T) of a crystalline lattice

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P7/plan/integral-dcris-lattice` (construction).

For a G_F-stable lattice T of a crystalline V, D_cris(T) is the image of N(T) in D_cris(V) under the isomorphism D_cris(V) = N(V)/pi N(V) of P7/wach-dcris-comparison. It is an O_F-lattice in D_cris(V), stable under phi when the weights are <= 0, with the induced filtration Fil^i_T; T |-> D_cris(T) is inclusion-preserving and injective on the lattices of a fixed V; and, if -r_1, ..., -r_d are the Hodge–Tate weights, the determinant of the comparison isomorphism B_max tensor V = B_max tensor D_cris(V) computed in bases of T and D_cris(T) lies in t^{r_1 + ... + r_d} W(k)^x.

**Hypotheses and scope.** K = F = W(k)[1/p] is absolutely unramified (Wach modules are only claimed over unramified bases). T is a G_F-stable Z_p-lattice in a crystalline representation V of dimension d, with Hodge–Tate weights in [a, b] for the convention HT(chi) = +1 (Berger writes r_j = -(weights) and calls V positive when all weights are <= 0). N(T) and N(V) = B^+_F tensor N(T) are the Wach modules imported from R07.4’s integral Wach interface (a Wach module over B^+_F must include the condition that B_F tensor N is an etale (phi, Gamma)-module, Berger errata 2026 for Definition III.4.1); q = phi(pi)/pi. V is a p-adic representation of G_K of dimension d; D_st, D_cris, D_dR are the period functors of PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/period-functors with Fontaine's normalisations (u = log[p~], N = -d/du, N phi = p phi N); HT(chi) = +1, so 'positive' in Berger's sense means Hodge–Tate weights <= 0.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Lattice: N(T) is free of rank d over A^+_F (the R07.4 integral Wach interface), so N(T)/pi N(T) is a free O_F-module of rank d inside N(V)/pi N(V).
2. Determinant: the inclusion A^+ tensor N(T) in A^+ tensor T has determinant generating (pi^{r_1+...+r_d}) (the R07.4 integral Wach interface, Berger 2004 Theoreme III.3.1); D_cris(T) is the set of x in (B^+_{rig,F} tensor N(T))^{Gamma_F} with x(0) in N(T)/pi N(T), and the inclusion B^+_{rig,F} tensor D_cris(T) in B^+_{rig,F} tensor N(T) has determinant (t/pi)^{sum r_i} f_0 with f_0 a unit of A^+_F; combine, and use crystallinity to land in W(k)^x (Berger 2004 Proposition V.1.2).
3. Injectivity on lattices: Berger 2004 Remarque V.1.3 (T recovered from N(T) by T = (A tensor N(T))^{phi=1}).

**API.**

- `Wach.dcrisLattice` (constructor): D_cris(T) = image of N(T) in N(V)/pi N(V) = D_cris(V).
- `Wach.dcrisLattice_isLattice` (characterisation): D_cris(T) is a free O_F-submodule of rank d spanning D_cris(V).
- `Wach.dcrisLattice_phi` (relation): phi(D_cris(T)) is contained in D_cris(T) when all Hodge–Tate weights are <= 0.
- `Wach.dcrisLattice_mono` (functoriality): T_1 contained in T_2 implies D_cris(T_1) contained in D_cris(T_2).
- `Wach.dcrisLattice_injective` (characterisation): D_cris(T_1) = D_cris(T_2) iff T_1 = T_2.
- `Wach.det_comparison` (relation): det of B_max tensor V = B_max tensor D_cris(V) in bases of T and D_cris(T) lies in t^{sum r_i} W(k)^x.
- `Wach.filtrationT` (data): Fil^i_T D_cris(T): images of Fil^i N(T) = Fil^i N(V) cap N(T).

**Unit tests.**

- `wachLattice.test_twist` (computation): For T = Z_p(r), r <= 0: D_cris(T) = O_F t^{-r} e_r.
- `wachLattice.test_det` (computation): For T = Z_p(r) the comparison determinant is t^{-r} times a unit of W(k).
- `wachLattice.test_trivial` (degenerate): For T = Z_p: D_cris(T) = O_F.
- `wachLattice.test_not_dual` (non-example): D_cris(T) depends on T, not only on V: for T and pT (same V) D_cris(pT) = p D_cris(T) != D_cris(T).

**Uses.** PadicHodgeTheory:P7/plan/wach-fontaine-laffaille-comparison: D_cris(T) is strongly divisible in the Fontaine–Laffaille range. FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.3: comparison with the Fontaine–Laffaille lattice. PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/fontaine-laffaille-rational-consequences: rational consequences of the integral classification. Berger 2004, Section V.1: Tamagawa number computations (Benois–Berger).

**Checks.** For T = Z_p(r) (r <= 0): D_cris(T) = O_F t^{-r} e_r and the comparison determinant is t^{-r} up to a unit.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/plan/wach-dcris-comparison`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-plan-wach-dcris-comparison), `FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4`, [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/period-functors`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-period-functors), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/crystalline-period-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-crystalline-period-ring), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/plan/cyclotomic-log-element-t`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-annulus-foundations-plan-cyclotomic-log-element-t).

**Sources.** [L. Berger — Limites de représentations cristallines](https://perso.ens-lyon.fr/laurent.berger/articles/article06.pdf), Définition V.1.1, p. 28. Definition. [L. Berger — Limites de représentations cristallines](https://perso.ens-lyon.fr/laurent.berger/articles/article06.pdf), Proposition V.1.2, p. 28. Lattice property. [L. Berger — Limites de représentations cristallines](https://perso.ens-lyon.fr/laurent.berger/articles/article06.pdf), Remarque V.1.3, p. 29. Injectivity on lattices.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p7-plan-wach-fontaine-laffaille-comparison"></a>

### Wach lattices versus Fontaine–Laffaille strongly divisible lattices

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P7/plan/wach-fontaine-laffaille-comparison` (comparison).

(a) If the Hodge–Tate weights of V lie in an interval [a - (p-1), a] (filtration length <= p - 1), then M = D_cris(T) is a strongly divisible lattice of D_cris(V): sum_i p^{-i} phi(Fil^i M) = M with Fil^i M = Fil^i D_cris(V) cap M; and Fil^i_T = Fil^i_V on M. (b) Conversely, if M is a strongly divisible lattice of a (weakly admissible) filtered phi-module D with weights in [a - (p-1), a] such that D has no slope -a part or no slope -a + (p-1) part, there are a crystalline V and a lattice T with D_cris(V) = D and D_cris(T) = M; on an interval of length <= p - 2 no slope condition is needed. (c) Hence for weights in an interval of length <= p - 2, T |-> D_cris(T) is an inclusion-preserving bijection between G_F-stable lattices of V and strongly divisible lattices of D_cris(V), and agrees with the Fontaine–Laffaille correspondence of FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.3 after translating filtration indices to HT(chi) = +1. For length >= p the statement (a) fails in general.

**Hypotheses and scope.** K = F = W(k)[1/p] is absolutely unramified (Wach modules are only claimed over unramified bases). T is a G_F-stable Z_p-lattice in a crystalline representation V of dimension d, with Hodge–Tate weights in [a, b] for the convention HT(chi) = +1 (Berger writes r_j = -(weights) and calls V positive when all weights are <= 0). N(T) and N(V) = B^+_F tensor N(T) are the Wach modules imported from R07.4’s integral Wach interface (a Wach module over B^+_F must include the condition that B_F tensor N is an etale (phi, Gamma)-module, Berger errata 2026 for Definition III.4.1); q = phi(pi)/pi. V is a p-adic representation of G_K of dimension d; D_st, D_cris, D_dR are the period functors of PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/period-functors with Fontaine's normalisations (u = log[p~], N = -d/du, N phi = p phi N); HT(chi) = +1, so 'positive' in Berger's sense means Hodge–Tate weights <= 0. Strongly divisible (Fontaine–Laffaille 1982 Section 7.7): sum p^{-i} phi(Fil^i M) = M; for weakly admissible D it suffices that the sum is contained in M (Fontaine–Laffaille Section 7.8).

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a) Twist to a = 0. Since q is congruent to p modulo pi, phi(Fil^i_T M) is in p^i M, so sum p^{-i} phi(Fil^i_T M) is contained in M; it remains to see Fil^i_V M = Fil^i_T M for 1 <= i <= p - 1. For gamma with chi(gamma)^i != 1 mod p (1 <= i <= p-2) let T_i(gamma) = product_{j=1}^{i-1} (1 - chi(gamma)^{-j} gamma); for x = x_0 + pi y_1 lifting an element of Fil^i_V, T_i(gamma) x = T_i(gamma) x_0 + pi^i y_i, so T_i(gamma) x_0 lies in Fil^i N(V) cap N(T) = Fil^i N(T), and T_i(gamma) acts on M by a p-adic unit when i <= p - 1 (Berger 2004 Proposition V.2.1, after Wach 1997 Theorem 3).
2. (b) In a basis adapted to the filtration the matrix of phi on M is A_0 P_0 with P_0 = Diag(p^{r_i}); lift to P = A_0 Diag(q^{r_i} mu^{r_i}) with mu = p/(q - pi^{p-1}) a unit of A^+_F, and solve G_gamma gamma(P) = P phi(G_gamma) with G_gamma = Id + pi^{p-1} H by a contraction argument, which converges when D has no slope -a or no slope -a + (p-1) part; then T = (A_F tensor N)^{phi=1} (the P7 realization and R07.4 integral Wach interfaces; Berger 2004 Proposition V.2.3).
3. (c) Combine (a), (b), injectivity (P7/integral-dcris-lattice) and the Fontaine–Laffaille lattice correspondence (R07.3; Fontaine–Laffaille 1982 Proposition 7.17).

**Checks.** The supersingular example of P7/wach-dcris-comparison (weights 0 and -1, p >= 3): M = O_F e + O_F f with Fil^1 M = O_F e, phi(e) = p f, phi(f) = e, and p^{-1} phi(Fil^1 M) + phi(Fil^0 M) = O_F f + O_F e = M is strongly divisible.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/plan/integral-dcris-lattice`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-plan-integral-dcris-lattice), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/plan/wach-dcris-comparison`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-plan-wach-dcris-comparison), `FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4`, [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/etale-realization-and-overconvergence`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-etale-realization-and-overconvergence), `FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.3`, [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/weak-admissibility`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-weak-admissibility), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/filtered-phi-n-modules`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-filtered-phi-n-modules).

**Sources.** [L. Berger — Limites de représentations cristallines](https://perso.ens-lyon.fr/laurent.berger/articles/article06.pdf), Proposition V.2.1, p. 30. (a). [L. Berger — Limites de représentations cristallines](https://perso.ens-lyon.fr/laurent.berger/articles/article06.pdf), Proposition V.2.3, p. 31. (b) with the endpoint slope restriction. [L. Berger — Limites de représentations cristallines](https://perso.ens-lyon.fr/laurent.berger/articles/article06.pdf), Proposition V.2.1, proof, p. 30. Failure beyond length p - 1. [L. Berger — Limites de représentations cristallines](https://perso.ens-lyon.fr/laurent.berger/articles/article06.pdf), Remarque V.2.2, p. 30. Beyond the range the image is unknown.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p7-coefficient-b-pairs"></a>

### Coefficient B-pairs and strict morphisms

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P7/coefficient-b-pairs` (definition).

For K,E/Q_p finite let B_e=B_cris^{φ=1}. An E-B-pair W consists of a finite free (B_e⊗E)-module W_e with continuous semilinear G_K-action and a G_K-stable finite free (B_dR^+⊗E)-lattice W_dR^+ in W_dR=B_dR⊗_{B_e}W_e. Both have the same E-rank. A morphism has compatible equivariant linear maps on both components agreeing after B_dR extension. It is strict when the cokernel of its lattice map is torsion free over B_dR^+⊗E. Exact sequences use strict maps; the category of B-pairs is not abelian. Tensor products and duals are componentwise. A modification changes the lattice while retaining W_e. W(V)=(B_e⊗V,B_dR^+⊗V), and W(D)=((B_st⊗D)^{φ=1,N=0},Fil^0(B_dR⊗D_K)).

**Hypotheses and scope.** Coefficient tensor products retain the complete E-algebra, rather than one scalar factor; all actions have the natural period topology.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Use the existing period rings and their comparison embeddings. Specify free modules, the common scalar extension and a full lattice. Define componentwise morphisms and restrict exactness to torsion-free lattice quotients. Extend Berger’s Q_p formulation by the E-action and use Nakamura’s coefficient definition.

**API.**

- `BPair.of_representation` (constructor): A continuous E-representation V gives W(V) of the same E-rank.
- `BPair.of_filtered_module` (constructor): A filtered (φ,N)-module gives W(D) with Fil^0 lattice.
- `BPair.hom_ext` (extensionality): Morphisms are equal if their e and lattice components agree.
- `BPair.strict` (characterisation): Strictness is the torsion-free lattice-cokernel condition.
- `BPair.tensor_dual` (structure): Tensor, unit and dual are the componentwise period operations.
- `BPair.modify` (constructor): A full G_K-stable replacement lattice gives a modification with unchanged e-component.

**Unit tests.**

- `BPair.unit` (computation): W(Q_p)=(B_e,B_dR^+), of rank one.
- `BPair.non_strict` (non-example): The map (B_e,tB_dR^+)→(B_e,B_dR^+) is injective but not strict.
- `BPair.zero` (degenerate): The two zero modules form the unique rank-zero pair.
- `BPair.filtered_unit` (compatibility): For the weakly admissible unit D, W(D)=W(Q_p).

**Uses.** Ding §2 and triangulations: Keeps the e-part fixed while modifying embedding-indexed lattices.. Colmez–Nizioł Remark 5.5: Attaches a genuine lattice to the fundamental period data..

**Checks.** The quotient B_dR/W_dR^+ is not the lattice component.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/fundamental-period-complex`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-fundamental-period-complex), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/fundamental-exact-sequence`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-fundamental-exact-sequence), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/semistable-period-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-semistable-period-ring), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/coefficient-field-base-change`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-coefficient-field-base-change).

**Sources.** [Laurent Berger — B-paires et (φ,Γ)-modules](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0704.1083v2), Definition 2.1.1, Examples 2.1.2, Definitions 2.1.6 and 2.1.8, pp.12–13. Defines the two components, strict exactness, modifications and the classical examples. [Kentaro Nakamura — Classification of two-dimensional split trianguline representations of p-adic fields](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0801.1230), §1.1, Definition 1.1, pp.3–4. Retains E-coefficients and the period-module lattice data.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p7-b-pair-robba-equivalence"></a>

### Berger’s B-pair–Robba equivalence

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P7/b-pair-robba-equivalence` (theorem).

The category of E-B-pairs is tensor equivalent to finite free (φ,Γ_K)-modules over the coefficient Robba ring. For W, its extended module consists of y in B̃_rig^†[1/t]⊗_{B_e}W_e whose images under every sufficiently large localization ι_n lie in W_dR^+. Descent gives D(W). Conversely W_e(D)=(B̃_rig^†[1/t]⊗D)^{φ=1} and W_dR^+(D)=B_dR^+⊗_{ι_n}D^{r_n} for n large; the latter is independent of n. These constructions are mutually inverse, preserve strict exact sequences and identify W(V) with D_rig^†(V). The pairs arising from representations correspond precisely to étale modules. A modification corresponds to an isomorphism after inverting t.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Use radii and localization maps on the shared Robba carriers; coefficient E-actions commute with φ,Γ_K.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Impose the lattice condition simultaneously at every large cyclotomic localization. Prove finite freeness over the extended Robba ring by elementary divisors and control of all localization ideals. Use Tate–Sen descent and annulus gluing to descend the extended module. Construct the reverse e-invariants and lattice, prove its stability for increasing n, and compare both scalar extensions to obtain inverse functors. Apply the shared slope-zero criterion for the representation subcategory.

**Checks.** Multiplying the lattice by t^m replaces D(W) by t^mD(W). The equivalence is for all B-pairs, but only slope-zero pairs come from Galois representations.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/coefficient-b-pairs`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-coefficient-b-pairs), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/plan/extended-robba-ring-with-galois-action`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-plan-extended-robba-ring-with-galois-action), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/plan/extended-localisation-maps`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-plan-extended-localisation-maps), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/cyclotomic-field-of-norms-interface`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-cyclotomic-field-of-norms-interface), `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2`.

**Sources.** [Laurent Berger — B-paires et (φ,Γ)-modules](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0704.1083v2), Lemmas 2.2.1–2.2.2, Propositions 2.2.4–2.2.6, Theorem 2.2.7 and Proposition 2.2.9, pp.13–17. Builds the two functors, proves descent, and identifies the étale subcategory.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p7-b-pair-cohomology-handoff"></a>

### Cohomology of B-pairs through Robba modules

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P7/b-pair-cohomology-handoff` (theorem).

Transport the shared Herr cohomology of D(W) to an E-B-pair W. The cohomology is finite dimensional, concentrated in degrees 0,1,2, and χ(W)=−[K:Q_p]rk_E(W). Cup product and trace induce perfect pairings H^i(W)×H^{2−i}(W^∨(1))→E. For W(V) these are the continuous G_K-cohomology groups and their Tate pairings. The complex, cup product and trace are the shared P7 Herr interface.

**Hypotheses and scope.** K,E finite over Q_p; W an E-B-pair; the source Q_p results are extended by the finite coefficient action.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Apply Berger’s equivalence and import Liu’s Herr cohomology, Euler characteristic and duality. Verify that W(V) maps to the étale module in Liu Theorem 0.1 and that tensor duality preserves the cyclotomic dualizing object.

**Checks.** For rank one and K=Q_p the Euler characteristic is −1, independent of its slope.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/b-pair-robba-equivalence`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-b-pair-robba-equivalence), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/herr-complex-interface`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-herr-complex-interface).

**Sources.** [Ruochuan Liu — Cohomology and duality for (φ,Γ)-modules over the Robba ring](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0711.4346v2), Theorems 0.1–0.2, p.3; §2.1, pp.8–9. Identifies Galois cohomology on the étale subcategory and proves Euler characteristic and perfect duality for all Robba modules.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p7-coefficient-bdr-representations"></a>

### Coefficient de Rham period representations

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P7/coefficient-bdr-representations` (definition).

A B_dR-representation of G_K is a finite-dimensional B_dR-vector space with continuous semilinear G_K-action. An E-coefficient representation is a finite free B_dR⊗E-module with commuting E-action. A stable positive lattice is a finite free B_dR^+⊗E-submodule spanning it after inversion of t. Put D_dR(W)=W^{G_K}; the representation is de Rham when the scalar-extension map B_dR⊗_K D_dR(W)→W is invertible. A stable lattice induces Fil^iD_dR(W)=D_dR(W)∩t^iW_dR^+. If E contains all K-embeddings, group the coefficient decomposition by σ:K→E as W_dR^+=⊕_σ W_dR,σ^+, over B_dR^+⊗_{K,σ}E; each factor retains its E-algebra structure and rank.

**Hypotheses and scope.** K,E finite over Q_p for Fontaine’s classification; the coefficient σ-components are not asserted to be fields.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Use finite free period modules and the actual topological semilinear action. Define the comparison map and lattice-intersection filtration. Decompose E⊗K by K-embeddings and transport this decomposition to the coefficient period module.

**API.**

- `BdRRep.comparison` (characterisation): De Rhamness is invertibility of the invariant scalar-extension map.
- `BdRRep.lattice_filtration` (constructor): Intersect invariant vectors with t^i times the chosen stable lattice.
- `BdRRep.coefficient_components` (projection): The σ-components are obtained from E⊗K idempotents.
- `BdRRep.tensor` (compatibility): Tensor modules, duals and lattices use the induced tensor and dual filtrations.

**Unit tests.**

- `BdRRep.unit` (computation): B_dR with its natural action and lattice B_dR^+ has invariants K and filtration jump 0.
- `BdRRep.twisted_lattice` (non-example): Replacing B_dR^+ by t^mB_dR^+ changes the filtration jump to −m without changing the B_dR-representation.
- `BdRRep.coefficient_rank` (compatibility): A rank-d E-coefficient lattice has rank d in each σ-component over its component algebra.
- `BdRRep.zero` (degenerate): The zero module has zero invariant space and zero lattice.

**Uses.** Ding Proposition 2.5: Modifies one σ-component while retaining the common B_dR-representation.. Fontaine Theorem 3.19: Classifies the ambient continuous semilinear representation before a lattice is chosen..

**Checks.** A stable lattice is extra data: the B_dR-representation alone does not determine its integer filtration jumps.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/coefficient-b-pairs`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-coefficient-b-pairs), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/period-functors-perfect-residue-base`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-period-functors-perfect-residue-base).

**Sources.** [Jean-Marc Fontaine — Almost C_p Galois representations and vector bundles](https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_2004__295__1_0.pdf), §3.7, pp.67–69. Uses semilinear B_dR-representations and their stable positive lattices. [Yiwen Ding — p-adic Hodge parameters in the crystabelline representations of GL_n](https://pmihes.centre-mersenne.org/item/10.1007/s10240-025-00156-2.pdf), §2.1.1–§2.1.2, pp.9–10. Defines and groups coefficient de Rham lattices by the embeddings σ.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p7-fontaine-bdr-indecomposable-classification"></a>

### Fontaine’s de Rham representation classification

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P7/fontaine-bdr-indecomposable-classification` (theorem).

For K/Q_p finite, the simple continuous semilinear B_dR-representations are indexed by G_K-orbits a in Kbar/Z. For a chosen lift A in Kbar, let D_a be the associated endomorphism division algebra with center K_a, [D_a:K_a]=p^{2s_a}, and d_a=[K_a:K]. The simple B_dR[a] has dimension d_ap^{s_a}; changing the lift by an integer gives an isomorphic simple. The indecomposables are B_dR[a;d]=B_dR[a]⊗_{Z_p}Z_p(0;d), where d≥1 and Z_p(0;d) is Fontaine’s logarithmic unipotent block. Every B_dR-representation has a unique finite decomposition into these blocks with multiplicities. An E-action is retained by passing to modules with commuting E-action; it is not discarded by the classification. The trivial de Rham objects are sums of B_dR, whereas almost de Rham logarithmic blocks need not be trivial.

**Hypotheses and scope.** The Sen-block notation D_a,K_a,s_a,d_a and Z_p(0;d) is defined by the Sen classification and logarithmic unipotent representation in Fontaine §§2.6 and 3.2.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Apply Fontaine’s decompletion to regular-singular K_∞((t))-connections. Reduce their semisimple blocks to the Sen representation classification; integer shifts are removed by multiplication by t. Identify the indecomposable logarithmic extensions and use their division-algebra endomorphisms and Krull–Schmidt uniqueness. Keep any commuting E-action throughout.

**Checks.** B_dR(χ_p^m)≅B_dR by a t-power, although a fixed positive lattice retains its integer jump. B_dR[0;2] is indecomposable and almost de Rham but not the trivial rank-two representation.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/coefficient-bdr-representations`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-coefficient-bdr-representations), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/plan/sen-module`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-plan-sen-module), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/plan/fontaine-dif-module`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-plan-fontaine-dif-module).

**Sources.** [Jean-Marc Fontaine — Almost C_p Galois representations and vector bundles](https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_2004__295__1_0.pdf), Proposition 3.18 and Theorem 3.19, pp.67–68; paragraph after Theorem 3.19, p.69. Classifies simples and indecomposables with their division-algebra dimensions and unique multiplicities.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p7-embedding-selective-crystalline-modification"></a>

### Embedding-selective de Rham lattice modification

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P7/embedding-selective-crystalline-modification` (construction).

In Ding Proposition 2.5’s generic noncritical crystabelline rank-n setup, fix σ:K→E and strictly decreasing labeled weights h_{τ,1}>⋯>h_{τ,n}, using HT(χ_p)=+1. Define an E-B-pair W_σ with the same e-component as W(D) and the same σ-component of W_dR^+. For τ≠σ, replace its lattice by t^{h_{τ,n}}(B_dR^+⊗_{K,τ}E)^n inside the common trivialized de Rham component. Berger’s equivalence gives D_σ with D⊂D_σ, D[1/t]=D_σ[1/t], D_pst(D)=D_pst(D_σ), and the σ-filtered de Rham components agree. At each other τ all weights become h_{τ,n}. This is the local period modification; deformation spaces and critical-type local models remain with their owners.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Use all generic/noncritical crystabelline hypotheses of Ding Proposition 2.5 and a common de Rham trivialization; the minimum-weight lattice contains the original.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Keep the e-part and σ-lattice, replace the other positive lattices by the displayed homotheties, and check G_K-stability. Use Fontaine’s de Rham representation and lattice description for the coefficient components. Apply Berger’s modification equivalence and invariance of the e-period functors to obtain D_σ.

**API.**

- `SigmaModification.lattice` (constructor): Preserve the σ-lattice and replace every other component by its minimum-weight homothety.
- `SigmaModification.inclusion` (relation): The original D maps into D_σ and the map becomes invertible after inverting t.
- `SigmaModification.potential_periods` (compatibility): The e-component and D_pst are unchanged.
- `SigmaModification.selected_filtration` (compatibility): The σ-filtered D_dR module is unchanged.

**Unit tests.**

- `SigmaModification.single_embedding` (degenerate): With one embedding the modification is the identity.
- `SigmaModification.other_weights` (computation): At τ≠σ, weights (3,1) become (1,1), since the replacement lattice is t^1 times the standard lattice.
- `SigmaModification.selected_weights` (compatibility): At σ, weights (3,1) retain both entries and their filtration.
- `SigmaModification.invert_t` (non-example): The lattice inclusion can be strict even though the e-components and t-inverted modules coincide.

**Uses.** Ding’s σ-deformation construction: Separates the selected embedding’s period data from the other embeddings without a new B-pair carrier..

**Checks.** For [K:Q_p]=1 and σ its sole embedding, D_σ=D.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/coefficient-b-pairs`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-coefficient-b-pairs), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/b-pair-robba-equivalence`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-b-pair-robba-equivalence), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/coefficient-bdr-representations`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-coefficient-bdr-representations), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/fontaine-bdr-indecomposable-classification`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-fontaine-bdr-indecomposable-classification).

**Sources.** [Yiwen Ding — p-adic Hodge parameters in the crystabelline representations of GL_n](https://pmihes.centre-mersenne.org/item/10.1007/s10240-025-00156-2.pdf), Proposition 2.5 and its proof, pp.13–14; §2.1, pp.9–10. Constructs the one-embedding modification and proves its period invariance, invoking Fontaine Theorem 3.19.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p7-cyclotomic-field-of-norms-interface"></a>

### Cyclotomic field of norms and Cohen periods

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P7/cyclotomic-field-of-norms-interface` (construction).

For K/Q_p finite, K_n=K(μ_{p^n}) and K_∞=union K_n, the field of norms X_K has multiplicative carrier lim_N K_n. Multiplication is coordinatewise; addition at level n is lim_m N_{K_{n+m}/K_n}(x_{n+m}+y_{n+m}). It is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic p, identified with the field E_K inside C^flat by the p-power limit. Finite extensions L_∞/K_∞ correspond to finite separable extensions X_L/X_K; hence H_K is canonically G_{X_K}. Choose its Cohen lift A_K inside W(C^flat), with residue E_K, and put B_K=A_K[1/p]. Let B be the p-adic completion of the maximal unramified extension of B_K inside W(C^flat)[1/p], A=B∩W(C^flat). Then B^{H_K}=B_K, and φ and Γ_K act compatibly. The overconvergent rings are the intersections B^{†,r}=B∩B̃^{†,r}, with B_K^{†,r}=(B^{†,r})^{H_K}.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Use the eventually totally ramified cyclotomic tower and its actual residue field; its Γ_K action is the residual G_K/H_K action. Cohen parameters are choices, and their coordinate formula is asserted only in the unramified cyclotomic case.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Construct the norm-limit addition using ramification estimates, prove the valuation and completeness, and compare with the tilt limit. Prove finite-extension descent and construct the Cohen lift by unramified lifting, extending φ and the Galois action. Intersect with the weighted Witt overconvergence condition.

**API.**

- `NormField.mul` (simp): Multiplication agrees with coordinatewise multiplication.
- `NormField.add` (characterisation): The n-th coordinate of a sum is the norm-limit formula, rather than coordinatewise addition.
- `NormField.finite_extension` (equivalence): Finite separable extensions are the extensions induced by finite extensions of the tower.
- `CohenPeriods.residue` (compatibility): A_K/p identifies with X_K and φ reduces to p-th power.
- `CohenPeriods.invariants` (characterisation): B^{H_K}=B_K and overconvergent invariants are B_K^{†,r}.

**Unit tests.**

- `NormField.characteristic` (computation): p times the unit is zero in X_K, although p is nonzero in each K_n.
- `NormField.cyclotomic` (compatibility): The compatible cyclotomic parameter maps to ε−1 in C^flat.
- `CohenPeriods.integral` (non-example): p is invertible in B_K and is a uniformizer in A_K; their integral lattices differ.
- `CohenPeriods.frobenius` (computation): For unramified K, φ(π_K)=(1+π_K)^p−1 reduces to π_K^p.

**Uses.** Berger Robba realization: Supplies the arithmetic subrings and H_K descent inside extended Witt periods.. Fontaine representation equivalence: Identifies the characteristic-p Galois group used by étale φ descent..

**Checks.** For K unramified, X_K=k((ε−1)), π_K=[ε]−1 and φ(π_K)=(1+π_K)^p−1.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field`, [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/plan/amice-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-annulus-foundations-plan-amice-ring), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/plan/overconvergent-cyclotomic-rings`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-annulus-foundations-plan-overconvergent-cyclotomic-rings).

**Sources.** [Laurent Berger — An introduction to the theory of p-adic representations](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0210184v1), §III.1.1 and §III.2.1–§III.3, pp.21–25. Constructs Cohen periods, the norm-limit field and its Galois and overconvergence interfaces.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p7-phi-gamma-module-interface"></a>

### Frobenius and cyclotomic modules

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P7/phi-gamma-module-interface` (definition).

Over B_K, B_K^† or B_{rig,K}^†, a (φ,Γ_K)-module is a finite free module D with a semilinear Frobenius whose linearization R⊗_{φ,R}D→D is invertible and a continuous semilinear Γ_K-action commuting with φ. Over B_K or B_K^† it is étale when it admits an A_K or A_K^† lattice L with φ^*L=L. Over the Robba ring it is étale when it is obtained from such an étale overconvergent module; equivalently its Newton slopes are all zero. With E-coefficients use finite projective modules of fixed rank over E⊗R and check étaleness on every coefficient factor.

**Hypotheses and scope.** K,E/Q_p finite; Frobenius acts trivially on E. A φ-stable lattice is insufficient without the invertible integral linearization. The topology and semilinear scalar action are included in morphisms and continuity.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Use the shared Cohen and Robba carriers and their operators. Define the linearization and commuting action; define morphisms intertwining both. Construct tensor and dual operations by linearization. Import the Robba slope-zero criterion from RD.1.

**API.**

- `PhiGamma.linearization` (data): The Frobenius linearization is an R-linear isomorphism.
- `PhiGamma.morphism` (characterisation): Morphisms are R-linear maps commuting with φ and every γ.
- `PhiGamma.tensor_dual` (constructor): Tensor, dual and determinant carry the induced commuting actions.
- `PhiGamma.etale_lattice` (characterisation): An integral lattice has invertible Frobenius linearization, not just φ(L)⊆L.
- `PhiGamma.coefficients` (functoriality): Finite coefficient extension preserves ranks and étaleness.

**Unit tests.**

- `PhiGamma.unit` (degenerate): The scalar rank-one object is étale with lattice A_K.
- `PhiGamma.nonunit` (non-example): φ(e)=pe is a legitimate rational rank-one φ-module but has slope one and is not étale.
- `PhiGamma.tate` (compatibility): For Q_p(1), a representation basis has φ(e)=e and γ(e)=χ_p(γ)e; its Robba slope is zero.
- `PhiGamma.commutation` (computation): Matrices P,G in a basis satisfy γ(P)G=φ(G)P; arbitrary matrices do not define the object.

**Uses.** Berger differential bridge: Supplies the carrier and commuting operators of D_rig^†(V).. Berger B-pair equivalence: Supplies its target category including non-étale objects..

**Checks.** The unit object has the scalar φ and Γ actions and integral lattice A_K.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/cyclotomic-field-of-norms-interface`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-cyclotomic-field-of-norms-interface), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/plan/robba-ring-of-p-adic-field`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-plan-robba-ring-of-p-adic-field), `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1`.

**Sources.** [Laurent Berger — B-paires et (φ,Γ)-modules](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0704.1083v2), §1.2 and Definition 1.2.2, p.10. Defines the finite-free semilinear actions and the slope convention. [Laurent Berger — An introduction to the theory of p-adic representations](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0210184v1), §III.1.1–§III.2.2, pp.21–23. States the integral unit-root criterion and representation realization.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p7-etale-realization-and-overconvergence"></a>

### Étale realization and overconvergence

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P7/etale-realization-and-overconvergence` (theorem).

The functors V↦D(V)=(B⊗V)^{H_K} and D↦(B⊗_{B_K}D)^{φ=1} are mutually inverse exact tensor equivalences between continuous finite-dimensional Q_p-representations of G_K and étale (φ,Γ_K)-modules over B_K. Every such D has a unique full-rank overconvergent realization D^† over B_K^†, with D=B_K⊗D^†. For every representation V, D^{†,r}(V)=(B^{†,r}⊗V)^{H_K} has rank dim V for sufficiently large r and D_rig^†(V)=B_rig,K^†⊗D^†(V). The equivalence extends to E-coefficients and to stable Z_p-lattices with integral étale modules. Overconvergence uses Γ_K and is not a theorem about arbitrary étale φ-modules.

**Hypotheses and scope.** K/Q_p finite. Integral descent uses finite free lattices and continuous action; rational coefficient extensions retain all factors.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Apply characteristic-p semilinear descent over the separable norm field and lift modulo p^n by Hensel and Hilbert 90. Take the complete limit and invert p; recover the residual Γ_K action. Apply the Cherbonnier–Colmez overconvergence theorem with its Tate–Sen estimates to obtain a finite-radius basis. Uniqueness follows from étale descent and the slope-zero full-faithfulness theorem.

**Checks.** For Q_p(n) the basis has φ(e)=e, γ(e)=χ_p(γ)^n e; changing to t^{-n}e exposes the period Frobenius p^{-n}.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/phi-gamma-module-interface`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-phi-gamma-module-interface), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/tate-sen-axioms-cyclotomic`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-tate-sen-axioms-cyclotomic).

**Sources.** [Laurent Berger — An introduction to the theory of p-adic representations](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0210184v1), §III.1.1, §III.2.2 and §III.3, pp.21–25. Explains descent and states the representation and overconvergence equivalences. [Laurent Berger — B-paires et (φ,Γ)-modules](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0704.1083v2), Theorem A, p.3; §2.2, pp.13–17. Identifies the étale subcategory in the Robba realization.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p7-herr-complex-interface"></a>

### Herr’s cyclotomic cohomology complex

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P7/herr-complex-interface` (construction).

Let Δ_K be the finite torsion subgroup of Γ_K and choose γ generating Γ_K/Δ_K. For a rational coefficient (φ,Γ)-module put D′=D^{Δ_K}, using the average |Δ_K|^{-1}Σδ. Define C_{φ,γ}(D) in degrees 0,1,2 as D′→D′⊕D′→D′, with d^0(x)=((γ−1)x,(φ−1)x) and d^1(a,b)=(φ−1)a−(γ−1)b. Its cohomology is independent of the generator and compatible with finite extensions. For D_rig^†(V) it equals continuous G_K-cohomology. For any finite-free Robba module it is finite dimensional, has Euler characteristic −[K:Q_p]rank D, and cup product with D^∨(1) followed by the trace yields perfect local duality.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Rational coefficients allow the torsion average even for p=2. Integral p=2 complexes require a separate torsion-resolution interface and are not asserted by this formula.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Commutation proves d^1d^0=0. Identify H^0 with joint invariants and H^1 with extensions, and compare generators by the cyclotomic difference operators. Use the overconvergent-to-Robba cohomology comparison and Liu’s finiteness, Euler characteristic and duality theorems. Compare the étale case with Herr’s Galois complex, including its trace normalization.

**API.**

- `HerrComplex.d_squared` (relation): d^1d^0=0 follows from φγ=γφ.
- `HerrComplex.h0` (characterisation): H^0=D^{φ=1,Γ_K=1}.
- `HerrComplex.generator_change` (equivalence): Generator change induces the canonical cohomology comparison.
- `HerrComplex.cup` (functoriality): The cup product uses y⊗γ(z)−x⊗φ(t) for degree-one representatives (x,y),(z,t).
- `HerrComplex.galois` (compatibility): For étale realizations the comparison intertwines the continuous Tate pairing.

**Unit tests.**

- `HerrComplex.commutation` (computation): Substitution gives (φ−1)(γ−1)x−(γ−1)(φ−1)x=0.
- `HerrComplex.unit` (degenerate): H^0 of the unit Robba module is Q_p, extended to E with E-coefficients.
- `HerrComplex.euler` (computation): For the unit over Q_p, dimensions (1,2,0) give Euler characteristic −1.
- `HerrComplex.duality` (compatibility): The cyclotomic line has H^2=Q_p and its trace matches the Tate local fundamental class.

**Uses.** Ding and Pan coefficient B-pairs: Provides their cohomology and duality after Berger’s equivalence.. Arithmetic Galois cohomology: Computes the continuous cohomology of the realized representations..

**Checks.** The signs and ordering of the two degree-one factors agree with Liu §2.1; swapping them requires changing d^1 and the cup formula.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/phi-gamma-module-interface`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-phi-gamma-module-interface), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/etale-realization-and-overconvergence`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-etale-realization-and-overconvergence), `ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.1`.

**Sources.** [Ruochuan Liu — Cohomology and duality for (φ,Γ)-modules over the Robba ring](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0711.4346v2), §2.1, pp.8–9; Theorems 0.1–0.3, p.3. Gives the complex, extension interpretation, cup formulas and cohomology theorems.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p7-wach-kisin-lattice-comparison"></a>

### Wach and Kisin lattice comparison

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P7/wach-kisin-lattice-comparison` (theorem).

Let K=Frac W(k) be unramified, T a stable Z_p-lattice in a crystalline representation with HT weights in {0,…,r}, r≥0. Use the contravariant integral functors: M(T) is the Kisin module and N(T) the Wach module. Put R=O_C^flat, S_ε=W(k)[[v]]⊂W(R) via v=[ε]−1, and R̂=W(R)∩ℛ_{K_0}, where ℛ_{K_0} consists of the convergent sums Σ f_i t^{\{i\}}, f_i∈S[1/p], f_i→0, with t^{\{i\}}=t^i/(p^{q(i)}q(i)!) and i=(p−1)q(i)+s(i), 0≤s(i)<p−1. The (φ,Ĝ)-structure on M(T) gives a canonical isomorphism N(T)≃(R̂⊗_{φ,S}M(T))^{H_{p∞}}, H_{p∞}=Gal(Kbar/K(μ_{p∞})). It preserves φ and the residual Γ_K action. Inside T^∨⊗W(R), the Kisin and Wach realizations become equal after scalar extension to R̂. This is a comparison through R̂ and invariants; it does not assert equality of the two original modules over different scalar rings.

**Hypotheses and scope.** K unramified and T crystalline; both modules are attached by the same contravariant convention. The rational period comparison with covariant D_cris uses dualization. Any p=2 application uses the integral classification and the modified τ argument in Liu Lemma 3.3.2.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Compare the two bases through D_cris(T[1/p]) over ℛ_{K_0}. The Wach and Kisin realization inclusions bound denominators by powers of v and the corresponding I^[1] generator. Use the saturation statement of Liu Lemma 3.1.3, iterated on those powers, to prove that the change matrix and its inverse are in W(R), hence in R̂. Compute ℛ_{K_0}^{H_{p∞}} from the unique expansion and the nontrivial Kummer τ action; intersection with W(R) gives S_ε. Taking invariants of the equal realized submodules recovers N(T).

**Checks.** For the trivial lattice both modules have rank one and the invariant comparison recovers the unit Wach module. The cyclotomic twist must be dualized when passing from these contravariant lattice functors to the covariant period basis t^{-1}.

**Prerequisites.** `FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4`, [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/cyclotomic-field-of-norms-interface`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-cyclotomic-field-of-norms-interface), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/plan/wach-dcris-comparison`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-plan-wach-dcris-comparison).

**Sources.** [Tong Liu — Compatibility of Kisin modules for different uniformizers](https://www.math.purdue.edu/~tongliu/pub/compatible.pdf), Theorem 1.0.2, p.2; §3.3, Theorem 3.3.1 and Lemma 3.3.2, pp.11–12; Lemma 3.1.3, p.9. Gives the invariant formula and proves the change-matrix and invariant steps, isolating the integral saturation input.

### Worked example — Tate twists in the Robba realization

Write e_n for the basis of D_rig(Q_p(n)) with φ(e_n)=e_n and γ(e_n)=χ_p(γ)^n e_n. The coefficient t transforms by χ_p, hence t^{−n}e_n is Γ-invariant. It belongs to the Robba module before inverting t precisely when n≤0; for n>0 the Γ-invariant submodule is zero. After inverting t, it spans the invariant line for every n. Frobenius on this invariant generator is p^{−n}, agreeing with D_cris. For a B-pair the positive de Rham lattice still matters: replacing B_dR^+ by B_dR would erase the filtration position and identify objects whose period vector spaces agree but whose integral period lattices differ. The Herr realization of the trivial representation must also retain H^2 and its Tate-duality trace, rather than being replaced by a fixed-vector calculation alone.


<a id="layer-r06-3"></a>

## R06.3 — Monodromy and Weil–Deligne comparison

Construct the differential equation of a de Rham representation and apply the analytic local-monodromy theorem over the correct constant field. Descend the resulting semistable periods and their Weil–Deligne parameter. Changing a period embedding, a finite extension or a monodromy normalization must give an explicit intertwining map, with the geometric-Frobenius convention retained.

**Landmarks:** Berger's (φ,∇)-module N_dR(V); p-adic monodromy theorem; Fontaine's Weil–Deligne recipe; Potentially semistable Weil–Deligne parameter; Berger’s filtered Robba module.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-r06-3-plan-de-rham-iff-dif-connection-trivial"></a>

### Fontaine's criterion: K_∞ ⊗_K D_dR(V) = ker(∇_V on D_dif(V)); V is de Rham iff ∇_V is trivial on D_dif(V)

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/plan/de-rham-iff-dif-connection-trivial` (theorem).

Throughout: p is a prime, K a finite extension of Q_p with residue field k, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], K_n = K(μ_{p^n}), K_∞ = ∪K_n, H_K = Gal(K̄/K_∞), Γ_K = G_K/H_K identified with an open subgroup of Z_p^× by χ, F'_K = K_∞ ∩ K_0^nr (the maximal unramified extension of K_0 in K_∞), r_n = p^{n−1}(p−1), n(r) the least n with r ≤ r_n, π = [ε] − 1 ∈ A_inf, q = φ(π)/π, π̄ = ε − 1 ∈ O_{C^♭}, t = log(1+π) = log[ε]. For every p-adic representation V of G_K: K_∞ ⊗_K D_dR(V) is the kernel of ∇_V acting on D_dif(V); in particular V is de Rham iff the meromorphic connection on D_dif(V) is trivial (flat), i.e. dim_{K_∞} ker(∇_V) = d. Moreover, if V is de Rham with Hodge–Tate weights ≤ 0 then K_∞[[t]] ⊗_K D_dR(V) ⊂ D_dif^+(V) ⊃ t^w D_dif^+(V) for some w ≥ 0.

**Hypotheses and scope.** D_dR(V) = (B_dR ⊗ V)^{G_K} (R06.2/period-functors); Hodge–Tate weights in the convention of PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/hodge-tate-weight-convention.

**Construction or proof.**

1. ∇_V kills K_∞ ⊗ D_dR(V), and t^r K_∞[[t]] ⊗_K D_dR(V) is a finitely generated Γ_K-stable K_∞[[t]]-submodule of (B_dR^+ ⊗ V)^{H_K} for r ≫ 0, hence lies in D_dif^+(V).
2. The kernel of ∇_V on D_dif(V) is a finite-dimensional K_∞-space (at most dim_{K_∞((t))} D_dif(V)), Γ_K-stable, hence of the form K_∞ ⊗ W_n for a Γ_K-stable K_n-space W_n; the Lie algebra of Γ_K acts trivially on W_n, so an open subgroup Γ_{K_m} acts trivially (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/lie-algebra-trivial-gamma-action), and W_n ⊂ D_dR(V|_{G_{K_m}}) = K_m ⊗_K D_dR(V) (Hilbert 90 for K_m/K, R06.2/period-functors).
3. Equivalently (Brinon–Conrad Propositions 15.4.13 and 15.4.15): K_∞ ⊗_K D_dif(V)^{Γ_K} ≅ D_dif(V)^{∇=0} and D_dif(V)^{Γ_K} = D_dR(V).

**Checks.** V = Q_p(n): ker ∇_V = K_∞·t^{−n}e_n = K_∞ ⊗ D_dR(Q_p(n)). A non-split extension of Q_p(1) by Q_p is Hodge–Tate but not de Rham (Brinon–Conrad §6.3): ker ∇_V has K_∞-dimension 1 < 2.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/plan/fontaine-dif-module`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-plan-fontaine-dif-module), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/period-functors`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-period-functors), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/plan/sen-module`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-plan-sen-module), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/hodge-tate-weight-convention`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-hodge-tate-weight-convention).

**Proof ingredients.** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/lie-algebra-trivial-gamma-action`; their statements and locators appear in the proof-ingredient index.

**Sources.** [L. Berger — Représentations p-adiques et équations différentielles](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0102179v3), Proposition 5.9, p. 51. Statement. [O. Brinon and B. Conrad — CMI Summer School notes on p-adic Hodge theory](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/notes.pdf), Proposition 15.4.15, p. 285. Public proof of the criterion.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-r06-3-plan-de-rham-differential-equation"></a>

### Berger's (φ,∇)-module N_dR(V) of a de Rham representation

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/plan/de-rham-differential-equation` (construction).

Throughout: p is a prime, K a finite extension of Q_p with residue field k, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], K_n = K(μ_{p^n}), K_∞ = ∪K_n, H_K = Gal(K̄/K_∞), Γ_K = G_K/H_K identified with an open subgroup of Z_p^× by χ, F'_K = K_∞ ∩ K_0^nr (the maximal unramified extension of K_0 in K_∞), r_n = p^{n−1}(p−1), n(r) the least n with r ≤ r_n, π = [ε] − 1 ∈ A_inf, q = φ(π)/π, π̄ = ε − 1 ∈ O_{C^♭}, t = log(1+π) = log[ε]. Let V be a de Rham representation of G_K of dimension d with Hodge–Tate weights ≤ 0 (convention HT(χ_p) = +1). There is a unique B†_rig,K-submodule N_dR(V) ⊂ D†_rig(V), free of rank d and stable by ∂_V = t^{−1}∇_V. It is stable by φ and Γ_K, satisfies φ^*N_dR(V) = N_dR(V) (the linearisation of φ is an isomorphism), N_dR(V)[1/t] = D†_rig(V)[1/t], and for s ≫ 0 there is N_s ⊂ D†,s_rig(V) free of rank d, stable by ∂_V and Γ_K, with N_dR(V) = B†_rig,K ⊗ N_s. For general de Rham V, N_dR(V) := t^{−h}N_dR(V(−h)) ⊗ e_h ⊂ D†_rig(V)[1/t] for any h ≥ (largest Hodge–Tate weight), independent of h. Thus (N_dR(V), φ, ∂_V) is a p-adic differential equation with Frobenius structure over B†_rig,K.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Hodge–Tate weights ≤ 0 is needed for N_dR(V) ⊂ D†_rig(V) (otherwise only N_dR(V) ⊂ D†_rig(V)[1/t]). Called N_dR by analogy with Wach modules (Berger's Théorème 5.10).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Take N_s from PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/de-rham-lattice-Ns: free of rank d with ∇_V(N_s) ⊂ tN_s, i.e. ∂_V-stable; Γ_K-stable by construction.
2. For s_1 ≤ s_2, B†,s_2_rig,K ⊗ N_{s_1} ⊂ N_{s_2} is an equality by uniqueness (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/determinant-of-stable-submodule); set N_dR(V) = B†_rig,K ⊗ N_s, independent of s.
3. φ(N_s) is free of rank d in D†,ps_rig(V) and ∂_V-stable (∂_V∘φ = pφ∘∂_V, PadicHodgeTheory:P7/plan/connection-on-robba-realisation), so φ(N_s) = N_ps by uniqueness; hence φ(N_dR(V)) ⊂ N_dR(V) and φ^*N_dR(V) is a free rank-d ∂_V-stable submodule, equal to N_dR(V).
4. Uniqueness of N_dR(V) itself: N_dR(V) determines N_s, which is unique (Berger proof of Théorème 5.10).
5. The twisted definition for general V is independent of h by the uniqueness statement applied to V(−h) and V(−h−1) (t·N_dR(V(−h)) ⊗ e_{−1} is ∂-stable of rank d).

**API.**

- `deRhamDiffEq` (constructor): N_dR(V) ⊂ D†_rig(V) for de Rham V with weights ≤ 0 (twisted definition in general).
- `deRhamDiffEq_free` (characterisation): N_dR(V) is free of rank d and N_dR(V)[1/t] = D†_rig(V)[1/t].
- `deRhamDiffEq_unique` (characterisation): N_dR(V) is the unique free rank-d ∂_V-stable submodule of D†_rig(V).
- `deRhamDiffEq_frobenius` (structure): φ(N_dR(V)) ⊂ N_dR(V) and φ^*N_dR(V) = N_dR(V).
- `deRhamDiffEq_gamma` (structure): N_dR(V) is Γ_K-stable and ∂_V∘φ = pφ∘∂_V on it.
- `deRhamDiffEq_crystalline` (compatibility): For V crystalline with weights ≤ 0, N_dR(V) = B†_rig,K ⊗_{K_0} D_cris(V).
- `deRhamDiffEq_functor` (functoriality): V ↦ N_dR(V) is an exact faithful ⊗-functor from de Rham representations (with the twisted definition) to p-adic differential equations with Frobenius structure.

**Unit tests.**

- `deRhamDiffEq_twist` (computation): For V = Q_p(−n), n ≥ 0: N_dR(V) = t^n·D†_rig(V) = B†_rig,K·(t^n e_{−n}), with ∂_V(t^n e_{−n}) = 0.
- `deRhamDiffEq_trivial` (degenerate): For V = Q_p: N_dR(V) = D†_rig(V) = B†_rig,K with ∂_V = ∂.
- `deRhamDiffEq_crystalline_eq` (compatibility): For V crystalline with weights ≤ 0: N_dR(V) = B†_rig,K ⊗_{K_0} D_cris(V) (Berger intro IV.4).
- `deRhamDiffEq_not_for_nonDeRham` (non-example): For a non-split extension V of Q_p(1) by Q_p (Hodge–Tate, not de Rham) no free rank-2 ∂_V-stable submodule of D†_rig(V)[1/t] exists (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/robba-lattice-implies-de-rham).

**Uses.** Berger 2002, Théorème 5.19: input to André's/Kedlaya's local monodromy theorem. PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/berger-form-of-local-monodromy: M = N_dR(V) is the finitely presented module with connection and Frobenius structure. Berger 2008, Théorème V.2.3: D_st,L(V) = Sol_L(N_dR(V)) and N_dR(V) = (B†_rig,L[ℓ_X] ⊗ D_st,L(V))^{H_K, N=0}.

**Checks.** V crystalline with weights ≤ 0: N_dR(V) = B†_rig,K ⊗_{K_0} D_cris(V) (Berger intro IV.4). V semistable with weights ≤ 0: N_dR(V) = (B†_log,K ⊗_{K_0} D_st(V))^{N=0} (Berger intro IV.4; Berger 2008 Théorème V.2.3(3)).

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/plan/extended-robba-ring-with-galois-action`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-plan-extended-robba-ring-with-galois-action), ### The p-adic monodromy theorem: every de Rham representation is potentially semistable

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/plan/p-adic-monodromy-theorem` (theorem).

Throughout: p is a prime, K a finite extension of Q_p with residue field k, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], K_n = K(μ_{p^n}), K_∞ = ∪K_n, H_K = Gal(K̄/K_∞), Γ_K = G_K/H_K identified with an open subgroup of Z_p^× by χ, F'_K = K_∞ ∩ K_0^nr (the maximal unramified extension of K_0 in K_∞), r_n = p^{n−1}(p−1), n(r) the least n with r ≤ r_n, π = [ε] − 1 ∈ A_inf, q = φ(π)/π, π̄ = ε − 1 ∈ O_{C^♭}, t = log(1+π) = log[ε]. Let E/Q_p be finite and V a de Rham E-linear representation of G_K (K/Q_p finite). Then V is potentially semistable: there is a finite Galois extension L/K such that V|_{G_L} is semistable, i.e. dim_{L_0} (B_st ⊗_{Q_p} V)^{G_L} = dim_{Q_p} V. Conversely every potentially semistable representation is de Rham. Moreover, for V with Hodge–Tate weights ≤ 0, L can be chosen so that Γ_L acts trivially on Sol_L := (N_dR(V) ⊗_{B†_rig,K} B†_log,L)^{∂_V=0}, and then F'_L = L_0 and Sol_L = D_st(V|_{G_L}) as (φ,N)-modules.

**Hypotheses and scope.** K is a finite extension of Q_p (so the Robba rings involved are those of PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/berger-form-of-local-monodromy, stated there for K/Q_p finite); Berger's reduction to an algebraically closed residue field is not needed. The solution space of the RD.2 export is naturally an F'_L-vector space (F'_L = L_∞ ∩ K_0^nr, the constants of B†_rig,L), not an L ∩ K_0^nr-space; the proof enlarges L so that Γ_L fixes F'_L, after which F'_L = L_0.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Reduce to Hodge–Tate weights ≤ 0: V is potentially semistable (resp. de Rham) iff V(−h) is, since t ∈ B_st^{G_L}-eigen: D_st,L(V(−h)) = t^{h}D_st,L(V) ⊗ e_{−h} (R06.1/fontaine-element-t, R06.2/period-functors).
2. Form N_dR(V) (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/plan/de-rham-differential-equation); it satisfies the hypotheses of RD.2/berger-form-of-local-monodromy (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/de-rham-differential-equation-has-frobenius-structure).
3. PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/berger-form-of-local-monodromy (via RD.2/logarithmic-form-of-local-monodromy): there is a finite L/K such that Sol_L generates N_dR(V) ⊗ B†_log,L and has dimension d over the constants F'_L of B†_log,L (PadicHodgeTheory:P7/antiderivatives-on-log-robba-ring (3)).
4. Sol_L is Γ_L-stable (γ∂_V = χ(γ)^{−1}∂_Vγ) and ∇ = t∂_V vanishes on it; by PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/lie-algebra-trivial-gamma-action an open subgroup Γ_{L'} (L' = L(ε^{(m)}), m ≫ 0, so L'_∞ = L_∞) acts trivially; then Γ_{L'} fixes F'_{L'} = F'_L (γ(λs) = γ(λ)s for s ∈ Sol_L), so F'_L ⊂ L' ∩ K_0^nr = L'_0.
5. N_dR(V) ⊗ B†_log,L' ⊂ D†_log(V|_{G_{L'}}) (N_dR(V) ⊂ D†_rig(V) and D†(V|_{G_{L'}}) = B†_{L'} ⊗ D†(V), the P7 norm-field and étale-realization interfaces), so Sol_L ⊂ (D†_log(V|_{G_{L'}})[1/t])^{Γ_{L'}} = D_st(V|_{G_{L'}}) (PadicHodgeTheory:P7/plan/berger-dcris-dst-dictionary over L'); dim_{L'_0} Sol_L = d ≥ dim D_st(V|_{G_{L'}}) forces equality: V|_{G_{L'}} is semistable.
6. Converse: if V|_{G_L} is semistable then it is de Rham over L (L ⊗_{L_0} B_st ⊂ B_dR, R06.2/admissible-representations), and a representation that is de Rham over a finite extension is de Rham, by Hilbert 90 for the semilinear Gal(L/K)-action on D_dR(V|_{G_L}) (Fontaine–Ouyang Proposition 6.58).
7. E-coefficients: apply the theorem to the underlying Q_p-representation.

**Checks.** V = Q_p(n): L = K suffices (crystalline). V = E(ψ) with ψ a finite-order character: de Rham (C-admissible) and semistable exactly over L = K̄^{ker ψ}; the minimal L is the splitting field. V = V_p(E) for E/K with potentially good reduction: potentially crystalline, with L the field over which E acquires good reduction (application in R06.6). A Hodge–Tate, non-de Rham V (non-split extension of Q_p(1) by Q_p, Brinon–Conrad §6.3) is not potentially semistable: the theorem does not extend to Hodge–Tate representations.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/plan/de-rham-differential-equation`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-3-plan-de-rham-differential-equation), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/plan/connection-on-robba-realisation`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-plan-connection-on-robba-realisation), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/plan/nabla-operator-on-robba-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-plan-nabla-operator-on-robba-ring), `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/berger-form-of-local-monodromy`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/logarithmic-form-of-local-monodromy`, [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/plan/sen-module`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-plan-sen-module), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/period-functors`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-period-functors), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/plan/overconvergent-cyclotomic-rings`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-annulus-foundations-plan-overconvergent-cyclotomic-rings), `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/log-robba-ring-antiderivative`, [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/plan/log-extended-period-rings`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-plan-log-extended-period-rings), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/cyclotomic-field-of-norms-interface`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-cyclotomic-field-of-norms-interface), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/plan/berger-dcris-dst-dictionary`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-plan-berger-dcris-dst-dictionary), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/plan/de-rham-iff-dif-connection-trivial`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-3-plan-de-rham-iff-dif-connection-trivial), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/admissible-representations`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-admissible-representations), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/fontaine-element-t`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-fontaine-element-t), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/semistable-period-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-semistable-period-ring), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P7/etale-realization-and-overconvergence`](#target-padichodgetheory-p7-etale-realization-and-overconvergence).
