Devissage gives finite p-power coefficients, the inverse-limit theorem gives finite Z_p-cohomology, and inversion of p kills almost errors. For B_dR^+ use its filtered quotients, gr^j=Ô_X(j), finite-coefficient primitive comparison and controlled inverse limits as in Scholze Theorem 8.4. The argument uses the perfectoid and almost section calculations directly.

**Checks.** For X=Spa(C,O_C), H^0(F_p)=F_p and all higher finite-constant cohomology vanishes. For P^1_C, H^0 and H^2(F_p) have dimension 1 and H^1=0. An arbitrary nonproper smooth affinoid is not covered by the finiteness conclusion.

**Prerequisites.** `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3`, `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6`, [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/etale-proetale-cohomology-and-base-change`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-etale-proetale-cohomology-and-base-change).

**Sources.** [Peter Scholze — p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.3463v2), Theorem 5.1, pp.28–29; Lemmas 5.6 and 5.8–5.10 and proof, pp.31–34; Theorem 8.4 and proof, pp.48–50. Proves the early almost primitive theorem by finite covers and tilted Artin–Schreier, then the positive-period comparison.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-etale-proetale-cohomology-and-base-change"></a>

### Étale–pro-étale cohomology and base change

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/etale-proetale-cohomology-and-base-change` (theorem).

Let ν:X_proet→X_et for a locally noetherian adic space. For an abelian étale sheaf F, F→Rν_*ν^*F is invertible. In particular étale and pro-étale cohomology agree for F_p-local systems and for the uncompleted étale sheaf O_X^+/p pulled back by ν. If f:X→Y is qcqs, ν_Y^*Rf_et*F→Rf_proet*ν_X^*F is invertible. For qcqs U=lim_jU_j in X_proet, H^i(U,ν^*F)=colim_jH^i(U_j,F). The assertion does not identify a completed integral sheaf with its uncompleted pullback in every topology.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Locally noetherian spaces and qcqs f or U where stated; F is an étale sheaf before pullback.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Compute an injective étale sheaf on inverse limits of qcqs étale objects. Reduce finite pro-étale covers to finite-stage étale covers and pass their Čech complexes through filtered colimits. This proves the cohomology formula, the adjunction and the proper base-change map by sheafification.

**Checks.** The statement applies to ν^*(O_X^+/p), and completion is handled separately by the local-acyclicity theorem.

**Prerequisites.** `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1`, `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0`.

**Sources.** [Peter Scholze — p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.3463v2), Lemma 3.16 and Corollary 3.17, pp.19–20. Computes the cohomology of pulled-back étale sheaves and the qcqs base-change map.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-early-relative-primitive-comparison"></a>

### Relative primitive comparison

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/early-relative-primitive-comparison` (theorem).

For a proper smooth morphism f:X→S of locally noetherian adic spaces over Q_p and a finite F_p-local system L, (R^if_et*L)⊗O_S^{+a}/p→R^if_et*(L⊗O_X^{+a}/p) is an almost isomorphism. On the pro-étale site, if the finite-coefficient direct images of a finite free lisse Z_p-sheaf T are locally constant finite modules with the required inverse-limit control, R^if_*T⊗Ô_S→R^if_*(T⊗Ô_X) is an isomorphism. In particular R^if_*Ẑ_p⊗Ô_S≅R^if_*Ô_X under the local-freeness hypothesis on every R^if_*F_p used by Caraiani–Scholze.

**Hypotheses and scope.** The almost ideal is the sheaf of locally topologically nilpotent elements. The rational statement retains the finite-coefficient local-freeness and limit hypotheses.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Apply absolute primitive comparison at conservative geometric pro-étale fibers and proper base change. Use étale–pro-étale agreement to transport the finite-coefficient map. Pass through p-power devissage and controlled inverse limits and invert p.

**Checks.** For f the identity, the comparison is the scalar-extension identity. Geometric fiberwise comparison alone does not justify an uncontrolled inverse limit.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/early-primitive-comparison-and-finiteness`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-early-primitive-comparison-and-finiteness), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/etale-proetale-cohomology-and-base-change`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-etale-proetale-cohomology-and-base-change), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/lisse-zp-sheaf`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-lisse-zp-sheaf), `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0`, `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2`.

**Sources.** [Peter Scholze — p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.3463v2), Corollary 5.11, p.34 (arXiv v2); Theorem 8.8, pp.52–53. Gives the relative almost primitive theorem and the lisse-relative comparison hypotheses. [Ana Caraiani, Peter Scholze — On the generic part of the cohomology of compact unitary Shimura varieties](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1511.02418), Theorem 2.2.2 and Proposition 2.2.5, pp.14–15. Uses the primitive completed-structure comparison under finite-coefficient local freeness.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-fundamental-period-sheaf-sequences"></a>

### Fundamental crystalline period-sheaf sequences

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/fundamental-period-sheaf-sequences` (theorem).

In Tan–Tong’s absolutely unramified smooth formal-model setting, with the pro-étale crystalline sheaves and their completed filtration, the map 1−φ gives an exact sequence 0→Q_p→Fil^0B_cris→B_cris→0. Multiplication by t^r gives 0→Q_p(r)→Fil^rB_cris→B_cris→0 with map 1−p^{−r}φ for every integer r. The scalar sequence 0→Q_p→B_cris^{φ=1}→B_dR/B_dR^+→0 holds at the arithmetic geometric point. Its proposed sheaf analogue requires a separate local lifting proof and is not inferred from scalar exactness.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Fix the map B_cris→B_dR and the chosen cyclotomic t; retain the source’s base restrictions for structural crystalline periods.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Use the scalar fundamental sequences on geometric fibers and solve the Frobenius equation pro-étale locally on perfectoid objects. Check that the filtered image in the de Rham quotient is independent of the local generator. Use the exactness theorem of Tan–Tong for the stated unramified structural setting.

**Checks.** At a geometric point these are the scalar Fontaine sequences. The arrows form two short exact sequences; they are not one sequence obtained by concatenating their middle terms.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/fundamental-exact-sequence`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-fundamental-exact-sequence), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/bcris-twisted-frobenius-sequences`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-bcris-twisted-frobenius-sequences), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/crystalline-period-sheaves`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-crystalline-period-sheaves).

**Sources.** [Fucheng Tan; Jilong Tong — Crystalline comparison isomorphisms in p-adic Hodge theory: the absolutely unramified case](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1510.05543v2), Theorem 3.18 and proof, p.32. The filtered fundamental exact sequence is stated for the absolutely unramified formal-model period sheaves. [Olivier Brinon — Représentations p-adiques cristallines et de de Rham dans le cas relatif](https://www.numdam.org/item/MSMF_2008_2_112__1_0.pdf), Lemma 6.2.23 and Proposition 6.2.24, pp.84–85. The relative scalar invariant-to-quotient fundamental sequence is proved by the filtered Frobenius calculation.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-first-order-fundamental-period-diagram"></a>

### The first-order fundamental period diagram

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/first-order-fundamental-period-diagram` (theorem).

For a smooth rigid space X over complete algebraically closed C/Q_p, there is a natural commutative diagram of short exact pro-étale sheaf sequences: 0→Q_p(1)→(B_cris^+)^{φ=p}→Ô_X→0 and 0→Ô_X(1)→B_dR^+/t²→Ô_X→0. The right vertical map is the identity, the middle map is the period embedding followed by reduction modulo t², and the left map is the natural inclusion Q_p(1)→Ô_X(1). The top surjection is θ; the bottom is θ modulo t². The lower kernel is tB_dR^+/t², identified with Ô_X(1), not with the constant Q_p(1).

**Hypotheses and scope.** Period sheaves are shared with the corrected local-rational construction; exactness is in sheaves, not necessarily on every affinoid perfectoid section ring.

**Construction or proof.**

1. The lower row follows from gr^1 B_dR^+=Ô_X(1). Solve the φ=p lifting problem pro-étale locally for the top row by the crystalline fundamental-sequence construction. Multiplication by t identifies its kernel with the cyclotomic constant sheaf. Functoriality of θ and the period embedding makes the diagram commute.

**Checks.** At Spa(C,O_C) the two left terms are Q_p(1) and C(1), respectively. The natural cohomological boundary is used together with the intrinsic Kummer-to-dlog isomorphism; the rows alone do not compute curve cohomology.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/crystalline-period-sheaves`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-crystalline-period-sheaves), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/graded-de-rham-period-sheaf-tate-twist`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-graded-de-rham-period-sheaf-tate-twist), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/fundamental-period-sheaf-sequences`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-fundamental-period-sheaf-sequences).

**Sources.** [Pierre Colmez, Gabriel Dospinescu and Wiesława Nizioł — Cohomologie p-adique de la tour de Drinfeld : le cas de la dimension 1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1704.08928), §0.6.2, p.10; §3.2, pp.28–29. Uses precisely these two exact rows and their common right term for the canonical comparison diagram.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-model-relative-log-pd-period-complex"></a>

### Logarithmic period complexes of semistable charts

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/model-relative-log-pd-period-complex` (construction).

For a semistable chart R/O_K in Colmez–Nizioł §2.1, let S=R_π^PD be the logarithmic PD lift over the uniformizer variable, Λ=A_cris(Rbar), and ι:S→Λ the Kummer root embedding. Form the p-adically completed log-PD envelope E_R^PD of the multiplication map S⊗_{O_F}Λ→Λ, with partial PD level s=0 for p≥3 and s=1 for p=2. In logarithmic coordinates V_j=X_j/ι(X_j), sections have unique convergent expansions Σ_k a_k∏_j(1−V_j)^{[k_j]}, with a_k→0. The filtration is a_k∈Fil^{r−|k|}Λ, and the relative log connection is ∂_j=X_j∂/∂X_j. Frobenius and G_R act diagonally and extend continuously. The filtered log de Rham complex resolves Fil^rΛ after inverting p. This is a model-relative log-PD object; it is not a globally chosen polynomial OB_cris[u].

**Hypotheses and scope.** R has the semistable presentation of §2.1; use the source’s logarithmic base, p-adic completions and compatible Kummer roots. The PD lift and envelopes themselves are imported from CR.5–CR.6.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Apply the universal log-PD envelope to the chart map. Use the coefficient-extraction map and log derivations to prove uniqueness of the expansion, then lift from the étale toric chart to prove existence (Lemma 2.36). The source’s explicit contracting homotopy has denominators bounded by p^s; thus Lemma 2.37 is a p^s-quasi-isomorphism and becomes exact after inverting p. Extend φ and G_R by the formulas on the V_j and the PD universal property (Lemma 2.40).

**API.**

- `LogPDPeriods.augmentation` (projection): Multiplication extends to E_R^PD→Λ and extracts the constant expansion coefficient.
- `LogPDPeriods.expansion` (characterisation): The displayed multi-index expansion is unique and its coefficients satisfy the precise filtration criterion.
- `LogPDPeriods.connection` (relation): The log derivations commute, the connection is integrable and Griffiths-transversal.
- `LogPDPeriods.poincare` (equivalence): Fil^rΛ→Fil^rΩ^•_{E_R^PD/Λ} is a p^s-quasi-isomorphism, hence a rational quasi-isomorphism.
- `LogPDPeriods.operators` (compatibility): φ and G_R extend and commute with their prescribed action on logarithmic coordinates.

**Unit tests.**

- `LogPDPeriods.point` (compatibility): At R=O_K use Y=(1+X)^{−1}−1 relative to Breuil’s coordinate X. Then N(Y)=−(1+Y), φ(Y)=(1+Y)^p−1 and g(Y)=[ε_π(g)]^{−1}(1+Y)−1; both conventions satisfy Nφ=pφN.
- `LogPDPeriods.constant` (degenerate): The augmentation of a constant a∈Λ is a; all positive-index divided powers map to zero.
- `LogPDPeriods.p_two` (non-example): At p=2 the integral contracting homotopy has a bounded factor p; ordinary integral exactness is not asserted.
- `LogPDPeriods.filtration` (computation): A coefficient multiplying a PD monomial of total degree m lies in Fil^{r−m}Λ in filtration step r.

**Uses.** Colmez–Nizioł local syntomic comparison: Linearizes the log connection and transports Frobenius to the nearby-cycle computation.. Semistable model comparison: Gives an actual log-PD period evaluation for the model’s charts..

**Checks.** The logarithmic PD coordinate V_j−1 is present; replacing it by an ordinary polynomial variable gives the wrong integral ring.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/breuil-completed-semistable-rings`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-breuil-completed-semistable-rings), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.6`, [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/crystalline-period-sheaves`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-crystalline-period-sheaves).

**Sources.** [Pierre Colmez and Wiesława Nizioł — Syntomic complexes and p-adic nearby cycles](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~wieslawa.niziol/logvanishing6.pdf), §2.6.1–§2.6.3, Lemmas 2.36–2.40 and Example 2.41, pp.27–30. Defines the completed log-PD ring, expansion, filtration, contracting homotopy and operators; the point case is the completed semistable period ring.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-constructible-primitive-comparison"></a>

### Constructible primitive comparison with compact supports

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/constructible-primitive-comparison` (theorem).

Let f:X→Y be a proper morphism of algebraic varieties over complete algebraically closed C/Q_p, let C^+⊆O_C be an open valuation subring, and let F be a constructible F_p-sheaf on X_et. On associated adic spaces the natural map (R^if_*F)^ad⊗O_Y^{+a}/p→R^if_*^ad(F^ad⊗O_X^{+a}/p) is an almost isomorphism for every i. In particular, for j:U↪X with X proper and F a finite locally constant Z/p^n-sheaf on U, H^i_et(X,j_!F)⊗O_C^a/p^n≅H^i_et(X^ad,j_!(F^ad⊗O_U^{+a}/p^n)); these groups on the left are finite. Naturality includes maps of pairs and finite coefficient change. X need not be smooth, so the statement applies to a singular minimal compactification once its algebraic model is supplied.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Constructibility and properness are essential. The p^n assertion follows by finite devissage from the F_p comparison; no unrestricted constructible Z_p assertion is included.

**Construction or proof.**

1. First prove the closed-immersion restriction formula for O^+/p. For a normal-crossings boundary, resolve j_!F_p by the alternating complex of its closed strata and apply smooth primitive comparison. Use characteristic-zero resolution and proper base change to replace a general compactification by that case. Trivialize a lisse F_p-sheaf after a finite étale torsor and use its normalized proper cover and Čech resolution. Induct on support dimension for constructible F. For the relative assertion check geometric stalks by proper base change. Devissage through multiplication by p proves the finite p^n form.

**Checks.** For U=X and X smooth proper this is the earlier primitive comparison. For an empty U both sides are zero; for a nonempty boundary j_! is retained and cannot be replaced by j_*.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/early-primitive-comparison-and-finiteness`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-early-primitive-comparison-and-finiteness), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/etale-proetale-cohomology-and-base-change`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-etale-proetale-cohomology-and-base-change), `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2`, `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H5`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4`.

**Sources.** [Peter Scholze — Perfectoid spaces: a survey](https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.5948), Theorem 3.13, Lemmas 3.14–3.16 and proof, pp.17–20. Derives constructible proper comparison by strata, resolution, finite covers and support induction. [Peter Scholze — On torsion in the cohomology of locally symmetric varieties](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v182-n3-p03-p.pdf), Proof of Theorem 4.2.1, published p.1021. Uses this extension-by-zero comparison on the proper minimal compactification.

### Worked example — The arithmetic and geometric direct images

For a geometric point over C, Ô has sections C and no positive-degree rational cohomology. Over a complete discretely valued base k, the arithmetic direct image has R^0ν_*Ô=O_X and R^1ν_*Ô=O_X·log χ. With twist one, the nonzero images occur in degrees one and two and are Ω_X^1 and Ω_X^1·log χ. These are different from the geometric direct images R^iν_*Ô(i)=Ω_X^i. Locally, with toric coordinate T and lift [T^flat], the structural displacement u=T⊗1−1⊗[T^flat] satisfies ∇u=dT. Taking horizontal sections removes these structural variables and recovers the nonstructural period sheaf. For a smooth map with base coordinates, the relative horizontal sections retain formal power series in those base variables; this explains the completed tensor product at the beginning of the relative Poincaré resolution.


<a id="layer-p8"></a>

## P8 — Relative periods and local systems

Glue local periods into tensor functors on relative local systems and filtered connections. Proper smooth pushforward preserves de Rham pairs under the stated local-system hypotheses. Relative Hodge–Tate filtrations, horizontal monodromy on polyannuli and Witt/Robba sheaves have distinct objects and assumptions. Untilting patching supplies two-period pairs; the geometry of the relative curve belongs to RF1 and VB1.

**Landmarks:** B_dR^+-local systems and integrable connections; Filtered modules with integrable connection; Associated de Rham pairs; Horizontal relative periods; Relative Frobenius realization; Gauss–Manin de Rham pairs.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-bdr-plus-local-system"></a>

### B_dR^+-local systems and OB_dR^+-modules with integrable connection

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/bdr-plus-local-system` (definition).

Let X smooth over Spa(k, O_k), k a complete discretely valued extension of Q_p with perfect residue field κ. (i) A B_dR^+-local system is a sheaf of B_dR^+-modules M on X_proét that is locally on X_proét free of finite rank. (ii) An OB_dR^+-module with integrable connection is a sheaf of OB_dR^+-modules ℳ on X_proét, locally free of finite rank, with an integrable connection ∇_ℳ: ℳ → ℳ ⊗_{O_X} Ω¹_X satisfying the Leibniz rule for ∇ on OB_dR^+. Morphisms are module maps, compatible with ∇ in (ii). A B_dR^+-local system M has the filtration Fil^i M = Fil^i B_dR^+·M and gr⁰M = M/Fil¹M, a locally free Ô_X-module; every lisse Ẑ_p-sheaf L gives the B_dR^+-local system L ⊗_{Ẑ_p} B_dR^+.

**Hypotheses and scope.** X smooth over Spa(k, O_k), k a complete discretely valued extension of Q_p with perfect residue field κ.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Definitions; tensor products, duals and internal Hom of locally free modules are again locally free; the tensor connection is ∇ ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ ∇.

**API.**

- `BdRPlusLocalSystem` (data): A sheaf of B_dR^+-modules on X_proét locally free of finite rank.
- `OBdRPlusConnection` (data): A locally free OB_dR^+-module of finite rank with an integrable connection satisfying the Leibniz rule for ∇.
- `BdRPlusLocalSystem.ofLisse` (constructor): L ↦ L ⊗_{Ẑ_p} B_dR^+ for a lisse Ẑ_p-sheaf L.
- `BdRPlusLocalSystem.tensor` (structure): Tensor product, dual and internal Hom (and the tensor connection in (ii)).
- `BdRPlusLocalSystem.gr0` (projection): gr⁰M = M/Fil¹B_dR^+·M, a locally free Ô_X-module of the same rank.
- `BdRPlusLocalSystem.pullback` (functoriality): Pullback along morphisms of smooth adic spaces over k.

**Unit tests.**

- `BdRPlusLocalSystem.trivial` (degenerate): B_dR^+ is a B_dR^+-local system of rank 1 with associated OB_dR^+-module (OB_dR^+, ∇).
- `BdRPlusLocalSystem.ofLisse_tate` (computation): Ẑ_p(1) ⊗ B_dR^+ ≅ Fil¹B_dR^+ = t·B_dR^+ as B_dR^+-modules, via ε ⊗ b ↦ tb (locally, t a nonzerodivisor).
- `BdRPlusLocalSystem.gr0_rank` (characterisation): gr⁰(L ⊗ B_dR^+) = L ⊗ Ô_X is locally free over Ô_X of rank rk L.
- `BdRPlusLocalSystem.ohat_non_example` (non-example): Ô_X with B_dR^+ acting through θ is not a B_dR^+-local system (it is killed by the nonzero ideal Fil¹B_dR^+).

**Uses.** Scholze, Theorems 7.2 and 7.6: equivalence with OB_dR^+-modules with connection; association with filtered modules. Scholze, Definition 8.3 and Theorems 8.4, 8.8: M = L ⊗ B_dR^+ and its cohomology. HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T1: R¹f_*Ẑ_p ⊗ B_dR^+ for abelian families. HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T6:comparison: logarithmic Riemann–Hilbert extends the equivalence. CohomologyComparisons CP.3: the B_dR^+-lattice H^i(X_C, L ⊗ B_dR^+) compared with H^i_crys(X/B_dR^+).

**Checks.** M = B_dR^+ and ℳ = OB_dR^+ with ∇. Ô_X, viewed as a B_dR^+-module through θ, is killed by Fil¹ and is not a B_dR^+-local system.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/period-sheaves-definitions`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-period-sheaves-definitions), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/corrected-structural-de-rham-sheaf`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-corrected-structural-de-rham-sheaf), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/structural-de-rham-sheaf-connection`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-structural-de-rham-sheaf-connection).

**Sources.** [Peter Scholze — p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties](https://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/scholze/pAdicHodgeTheory.pdf), Section 7, Definition 7.1, pp. 41-42. Definition (i); (ii) defines OB+dR-modules with integrable connection in the same way.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-bdr-plus-local-systems-and-integrable-connections"></a>

### B_dR^+-local systems are equivalent to OB_dR^+-modules with integrable connection

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/bdr-plus-local-systems-and-integrable-connections` (theorem).

Let X smooth over Spa(k, O_k), k a complete discretely valued extension of Q_p with perfect residue field κ. The functor M ↦ (ℳ, ∇_ℳ) = (M ⊗_{B_dR^+} OB_dR^+, id ⊗ ∇) is an equivalence between the category of B_dR^+-local systems and the category of OB_dR^+-modules with integrable connection, with quasi-inverse ℳ ↦ ℳ^{∇_ℳ = 0}.

**Hypotheses and scope.** X smooth over Spa(k, O_k), k a complete discretely valued extension of Q_p with perfect residue field κ.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (M ⊗ OB_dR^+)^{∇=0} = M ⊗ (OB_dR^+)^{∇=0} = M by the Poincaré lemma in degree 0 (M locally free).
2. Essential surjectivity: every ℳ has enough horizontal sections; this is local, so assume X étale over Tⁿ and work over X̃_K where OB_dR^+ = B_dR^+[[X_1, …, X_n]] with ∇ = Σ ∂/∂X_i ⊗ dT_i (nodes local-structure-of-structural-de-rham-sheaf, connection-and-filtration-in-local-coordinates).
3. Over a Q-algebra B, a finite free B[[X]]-module with integrable connection has a basis of horizontal sections (the formal Taylor series e ↦ Σ_m (−X)^m/m!·∇_∂^m(e) converges X-adically and is horizontal)

**Checks.** For M = B_dR^+: ℳ = OB_dR^+ and ℳ^{∇=0} = B_dR^+. For dim X = 0 both categories are finite free B_dR^+-modules and the functor is the identity.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/bdr-plus-local-system`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-bdr-plus-local-system), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/poincare-lemma-and-faltings-extension`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-poincare-lemma-and-faltings-extension), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/local-structure-of-structural-de-rham-sheaf`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-local-structure-of-structural-de-rham-sheaf), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/structural-de-rham-sheaf-connection`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-structural-de-rham-sheaf-connection), `mathlib:MvPowerSeries.pderiv`, `mathlib:PowerSeries.derivative`, `mathlib:MvPowerSeries`.

**Proof ingredients.** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/connection-and-filtration-in-local-coordinates`, `PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/formal-poincare-lemma`; their statements and locators appear in the proof-ingredient index.

**Sources.** [Peter Scholze — p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties](https://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/scholze/pAdicHodgeTheory.pdf), Section 7, Theorem 7.2 with proof, p. 42. The statement; the proof reduces to Proposition 6.10 and power series over Q-algebras.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-filtered-module-with-integrable-connection"></a>

### Filtered O_X-modules with integrable connection, and association with OB_dR^+-modules

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/filtered-module-with-integrable-connection` (definition).

Let X smooth over Spa(k, O_k), k a complete discretely valued extension of Q_p with perfect residue field κ. A filtered O_X-module with integrable connection is a locally free O_X-module E of finite rank on X (equivalently on X_an, X_ét or X_proét by the previous node) with a separated exhaustive decreasing filtration Fil^i E (i ∈ Z) by local direct summands and an integrable connection ∇: E → E ⊗ Ω¹_X satisfying Griffiths transversality ∇(Fil^i E) ⊂ Fil^{i−1}E ⊗ Ω¹_X. Its de Rham complex DR(E) = (E → E ⊗ Ω¹ → …) is filtered by Fil^m DR(E) = (Fil^m E → Fil^{m−1}E ⊗ Ω¹ → …). An OB_dR^+-module with integrable connection ℳ and such an E are associated if there is an isomorphism ℳ ⊗_{OB_dR^+} OB_dR ≅ E ⊗_{O_X} OB_dR of sheaves on X_proét compatible with filtrations (Fil on E ⊗ OB_dR is the tensor filtration) and connections.

**Hypotheses and scope.** X smooth over Spa(k, O_k), k a complete discretely valued extension of Q_p with perfect residue field κ.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Definitions. Tensor products and duals of filtered modules with integrable connection carry the tensor filtration and tensor connection, which again satisfy Griffiths transversality.

**API.**

- `FilteredConnection` (data): A locally free O_X-module E with a separated exhaustive filtration by local direct summands and an integrable Griffiths-transversal connection.
- `FilteredConnection.deRham` (constructor): The filtered de Rham complex DR(E) with Fil^m DR(E) = (Fil^m E → Fil^{m−1}E ⊗ Ω¹ → …).
- `FilteredConnection.tensor` (structure): Tensor product and dual with tensor filtration and connection.
- `FilteredConnection.shift` (other): The shift E[n] with Fil^i E[n] = Fil^{i+n}E.
- `FilteredConnection.Associated` (other): The relation 'ℳ and E are associated': ℳ ⊗ OB_dR ≅ E ⊗ OB_dR compatibly with Fil and ∇.
- `FilteredConnection.pullback` (functoriality): Pullback along morphisms of smooth adic spaces, compatible with DR and with association.

**Unit tests.**

- `FilteredConnection.trivial` (degenerate): (O_X, d, Fil⁰ = O_X ⊃ Fil¹ = 0) is a filtered module with integrable connection with DR(E) = Ω^•_X.
- `FilteredConnection.twist` (computation): (O_X, d) with Fil^{−1} = O_X ⊃ Fil⁰ = 0 (jump at −1) is associated to Fil¹B_dR^+ ⊗ OB_dR^+ = t·OB_dR^+ (the B_dR^+-local system of Ẑ_p(1)).
- `FilteredConnection.dR_graded` (characterisation): gr^j DR(E) = (gr^j E → gr^{j−1}E ⊗ Ω¹ → …) with O_X-linear differentials; for E trivial, gr^j DR(O_X) = Ω^j_X[−j].
- `FilteredConnection.griffiths_non_example` (non-example): On T¹, E = O e_1 ⊕ O e_2 with ∇e_1 = e_2 ⊗ dT/T, ∇e_2 = 0, Fil⁰ = E, Fil¹ = Fil² = O e_1, Fil³ = 0 is not a filtered module with integrable connection: ∇(Fil²) ⊄ Fil¹ ⊗ Ω¹.
- `FilteredConnection.nonminuscule` (non-example): On a smooth disk with coordinate x and trivial connection on O^2, put Fil^1=Fil^2=O·(e_1+x e_2), Fil^0=O^2, Fil^3=0. Then ∇(e_1+x e_2)=e_2 dx is not in Fil^1⊗Ω^1, so Griffiths transversality fails at i=2. This filtered bundle is excluded from the associated de Rham-local-system construction.

**Uses.** Scholze, Theorems 7.6, 7.11, 8.4, 8.8: the de Rham side of the comparison theorems. HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T1: H¹_dR of abelian families with Gauss–Manin connection and Hodge filtration. Tan–Tong, Definition 3.10: the crystalline analogue with filtered F-isocrystals.

**Checks.** (O_X, d) with Fil⁰ = O_X, Fil¹ = 0 is associated to OB_dR^+ (M = B_dR^+). For a proper smooth family f: A → S, (H¹_dR(A/S), ∇_GM, Fil) is a filtered O_S-module with integrable connection (Griffiths transversality of Gauss–Manin).

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/proetale-structure-sheaves-and-valuations`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-proetale-structure-sheaves-and-valuations), `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3`, [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/bdr-plus-local-system`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-bdr-plus-local-system), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/structural-de-rham-sheaf`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-structural-de-rham-sheaf), `AdicEtaleGeometry:A2`.

**Proof ingredients.** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/vector-bundles-on-analytic-etale-and-proetale-sites`; their statements and locators appear in the proof-ingredient index.

**Sources.** [Peter Scholze — p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties](https://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/scholze/pAdicHodgeTheory.pdf), Section 7, Definitions 7.4-7.5, p. 42. Definition 7.4; Definition 7.5 defines 'associated'. [Peter Scholze — p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.3463v2), Introduction following Theorem 1.5, p.3. The obstruction to the proposed non-minuscule period-domain local system is Griffiths transversality; the disk example makes this obstruction explicit.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-associated-bdr-plus-local-system"></a>

### The B_dR^+-local system M(E) = Fil⁰(E ⊗ OB_dR)^{∇=0} associated to a filtered module with connection

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/associated-bdr-plus-local-system` (construction).

Let X smooth over Spa(k, O_k), k a complete discretely valued extension of Q_p with perfect residue field κ. (i) If ℳ is an OB_dR^+-module with integrable connection with horizontal sections M, associated to a filtered O_X-module with integrable connection E, then M = Fil⁰(E ⊗_{O_X} OB_dR)^{∇=0} and E_ét ≅ ν_*(M ⊗_{B_dR^+} OB_dR) with its filtration and connection. (ii) For every filtered O_X-module with integrable connection E, M(E) := Fil⁰(E ⊗_{O_X} OB_dR)^{∇=0} is a B_dR^+-local system and E is associated to M(E) ⊗_{B_dR^+} OB_dR^+. Hence E ↦ M(E) is a fully faithful functor from filtered O_X-modules with integrable connection to B_dR^+-local systems.

**Hypotheses and scope.** X smooth over Spa(k, O_k), k a complete discretely valued extension of Q_p with perfect residue field κ.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (i): M = Fil⁰(M ⊗ B_dR) = Fil⁰(ℳ ⊗ OB_dR)^{∇=0} = Fil⁰(E ⊗ OB_dR)^{∇=0} (Theorem 7.2 and the Poincaré lemma); E_ét = ν_*(E ⊗ OB_dR) = ν_*(M ⊗ OB_dR) by ν_*OB_dR = O_{X_ét}; the filtration and connection are recovered.
2. (ii): first M_0 := (E ⊗ OB_dR^+)^{∇=0}, a B_dR^+-local system with E ⊗ OB_dR^+ ≅ M_0 ⊗ OB_dR^+ (Theorem 7.2, ignoring Fil). Induct on m − n where Fil^n E = E, Fil^{m+1}E = 0: if n = m take M = Fil^{−n}(M_0 ⊗ B_dR); otherwise twist to m = 0, let Fil' drop the last step, get M' by induction, and consider the 3 × (d + 1) diagram of Lemma 7.7 whose columns are M' ⊗ (0 → B_dR^+ → Fil⁰OB_dR → Fil^{−1}OB_dR ⊗ Ω¹ → …), the middle column, and Fil⁰E ⊗ gr⁰ of the Poincaré sequence.
3. (Lemma 7.7) rows and columns are complexes and commute; all rows but the first are exact; the outer columns are exact (Poincaré lemma, strict); so the whole diagram is exact and M := kernel of the first ∇ in the middle column sits in 0 → M' → M → Fil⁰E ⊗ Ô_X → 0; tensoring with Fil⁰OB_dR (flat over B_dR^+) and the five lemma give M ⊗ Fil⁰OB_dR ≅ Fil⁰(E ⊗ OB_dR), so M is locally free and associated.
4. Full faithfulness: by (i), E is recovered from M(E).

**API.**

- `associatedLocalSystem` (constructor): E ↦ M(E) = Fil⁰(E ⊗_{O_X} OB_dR)^{∇=0}, a B_dR^+-local system with E associated to M(E) ⊗ OB_dR^+.
- `associatedLocalSystem.recover` (characterisation): E_ét ≅ ν_*(M(E) ⊗_{B_dR^+} OB_dR) as filtered O_{X_ét}-modules with connection.
- `associatedLocalSystem.fullyFaithful` (characterisation): Hom(E, E') ≅ Hom(M(E), M(E')) for filtered modules with integrable connection E, E'.
- `associatedLocalSystem.map` (functoriality): Functoriality in E and compatibility with pullback along morphisms of smooth adic spaces.
- `associatedLocalSystem.shift` (compatibility): M(E[1]) = Fil¹B_dR·M(E) = t·M(E) inside M(E) ⊗ B_dR.

**Unit tests.**

- `associatedLocalSystem.trivial_filtration` (computation): For E = (O_X, d, Fil⁰ = O_X, Fil¹ = 0), M(E) = Fil⁰B_dR = B_dR^+.
- `associatedLocalSystem.tate` (computation): For E = (O_X, d) with filtration jump at −1, M(E) = Fil¹B_dR = t·B_dR^+ ≅ Ẑ_p(1) ⊗ B_dR^+.
- `associatedLocalSystem.shift_test` (compatibility): M(E[1]) = t·M(E) for every E.
- `associatedLocalSystem.filtration_matters` (non-example): The trivial and the shifted filtration on (O_X, d) give different B_dR^+-lattices B_dR^+ ≠ t·B_dR^+ in B_dR: M(E) depends on Fil, not only on (E, ∇).

**Uses.** Scholze, Definition 8.3: L is de Rham iff L ⊗ B_dR^+ ≅ M(E) for some E. Scholze, Theorems 7.11, 8.4 and 8.8: cohomology of M(E) versus de Rham cohomology of E. HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T1: the B_dR^+-lattice of H¹ of abelian families is M(H¹_dR). HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T6:comparison: the canonical local systems and their filtered de Rham bundles are compared through the logarithmic analogue.

**Checks.** E = (O_X, d, trivial filtration) gives M = B_dR^+; E with its filtration shifted by one (Fil^i E[1] = Fil^{i+1}E) gives M(E[1]) = t·M(E). The functor is not essentially surjective onto B_dR^+-local systems in general (it is fully faithful); de Rham lisse sheaves are those whose L ⊗ B_dR^+ is in the essential image.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/filtered-module-with-integrable-connection`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-filtered-module-with-integrable-connection), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/bdr-plus-local-systems-and-integrable-connections`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-bdr-plus-local-systems-and-integrable-connections), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/poincare-lemma-and-faltings-extension`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-poincare-lemma-and-faltings-extension), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/pushforward-of-structural-de-rham-sheaf`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-pushforward-of-structural-de-rham-sheaf), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/structural-de-rham-sheaf`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-structural-de-rham-sheaf).

**Sources.** [Peter Scholze — p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties](https://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/scholze/pAdicHodgeTheory.pdf), Section 7, Theorem 7.6 and Lemma 7.7 with proofs, pp. 42-44. The construction and full faithfulness.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-position-of-associated-local-system"></a>

### M(E) ⊂ M_0 ⊗ B_dR is the unique lattice with graded pieces Fil^{−i}E ⊗ Ô_X(i)

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/position-of-associated-local-system` (theorem).

Let X smooth over Spa(k, O_k), k a complete discretely valued extension of Q_p with perfect residue field κ, (E, ∇, Fil) a filtered O_X-module with integrable connection, M_0 the B_dR^+-local system of (E, ∇) with trivial filtration, and M = M(E). Then M ⊂ M_0 ⊗_{B_dR^+} B_dR and (M ∩ Fil^i M_0)/(M ∩ Fil^{i+1}M_0) = Fil^{−i}E ⊗_{O_X} Ô_X(i) ⊂ gr^i M_0 ≅ E ⊗ Ô_X(i) for all i ∈ Z; conversely M is the unique B_dR^+-submodule of M_0 ⊗ B_dR with this property. The uniqueness rests on: Ext¹(Fil⁰E, M_0') ↪ Hom(Fil⁰E, Fil^{−1}E ⊗ Ω¹_X) and Ext¹(Fil⁰E, Fil¹M_0) ↪ Hom(Fil⁰E, E ⊗ Ω¹_X) (Ext in abelian sheaves on X_proét), which in turn rest on Ext¹(F_1, F_2 ⊗ Ô_X(k)) = Hom(F_1, F_2 ⊗ Ω¹_X) for k = 1 and 0 for k ≥ 2 (F_1, F_2 locally free O_X-modules).

**Hypotheses and scope.** X smooth over Spa(k, O_k), k a complete discretely valued extension of Q_p with perfect residue field κ.

**Construction or proof.**

1. The containment and the graded pieces follow from the construction of M (induction on the filtration length, node associated-bdr-plus-local-system).
2. R Hom(ν^*F_1, F_2 ⊗ Ô_X(k)) = R Hom(F_1,ét, Rν_*(F_2 ⊗ Ô_X(k))); by node pushforward-of-structural-de-rham-sheaf, Rν_* vanishes in degrees 0, 1 for k ≥ 2 and in degree 0 for k = 1, with R¹ν_* = F_2 ⊗ Ω¹ for k = 1: this gives the Ext computation, and the two injections follow since M_0' and Fil¹M_0 are successive extensions of F ⊗ Ô_X(k), k ≥ 1.
3. Uniqueness: the sheaf N in the pull-back diagram along Fil⁰E → E ⊗ Ô_X is determined by its extension class, which by the injections is determined by its image in Hom(…, Ω¹) (Griffiths transversality governs existence).

**Checks.** For E with Fil⁰ = E, Fil¹ = 0: M = M_0. For the jump at −1: M = t·M_0, with graded piece Fil¹… = E ⊗ Ô_X(1) in degree 1.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/associated-bdr-plus-local-system`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-associated-bdr-plus-local-system), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/faltings-extension`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-faltings-extension), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/pushforward-of-structural-de-rham-sheaf`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-pushforward-of-structural-de-rham-sheaf), `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0`.

**Proof ingredients.** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/boundary-map-of-associated-local-system`; their statements and locators appear in the proof-ingredient index.

**Sources.** [Peter Scholze — p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties](https://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/scholze/pAdicHodgeTheory.pdf), Section 7, Proposition 7.9 and Lemma 7.10 with proofs, pp. 45-46. The uniqueness statement; Lemma 7.10 supplies the Ext injections.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-proper-smooth-bdr-local-system-comparison"></a>

### de Rham comparison for B_dR^+-local systems from filtered modules on proper smooth X

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/proper-smooth-bdr-local-system-comparison` (theorem).

Let X be proper smooth over Spa(k, O_k), (E, ∇, Fil) a filtered O_X-module with integrable connection with associated B_dR^+-local system M = M(E), k̄ an algebraic closure with completion Ĉ and B_dR = B_dR(Ĉ) Fontaine's field. Then there is a canonical Gal(k̄/k)-equivariant isomorphism H^i(X_k̄, M) ⊗_{B_dR^+} B_dR ≅ H^i_dR(X, E) ⊗_k B_dR compatible with filtrations, and a Gal(k̄/k)-equivariant isomorphism H^i(X_k̄, gr⁰M) ≅ ⊕_j H^{i−j,j}_Hodge(X, E) ⊗_k Ĉ(−j), where H^{i−j,j}_Hodge(X, E) = H^i(X, gr^j DR(E)).

**Hypotheses and scope.** X proper smooth over k; cohomology of M on X_proét/X_k̄; the de Rham and Hodge cohomology may be computed on X_an, X_ét or X_proét (Lemma 7.3).

**Construction or proof.**

1. M ⊗ B_dR is quasi-isomorphic to the filtered complex DR(E) ⊗_{O_X} OB_dR (Poincaré lemma tensored with E; association).
2. The natural map of filtered complexes DR(E) → DR(E) ⊗ OB_dR induces RΓ(X_k̄, DR(E)) ⊗_{k̄} B_dR → RΓ(X_k̄, DR(E) ⊗ OB_dR) in the filtered derived category.
3. It is a filtered quasi-isomorphism: check on gradeds and, using the naive filtration of DR(E), reduce to node coherent-cohomology-against-graded-structural-sheaf for A = gr^j E ⊗ Ω^m.
4. Hodge–Tate: the i-th cohomology of gr⁰(DR(E) ⊗ OB_dR) is ⊕_j H^i(X_k̄, gr^j DR(E)) ⊗ gr^{−j}B_dR = ⊕_j H^{i−j,j}_Hodge(X, E) ⊗ Ĉ(−j).

**Checks.** For E = (O_X, d, trivial filtration) and X a smooth proper curve of genus g: H¹(X_k̄, gr⁰M) ≅ H¹(X, O) ⊗ Ĉ ⊕ H⁰(X, Ω¹) ⊗ Ĉ(−1), of dimensions g and g; with HT(χ) = +1 the Ĉ(−1)-summand has Hodge–Tate weight −1. For X = Spa(k, O_k) (dimension 0): H⁰(M) ⊗ B_dR = E ⊗_k B_dR with the tensor filtration.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/associated-bdr-plus-local-system`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-associated-bdr-plus-local-system), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/cohomology-of-graded-structural-de-rham-sheaf-over-cyclotomic-base`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-cohomology-of-graded-structural-de-rham-sheaf-over-cyclotomic-base), `AdicEtaleGeometry:A2`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3`, [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/proetale-structure-sheaves-and-valuations`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-proetale-structure-sheaves-and-valuations), `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1`, [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/poincare-lemma-and-faltings-extension`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-poincare-lemma-and-faltings-extension), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/de-rham-period-sheaf`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-de-rham-period-sheaf), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/de-rham-period-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-de-rham-period-ring), `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0`.

**Proof ingredients.** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/coherent-cohomology-against-graded-structural-sheaf`, `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/vector-bundles-on-analytic-etale-and-proetale-sites`; their statements and locators appear in the proof-ingredient index.

**Sources.** [Peter Scholze — p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties](https://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/scholze/pAdicHodgeTheory.pdf), Section 7, Theorem 7.11 with proof, pp. 46-47. The statement; the Hodge–Tate part follows in the source.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-lisse-zp-sheaf"></a>

### Lisse Z_p-sheaves on X_ét and lisse Ẑ_p-sheaves on X_proét

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/lisse-zp-sheaf` (definition).

Let X be a locally noetherian adic space over Spa(Q_p, Z_p). A lisse Z_p-sheaf on X_ét is an inverse system L_• = (L_n) of sheaves of Z/p^n-modules, each locally on X_ét constant with finitely generated fibres, isomorphic in the pro-category to a system with L_{n+1}/p^n ≅ L_n. With Ẑ_p := lim Z/p^n on X_proét, a lisse Ẑ_p-sheaf is a sheaf of Ẑ_p-modules L on X_proét locally isomorphic to Ẑ_p ⊗_{Z_p} M for a finitely generated Z_p-module M. The functor L_• ↦ L̂_• := lim ν^*L_n sends lisse Z_p-sheaves to lisse Ẑ_p-sheaves; Q̂_p := Ẑ_p[1/p] and L ⊗ Q̂_p is the associated Q̂_p-local system.

**Hypotheses and scope.** X locally noetherian over Spa(Q_p, Z_p); X_proét and ν from A1.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Definitions; lim is taken in sheaves on X_proét.

**API.**

- `LisseZpSheaf` (data): A sheaf of Ẑ_p-modules on X_proét locally isomorphic to Ẑ_p ⊗ M with M finitely generated over Z_p.
- `LisseZpSheaf.ofEtale` (constructor): L_• ↦ lim ν^*L_n from lisse Z_p-sheaves on X_ét.
- `LisseZpSheaf.tensor` (structure): Tensor product and dual of lisse Ẑ_p-sheaves.
- `LisseZpSheaf.rational` (other): L ⊗_{Ẑ_p} Q̂_p, the associated Q̂_p-local system.
- `LisseZpSheaf.tate` (constructor): Ẑ_p(n) = Ẑ_p(1)^{⊗n}, Ẑ_p(1) = lim μ_{p^n}.
- `LisseZpSheaf.pullback` (functoriality): Pullback along morphisms of locally noetherian adic spaces, compatible with ofEtale.

**Unit tests.**

- `LisseZpSheaf.constant` (degenerate): Ẑ_p = lim ν^*Z/p^n is a lisse Ẑ_p-sheaf of rank 1.
- `LisseZpSheaf.tate_test` (computation): Ẑ_p(1) is lisse of rank 1 and becomes isomorphic to Ẑ_p over X_proét/X_K for K the completion of Q_p(μ_{p^∞}) (choice of ε).
- `LisseZpSheaf.sections_profinite` (characterisation): For U affinoid perfectoid and S profinite, Ẑ_p(U × S) = Hom_cont(S, Z_p) when |U| is connected.
- `LisseZpSheaf.naive_non_example` (non-example): The pullback ν^*Z_p of the constant étale sheaf Z_p is not Ẑ_p: on U × Z_p its sections are the locally constant maps Z_p → Z_p, which exclude the identity map, a section of Ẑ_p.

**Uses.** Scholze, Proposition 8.2 and Theorems 8.4, 8.8: the coefficients of the comparison theorems. HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T1: R¹f_*Ẑ_p of an abelian family (the dual Tate module local system). Tan–Tong, §3.2: crystalline lisse Ẑ_p-sheaves.

**Checks.** Ẑ_p = lim ν^*(Z/p^n) is itself lisse. Ẑ_p(1) = lim μ_{p^n}.

**Prerequisites.** `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1`, [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/proetale-structure-sheaves-and-valuations`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-proetale-structure-sheaves-and-valuations).

**Sources.** [Peter Scholze — p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties](https://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/scholze/pAdicHodgeTheory.pdf), Section 8, Definition 8.1, p. 48. The definition of lisse Ẑ_p-sheaves; lisse Z_p-sheaves on X_ét are defined just before.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-lisse-sheaves-etale-proetale-equivalence"></a>

### Lisse Z_p-sheaves on X_ét are equivalent to lisse Ẑ_p-sheaves on X_proét, with R^j lim ν^*L_n = 0

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/lisse-sheaves-etale-proetale-equivalence` (theorem).

Let X be a locally noetherian adic space over Spa(Q_p, Z_p) and L_• a lisse Z_p-sheaf on X_ét. Then L̂_• = lim ν^*L_n is a lisse Ẑ_p-sheaf on X_proét, R^j lim ν^*L_n = 0 for j > 0, and L_• ↦ L̂_• is an equivalence of categories. For a proper smooth f: X → Y with R^if_ét* L_• lisse, (R^if_ét* L_•)^ = R^if_proét* L̂_•.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Theorem 4.9 (node affinoid-k-pi-one-for-p-torsion); Lemma 3.18 (exact version, supplied by PerfectoidSpaces P6); Corollary 3.17 (ii) (A1).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Basis B: objects U = lim U_i with U_0 affinoid connected and U → U_0 a universal pro-finite-étale cover; on U, each L_n is constant and H^j(U, ν^*L_n) = colim H^j(U_i, L_n) = 0 for j > 0 by Theorem 4.9 (Lemma 3.16 for the colimit, A1); R¹lim L_n(U) = 0 since the transition maps are surjective.
2. Lemma 3.18 gives R^j lim ν^*L_n = 0 and (lim ν^*L_n)(U) = lim L_n(U) = Ẑ_p ⊗ M on B: L̂ is lisse.
3. Equivalence: the functor is fully faithful by Corollary 3.17 (i) at each finite level; essential surjectivity by reducing a lisse Ẑ_p-sheaf modulo p^n (a locally constant sheaf on X_proét with finite fibres descends to X_ét).
4. Pushforward: R^j lim vanishing and Corollary 3.17 (ii).

**Checks.** Check the equivalence at every finite coefficient level and prove the inverse-limit higher-image vanishing, so that the completed local system has no additional derived-limit terms.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/lisse-zp-sheaf`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-lisse-zp-sheaf), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/affinoid-k-pi-one-for-p-torsion`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-affinoid-k-pi-one-for-p-torsion), `PerfectoidSpaces:P6`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1`.

**Sources.** [Peter Scholze — p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties](https://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/scholze/pAdicHodgeTheory.pdf), Section 8, Proposition 8.2, p. 48. The statement, introduced by 'Using Theorem 4.9 and Lemma 3.18, one immediately verifies'.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-de-rham-lisse-sheaf"></a>

### De Rham lisse Ẑ_p-sheaves

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/de-rham-lisse-sheaf` (definition).

Let X smooth over Spa(k, O_k), k a complete discretely valued extension of Q_p with perfect residue field κ. A lisse Ẑ_p-sheaf L on X_proét is de Rham if its B_dR^+-local system M = L ⊗_{Ẑ_p} B_dR^+ is isomorphic to M(E) for some filtered O_X-module with integrable connection (E, ∇, Fil) (node associated-bdr-plus-local-system); E is then unique up to unique isomorphism (full faithfulness) and is called the filtered module associated to L. Scholze states the definition for proper smooth X; it is used for smooth X in Theorem 8.8.

**Hypotheses and scope.** X smooth over Spa(k, O_k), k a complete discretely valued extension of Q_p with perfect residue field κ.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Definition; uniqueness of E from full faithfulness of E ↦ M(E).

**API.**

- `LisseZpSheaf.IsDeRham` (other): The property that L ⊗ B_dR^+ ≅ M(E) for some filtered O_X-module with integrable connection E.
- `LisseZpSheaf.IsDeRham.associated` (data): The associated filtered module with integrable connection E, unique up to unique isomorphism.
- `LisseZpSheaf.IsDeRham.tensor` (structure): De Rham sheaves are stable under ⊗ and duals, with associated E ⊗ E' and E^∨ (node tensor-compatibility-of-associated-local-systems).
- `LisseZpSheaf.IsDeRham.point` (compatibility): For X = Spa(k, O_k): L is de Rham iff L ⊗ Q_p is a de Rham G_k-representation (R06.2), with E = D_dR.
- `LisseZpSheaf.IsDeRham.pullback` (functoriality): Stable under pullback, with E pulled back.

**Unit tests.**

- `LisseZpSheaf.IsDeRham.constant` (degenerate): Ẑ_p is de Rham with associated (O_X, d, Fil⁰ = O_X, Fil¹ = 0).
- `LisseZpSheaf.IsDeRham.tate` (computation): Ẑ_p(n) is de Rham with associated (O_X, d) and filtration jump at −n; for X = Spa(k), D_dR(Q_p(n)) has its unique jump in degree −n (consumer MordellLawrenceVenkatesh LV.1).
- `LisseZpSheaf.IsDeRham.point_compat` (compatibility): For X = Spa(k, O_k), IsDeRham(L) iff dim_k D_dR(L ⊗ Q_p) = rank L (R06.2/admissible-representations).
- `LisseZpSheaf.IsDeRham.non_example` (non-example): For p odd and s ∈ Z_p \ Z, the character χ^s: G_{Q_p} → 1 + pZ_p (through the projection of χ to 1 + pZ_p) gives a lisse sheaf on Spa(Q_p, Z_p) which is not de Rham: it is not even Hodge–Tate, since C(χ^s)^{G} = 0 and C(χ^s)(j)^G = 0 for all j ∈ Z (Brinon–Conrad Theorem 2.2.7).

**Uses.** Scholze, Theorems 8.4 and 8.8: hypothesis and conclusion of the comparison theorems. HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T1: R¹f_*Ẑ_p of an abelian family is de Rham with associated H¹_dR. PadicHodgeTheory R06.2: de Rham representations of G_k are the case X = Spa(k, O_k).

**Checks.** Ẑ_p is de Rham with E = (O_X, d, trivial filtration). For X = Spa(k, O_k), L de Rham ⇔ the G_k-representation V = L ⊗ Q_p is de Rham in the sense of R06.2 (D_dR(V) = E(k)).

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/associated-bdr-plus-local-system`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-associated-bdr-plus-local-system), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/lisse-zp-sheaf`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-lisse-zp-sheaf), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/bdr-plus-local-system`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-bdr-plus-local-system).

**Sources.** [Peter Scholze — p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties](https://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/scholze/pAdicHodgeTheory.pdf), Section 8, Definition 8.3, p. 48. The definition.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-etale-to-bdr-plus-comparison-for-lisse-sheaves"></a>

### H^i(X_k̄, L) ⊗ B_dR^+ ≅ H^i(X_k̄, L ⊗ B_dR^+) for proper smooth X

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/etale-to-bdr-plus-comparison-for-lisse-sheaves` (theorem).

Let X be proper smooth over Spa(k, O_k), L a lisse Ẑ_p-sheaf on X_proét, M = L ⊗_{Ẑ_p} B_dR^+. Then there is a Gal(k̄/k)-equivariant isomorphism H^i(X_k̄, L) ⊗_{Z_p} B_dR^+ ≅ H^i(X_k̄, M), where B_dR^+ = B_dR^+(Ĉ); in particular H^i(X_k̄, M) is a free B_dR^+-module of finite rank when H^i(X_k̄, L) is torsion free, and in general H^i(X_k̄, M) ⊗ B_dR = H^i(X_k̄, L) ⊗ B_dR.

**Hypotheses and scope.** X is proper smooth over k with perfect residue and L is a lisse Z_p-sheaf. The early primitive comparison of P8 provides finite-coefficient almost comparison and finiteness; the integral A_inf section comparison is its perfectoid inverse-limit input, not an AΩ comparison.

**Construction or proof.**

1. H^i(X_k̄, L_n) ⊗ A_inf^a ≅ H^i(X_k̄, L_n ⊗ A_inf^a) for all n (primitive comparison, owned by P8:local-rational's early cut under RS-01), then pass to lim_n by the almost Lemma 3.18: H^i(X_k̄, L) ⊗ A_inf^a ≅ H^i(X_k̄, L ⊗ A_inf^a).
2. Invert p: almost isomorphism with B_inf.
3. Multiplication by ξ^k: H^i(X_k̄, L) ⊗ B_inf/(ker θ)^k ≅ H^i(X_k̄, L ⊗ B_inf/(ker θ)^k), now a genuine isomorphism since the almost ideal becomes the unit ideal in B_inf/(ker θ)^k ([π] is a unit there).
4. Lemma 3.18 (exact) for the system L ⊗ B_inf/(ker θ)^k gives H^i(X_k̄, L) ⊗ B_dR^+ ≅ H^i(X_k̄, L ⊗ B_dR^+) (finite generation of H^i(X_k̄, L) makes ⊗ commute with lim).

**Checks.** For L = Ẑ_p and X an elliptic curve: H¹(X_k̄, L ⊗ B_dR^+) is free of rank 2 over B_dR^+. For X = Spa(k, O_k): H⁰(X_k̄, L ⊗ B_dR^+) = L_x̄ ⊗ B_dR^+.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/lisse-sheaves-etale-proetale-equivalence`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-lisse-sheaves-etale-proetale-equivalence), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/rational-acyclicity-of-de-rham-period-sheaves`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-rational-acyclicity-of-de-rham-period-sheaves), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/period-sheaves-on-affinoid-perfectoids`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-period-sheaves-on-affinoid-perfectoids), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/bdr-plus-of-perfectoid-affinoid-algebras`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-bdr-plus-of-perfectoid-affinoid-algebras), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/early-primitive-comparison-and-finiteness`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-early-primitive-comparison-and-finiteness), `PerfectoidSpaces:P6`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1`.

**Sources.** [Peter Scholze — p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties](https://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/scholze/pAdicHodgeTheory.pdf), Section 8, Theorem 8.4, p. 48. The first assertion of Theorem 8.4. [Peter Scholze — p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties](https://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/scholze/pAdicHodgeTheory.pdf), Section 8, proof of Theorem 8.4, p. 49. The dependence on the primitive comparison theorem.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-de-rham-comparison-for-de-rham-lisse-sheaves"></a>

### Hodge–de Rham degeneration and H^i(X_k̄, L) ⊗ B_dR ≅ H^i_dR(X, E) ⊗ B_dR for de Rham L

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/de-rham-comparison-for-de-rham-lisse-sheaves` (theorem).

Let X be proper smooth over Spa(k, O_k) and L a de Rham lisse Ẑ_p-sheaf with associated filtered module with integrable connection (E, ∇, Fil). Then the Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence H^{i−j,j}_Hodge(X, E) ⇒ H^i_dR(X, E) degenerates, and there are Gal(k̄/k)-equivariant isomorphisms H^i(X_k̄, L) ⊗_{Z_p} B_dR ≅ H^i_dR(X, E) ⊗_k B_dR preserving filtrations and H^i(X_k̄, L) ⊗_{Z_p} Ĉ ≅ ⊕_j H^{i−j,j}_Hodge(X, E) ⊗_k Ĉ(−j). In particular H^i(X_k̄, L) ⊗ Q_p is a de Rham G_k-representation with D_dR = H^i_dR(X, E) and Hodge filtration; with the convention HT(χ) = +1, H^{i−j,j}_Hodge contributes Hodge–Tate weight −j.

**Hypotheses and scope.** X proper smooth over k; L de Rham with associated E.

**Construction or proof.**

1. By node etale-to-bdr-plus-comparison-for-lisse-sheaves, H^i(X_k̄, M) ⊗ B_dR = H^i(X_k̄, L) ⊗ B_dR and dim_Ĉ H^i(X_k̄, gr⁰M) = dim_{B_dR}(H^i(X_k̄, M) ⊗ B_dR) (H^i(X_k̄, M) ⊗ B_dR^+-free up to torsion of H^i(L)).
2. Theorem 7.11 (node proper-smooth-bdr-local-system-comparison) translates this into Σ_j dim_k H^{i−j,j}_Hodge(X, E) = dim_k H^i_dR(X, E), i.e. degeneration.
3. The filtered isomorphism and the Hodge–Tate decomposition are Theorem 7.11 composed with the previous node.

**Checks.** X a smooth proper curve of genus g over Q_p, L = Ẑ_p: H¹_ét(X_Q̄p, Q_p) ⊗ Ĉ ≅ Ĉ^g ⊕ Ĉ(−1)^g, Hodge–Tate weights 0 and −1 each with multiplicity g (HT(χ) = +1). X = P¹: H²(X_k̄, Z_p) ⊗ B_dR ≅ H²_dR(P¹) ⊗ B_dR with H²_dR in Fil¹, matching H² = Z_p(−1). For K/Q_p finite, a torsion-free cocompact Γ⊂PGL_n(K) acting freely on Drinfeld upper half-space and a finite-dimensional K-representation M with Γ-stable O_K-lattice, the proper smooth quotient has degeneration H^a(X_Γ,Ω^b⊗M_Γ)⇒H^{a+b}_dR(X_Γ,O⊗M_Γ). The connection and filtration are those descended from the trivial filtered coefficient bundle.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/etale-to-bdr-plus-comparison-for-lisse-sheaves`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-etale-to-bdr-plus-comparison-for-lisse-sheaves), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/proper-smooth-bdr-local-system-comparison`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-proper-smooth-bdr-local-system-comparison), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/de-rham-lisse-sheaf`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-de-rham-lisse-sheaf).

**Sources.** [Peter Scholze — p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties](https://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/scholze/pAdicHodgeTheory.pdf), Section 8, Theorem 8.4 and its proof, pp. 48-49. The second half of Theorem 8.4 (degeneration, filtered comparison and Hodge–Tate decomposition). [Peter Scholze — p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.3463v2), Corollary 1.9, p.4. Specializes the filtered comparison to the indicated quotient and a coefficient representation with invariant lattice.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-relative-bdr-plus-local-system-comparison"></a>

### R^if_*(L ⊗ B_dR,X^+) ≅ R^if_*L ⊗ B_dR,Y^+ for proper smooth f

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/relative-bdr-plus-local-system-comparison` (theorem).

Let f: X → Y be a proper smooth morphism of smooth adic spaces over Spa(k, O_k), L a lisse Ẑ_p-sheaf on X_proét with M = L ⊗ B_dR,X^+, and assume R^if_proét* L is a lisse Ẑ_p-sheaf on Y_proét. Then there is a canonical isomorphism R^if_proét* M ≅ R^if_proét* L ⊗_{Ẑ_p} B_dR,Y^+; in particular R^if_proét* M is a B_dR,Y^+-local system associated with R^if_proét* L.

**Hypotheses and scope.** f:X→Y is proper smooth between smooth rigid spaces. L is a lisse Z_p-sheaf. Use the relative primitive comparison of P8 and the associated finite-coefficient almost comparison.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Work on Y_proét/Y_K, K = completion of k̄. From Corollary 5.11 and Corollary 3.17 (ii): (R^if_* L') ⊗ O_Y^{+a}/p ≅ R^if_proét*(L' ⊗ O_X^{+a}/p); with π ∈ O_K♭, π♯ = p, this is (R^if_* L') ⊗ O^{+a}_{Y♭}/π ≅ R^if_*(L' ⊗ O^{+a}_{X♭}/π), and by induction on m, modulo π^m.
2. Hence (R^if_* L_n) ⊗ A_inf,Y^a/[π]^m ≅ R^if_*(L_n ⊗ A_inf,X^a/[π]^m); lisseness of R^if_*L_n and Lemma 3.18 pass to lim_m, then lim_n: R^if_*L ⊗ A_inf,Y^a ≅ R^if_*(L ⊗ A_inf,X^a).
3. Invert p, multiply by ξ^k and pass to B_dR^+ exactly as in node etale-to-bdr-plus-comparison-for-lisse-sheaves.

**Checks.** For Y = Spa(k, O_k): node etale-to-bdr-plus-comparison-for-lisse-sheaves. For an abelian scheme f: A → S and i = 1: R¹f_*M ≅ (T_pA)^∨ ⊗ B_dR,S^+ (node degree-one-abelian-comparison).

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/etale-to-bdr-plus-comparison-for-lisse-sheaves`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-etale-to-bdr-plus-comparison-for-lisse-sheaves), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/lisse-sheaves-etale-proetale-equivalence`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-lisse-sheaves-etale-proetale-equivalence), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/period-sheaves-on-affinoid-perfectoids`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-period-sheaves-on-affinoid-perfectoids), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/early-primitive-comparison-and-finiteness`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-early-primitive-comparison-and-finiteness), `PerfectoidSpaces:P6`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1`.

**Proof ingredients.** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/relative-completed-structure-sheaf-computations`; their statements and locators appear in the proof-ingredient index.

**Sources.** [Peter Scholze — p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties](https://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/scholze/pAdicHodgeTheory.pdf), Section 8, Theorem 8.8 (i) with proof, pp. 51-52. Part (i); the proof starts from Corollary 5.11.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-geometric-hodge-tate-direct-images"></a>

### Geometric Hodge–Tate direct images

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/geometric-hodge-tate-direct-images` (theorem).

For X smooth over a complete algebraically closed extension C/Q_p and ν:X_proet→X_et, R^nν_*Ô_X is canonically Ω_X^n(−n), compatible with exterior cup products and étale pullback. These sheaves are coherent, vanish for n>dim X, and R^0ν_*Ô_X=O_X. This is a geometric statement. Over a discretely valued arithmetic base K the extra log χ row in R^iν_*Ô_X(j) must be retained; the geometric formula does not erase it before base change.

**Hypotheses and scope.** X is smooth; Ω_X is the analytic coherent differential sheaf over C.

**Construction or proof.**

1. On a toric chart compute continuous Z_p^d-cohomology of the perfectoid root tower and identify degree-one Kummer classes with dlog coordinates. Cup products identify higher degrees with exterior powers. Descend across étale chart changes using the intrinsic boundary of the Faltings extension, then sheafify. BMS’s integral Lη calculation agrees after inversion of p.
2. For arbitrary C, use Scholze survey Lemma 3.24: approximate coefficients by smooth finite-type Q_p-algebras, descend finite étale charts to a finite stage, and compare Faltings boundary maps. The boundedness of both maps on integral units and approximation modulo p^m establish Kummer compatibility independently of coordinates. Constants from the auxiliary base admit compatible p-power roots in C, so their boundary classes vanish. Exterior cup products give the higher-degree identifications.

**Checks.** For a one-dimensional torus, R^1ν_*Ô=O·dlog T(−1) and all R^n for n>1 vanish. Over K, the arithmetic log χ contribution provides a test distinguishing the two bases.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/etale-proetale-cohomology-and-base-change`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-etale-proetale-cohomology-and-base-change), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/faltings-extension`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-faltings-extension), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/completed-structure-sheaf-on-affinoid-perfectoids`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-completed-structure-sheaf-on-affinoid-perfectoids), `PerfectoidSpaces:P3`.

**Sources.** [Peter Scholze — p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.3463v2), Proposition 6.16 and its proof, pp.39–41; Corollary 6.19, p.41. Computes toric perfectoid cohomology and the intrinsic degree-one boundary; arithmetic invariants give the additional row. [Bhargav Bhatt; Matthew Morrow; Peter Scholze — Integral p-adic Hodge theory](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.03148v3), Theorem 8.3 and Theorem 8.7, pp.61–63; Proposition 8.9, p.63. Provides the compatible integral toric calculation, whose rationalization is the geometric direct-image formula. [Peter Scholze — Perfectoid spaces: a survey](https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.5948), Proposition 3.23, Lemma 3.24 and proof, pp.21–24. The all-C direct-image formula is proved by toric covers and intrinsic Kummer dlog descent; all exterior powers are included.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-relative-hodge-tate-filtration"></a>

### Relative Hodge–Tate filtration

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/relative-hodge-tate-filtration` (construction).

For a proper smooth π:X→S of smooth adic spaces over a complete discretely valued K with perfect residue, assume every R^iπ_*F_p is locally free. Put H=R^iπ_dR*O_X with Hodge filtration and Gauss–Manin connection, M=R^iπ_*Ẑ_p⊗B_dR,S^+ and M_0=(H⊗O_S OB_dR,S^+)^{∇=0}, where M_0 uses the trivial filtration on H. Relative comparison identifies M[1/t]=M_0[1/t]. In this ambient module M_0⊂M. Define the ascending filtration on M/tM by F_{−j}=(M∩t^jM_0)/(tM∩t^jM_0). Its graded piece gr_F^j(M/tM)=gr_Hodge^jH⊗Ô_S(−j), F_{−1}=0 and F_i=M/tM. Before reduction, (M∩t^jM_0)/(M∩t^{j+1}M_0)=Fil_Hodge^{−j}H⊗Ô_S(j).

**Hypotheses and scope.** π proper smooth; X,S smooth; every finite-coefficient direct image locally free. OB_dR^+ is the corrected completed structural sheaf.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Apply the existing corrected local Poincaré lemma and relative comparison to identify the two lattices in the same B_dR module. Use the lattice-filtration position theorem to compute their intersections. Reduce by tM to obtain an ascending filtration and compute its graded terms from the Hodge filtration.

**API.**

- `RelativeHT.lattices` (data): M and M_0 are lattices in their common B_dR extension, with M_0 contained in M.
- `RelativeHT.step` (constructor): F_{−j} is the image of M∩t^jM_0 in M/tM.
- `RelativeHT.graded` (characterisation): gr_F^j=gr_Hodge^jH⊗Ô_S(−j).
- `RelativeHT.pullback` (functoriality): Under proper smooth and lisse base-change hypotheses, the construction commutes with base change.
- `RelativeHT.tensor` (compatibility): For tensor constructions of associated de Rham pairs use the convolution of their filtrations, not a new geometric direct-image identification.

**Unit tests.**

- `RelativeHT.identity` (degenerate): For π=id and i=0, M=M_0, F_0=Ô_S and F_{−1}=0.
- `RelativeHT.p_one` (computation): For a P^1 family in degree 2, gr_F^1=Ô_S(−1) and the other graded terms vanish.
- `RelativeHT.twist` (compatibility): Tensor by a Tate line shifts the Hodge filtration and the ascending index with the corresponding opposite twist.
- `RelativeHT.lattice_direction` (non-example): For a positive Hodge-jump line the associated lattice contains the trivially filtered lattice; reversing M_0⊂M gives the wrong quotient.

**Uses.** Caraiani–Scholze Corollary 2.2.4 and §2.3: Uses graded relative periods on tensor constructions.. HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T1–T2: Consumes the degree-one filtration as a specialization..

**Checks.** The inclusion direction is M_0⊂M and the graded twist is −j.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/early-relative-primitive-comparison`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-early-relative-primitive-comparison), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/de-rham-pair-derived-pushforward`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-de-rham-pair-derived-pushforward), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/position-of-associated-local-system`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-position-of-associated-local-system), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/corrected-structural-de-rham-sheaf`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-corrected-structural-de-rham-sheaf).

**Sources.** [Ana Caraiani, Peter Scholze — On the generic part of the cohomology of compact unitary Shimura varieties](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1511.02418), Proposition 2.2.3 and Corollary 2.2.4, pp.14–15. Describes the two lattices, their intersections, ascending filtration and graded twists. [Peter Scholze — Erratum to p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties](https://www.math.uni-bonn.de/people/scholze/pAdicHodgeErratum.pdf), correction to Definition 6.8, p.1. Requires integral completion before inversion of p in the structural sheaf.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-relative-hodge-tate-first-step"></a>

### The natural first Hodge–Tate step

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/relative-hodge-tate-first-step` (theorem).

Under the preceding hypotheses, F_0 on R^iπ_*Ẑ_p⊗Ô_S is the image of the natural injective map R^iπ_*O_X⊗Ô_S→R^iπ_*Ô_X≅R^iπ_*Ẑ_p⊗Ô_S. The map is induced by O_X→Ô_X and the primitive comparison; it is not chosen from a splitting of the graded pieces. Associated tensor and dual constructions preserve the filtration by their tensor and dual rules.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Use the fixed relative comparison and corrected OB_dR^+.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Extend M_0→M to structural periods. The relative Poincaré lemma identifies this map with the inclusion O_X→OB_dR,X^+. Reduce the complex modulo Fil^1; it becomes O_X→Ô_X. The lattice-intersection graded formula shows that the image has the expected rank and that the natural map is injective. Tensor compatibility is inherited from the associated filtered flat bundle functor.

**Checks.** For an abelian family, this is the H^1(O) subbundle; the full degree-one specialization belongs to T1.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/relative-hodge-tate-filtration`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-relative-hodge-tate-filtration), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/early-relative-primitive-comparison`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-early-relative-primitive-comparison), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/relative-poincare-lemma`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-relative-poincare-lemma).

**Sources.** [Ana Caraiani, Peter Scholze — On the generic part of the cohomology of compact unitary Shimura varieties](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1511.02418), Proposition 2.2.5 and proof, pp.15–16. Identifies F_0 by the natural structure-sheaf map instead of a splitting.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-associated-de-rham-pairs"></a>

### Associated de Rham pairs

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/associated-de-rham-pairs` (definition).

For X smooth over a finite extension K/Q_p, an associated de Rham pair consists of a finite-rank Q_p-local system L, a filtered vector bundle (E,∇,Fil) with integrable Griffiths-transversal connection, and an isomorphism L⊗OB_dR≅E⊗OB_dR respecting connection and tensor filtration. Equivalently L⊗B_dR^+≅M(E), compatibly after structural extension. Association is data; being de Rham means such data exist. Morphisms respect both components and the isomorphism. Tensor products use convolution filtration; duals use Fil^iE^∨=(Fil^{1−i}E)^⊥. The filtered flat bundle functor M is fully faithful, but its essential image is the associated lattices, not every B_dR^+-local system.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Use the corrected structural period sheaf and finite, locally split, exhaustive separated filtration. A Q_p-local system is allowed to have lattices only locally, as in Shimizu Definition 8.2.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Use the existing M construction and horizontal Poincaré equivalence. Take Fil^0 of the comparison and horizontal sections to obtain the lattice isomorphism. Conversely extend it to OB_dR with the induced filtration and connection. Recover morphisms from horizontal maps and the filtration-position theorem.

**API.**

- `DeRhamPair.comparison` (data): The structural isomorphism respects tensor filtration and the two connections.
- `DeRhamPair.lattice_comparison` (characterisation): Association is equivalent to L⊗B_dR^+≅M(E).
- `DeRhamPair.tensor` (constructor): The tensor comparison is induced from the two given comparisons and convolution filtration.
- `DeRhamPair.dual` (constructor): Dualize the comparison with the orthogonal filtration.
- `DeRhamPair.pullback` (functoriality): Smooth or étale pullback transports the pair and its comparison; preserve the source hypotheses for period base change.
- `DeRhamPair.fully_faithful` (relation): A period-lattice map between M(E) and M(F) uniquely comes from a filtered horizontal bundle map.

**Unit tests.**

- `DeRhamPair.unit` (degenerate): The constant Q_p local system is associated to O_X with d and jump 0.
- `DeRhamPair.tate` (computation): Q_p(1) is associated to a flat line with filtration jump −1, and M(E)=t^{−1}B_dR^+e.
- `DeRhamPair.nontransverse` (non-example): A rank-two flat bundle with Fil^1 a line whose connection has a nonzero quotient component does not qualify when Fil^0 equals that line.
- `DeRhamPair.lattice_independence` (compatibility): Replacing a local Z_p-lattice by p times that lattice gives the same rational pair.

**Uses.** Howe–Klevdal §2.5: Supplies the filtered-flat-bundle input to admissible pairs.. Liu–Zhu and Shimizu: Makes de Rham local systems and their flat bundles available without a second definition..

**Checks.** Changing a Q_p-lattice leaves the rational associated pair unchanged.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/associated-bdr-plus-local-system`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-associated-bdr-plus-local-system), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/filtered-module-with-integrable-connection`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-filtered-module-with-integrable-connection), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/de-rham-lisse-sheaf`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-de-rham-lisse-sheaf), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/position-of-associated-local-system`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-position-of-associated-local-system).

**Sources.** [Peter Scholze — p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.3463v2), Definition 7.4, Theorem 7.6 and Proposition 7.9, pp.42–45; Definition 8.3, pp.48–49. Defines filtered flat bundles, the fully faithful association functor and the de Rham local-system condition. [Sean Howe and Christian Klevdal — Admissible pairs and p-adic Hodge structures II: the bi-analytic Ax-Lindemann theorem](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2308.11064), §2.5, pp.18–19. Restates the functor with Griffiths transversality and distinguishes its source from arbitrary period local systems. [Koji Shimizu — A p-adic monodromy theorem for de Rham local systems](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2003.10951v2), Definitions 8.1–8.2, p.45; §8.3, pp.47–48. Uses rational local systems defined by locally available lattices.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-diamond-period-local-system-equivalence"></a>

### Period local systems on rigid spaces and diamonds

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/diamond-period-local-system-equivalence` (theorem).

For X smooth over a p-adic field K, the category of finite-rank B_dR^+-local systems on X_proet is canonically equivalent to that on the associated locally spatial diamond X^diamond. On an affinoid perfectoid toric cover U=Spa(A,A^+), both categories are finite projective B_dR^+(A)-modules; the equivalence identifies continuous semilinear descent and preserves tensor products, duals, t-inversion and reduction modulo t. It sends M(E) to the same period lattice on the diamond.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Diamond period local systems use the period sheaf on the v-site and the descent convention of Howe–Klevdal §2.3.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Choose toric charts and their cyclotomic root towers. Use finite-projective descent on the perfectoid cover. Compare the same continuous semilinear action of Z_p(1)^n⋊Z_p^×, and then the étale descent between charts. This constructs the equivalence and its tensor compatibility.

**Checks.** A finite projective module need not have a chosen free basis globally.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/associated-de-rham-pairs`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-associated-de-rham-pairs), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/bdr-plus-local-system`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-bdr-plus-local-system), `DiamondsAndVStacks:D3`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D6`.

**Sources.** [Sean Howe and Christian Klevdal — Admissible pairs and p-adic Hodge structures II: the bi-analytic Ax-Lindemann theorem](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2308.11064), §2.5, pp.18–19. Gives the perfectoid-cover and descent-data proof and cites Scholze–Weinstein Corollary 17.1.9. [Peter Scholze; Jared Weinstein — Berkeley lectures on p-adic geometry](https://www.math.uni-bonn.de/people/scholze/Berkeley.pdf), Lemma 17.1.8 and Corollary 17.1.9, pp.150–151. Finite-projective B_dR^+ modules satisfy v-descent, and the category on an affinoid perfectoid is recovered from its period ring.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-horizontal-relative-periods"></a>

### Horizontal relative periods

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/horizontal-relative-periods` (construction).

Let K be finite totally ramified over Frac W(k), k perfect. Let R satisfy Shimizu Set-up 3.1: R is a normal domain finite flat over a p-adically completed toric base obtained by étale extensions, localizations and completions; R[1/p] is étale over that base, K is algebraically closed in R[1/p], its reduced special fiber is geometrically integral, and the stated geometrically regular-fiber or dimension<2 condition holds. Write Rbar for the union of finite normal extensions étale after inverting p and Rhat for its p-adic completion. Evaluate the shared relative period constructions on (Rhat[1/p],Rhat). Define B_max^∇, B_cris^∇ and B_dR^∇ by these evaluations. Define B_st^∇=B_max^∇[u] embedded by u↦log([p^flat]/p), with φ(u)=pu and N=−d/du. For V a continuous Q_p-representation of G_{R[1/p]}, set D_B^∇(V)=(B^∇⊗V)^G and its multiplication comparison. Horizontal crystalline, semistable or de Rham means that comparison is invertible for B_max^∇, B_st^∇ or B_dR^∇. Horizontal crystalline can equivalently use B_cris^∇. The invariant bases are K_0,K_0,K respectively; (B_st^∇)^{N=0}=B_max^∇. Condition (BR) means R equals its smooth toric base and is imposed for the crystalline/semistable dual and monodromy theorems.

**Hypotheses and scope.** A common root system and logarithm embedding is fixed; root changes add an element of B_max^∇ and transport all structures.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Evaluate the shared θ-completion and PD constructions; the max construction adjoins ker θ/p before p-adic completion. Use the logarithm transcendence theorem to identify the semistable ring with a polynomial algebra over B_max, rather than over B_cris. Apply invariant and injectivity theorems to prove the dimension criterion.

**API.**

- `HorizontalPeriods.base` (characterisation): Invariant bases are K_0 for max, crystalline and semistable periods, and K for de Rham periods.
- `HorizontalPeriods.monodromy` (relation): Nφ=pφN and ker N=B_max^∇.
- `HorizontalPeriods.crystalline` (equivalence): The B_max comparison is invertible exactly when the B_cris comparison is invertible.
- `HorizontalPeriods.dimension` (characterisation): For each period ring, injectivity makes admissibility equivalent to the corresponding full rank.
- `HorizontalPeriods.base_change` (compatibility): Admissible periods commute with the base-ring maps and finite field extensions of Shimizu §4.3.
- `HorizontalPeriods.tensor_dual` (compatibility): Tensor and subquotient rules hold; impose BR for the crystalline and semistable dual rules.

**Unit tests.**

- `HorizontalPeriods.constant` (degenerate): For V=Q_p, D_st^∇=K_0,N=0 and D_dR^∇=K.
- `HorizontalPeriods.logarithm` (computation): N(u)=−1 and Nφ(u)=−p=pφN(u).
- `HorizontalPeriods.kernel` (non-example): N=0 recovers B_max^∇, so a definition demanding ker N=B_cris^∇ is rejected.
- `HorizontalPeriods.arithmetic_point` (compatibility): For R=O_K the admissibility predicates recover the ordinary crystalline, semistable and de Rham predicates.

**Uses.** Shimizu Theorems 7.4–7.5: Supplies the local horizontal monodromy input.. Shimizu Theorem 9.2: Interprets a locally trivialized de Rham flat bundle through an affinoid base..

**Checks.** The structural period ring with connection is not substituted for the horizontal evaluation ring.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/bmax-period-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-bmax-period-ring), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/period-sheaves-definitions`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-period-sheaves-definitions), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/crystalline-period-sheaves`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-crystalline-period-sheaves), `PerfectoidSpaces:P3`.

**Sources.** [Koji Shimizu — A p-adic monodromy theorem for de Rham local systems](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2003.10951v2), Set-up 3.1 and Definition 3.2, pp.18–19; Definitions 2.25–2.38, pp.13–16; Definitions 4.7 and 4.16, Lemmas 4.14–4.19, pp.22–25. Specifies the base rings, horizontal period carriers, comparison definition, max/crystalline equivalence and dual restrictions.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-horizontal-and-local-system-monodromy"></a>

### Local monodromy for de Rham local systems

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/horizontal-and-local-system-monodromy` (theorem).

For R satisfying the preceding set-up and BR, every horizontal de Rham representation becomes horizontal semistable after a finite extension L/K; if one classical specialization is potentially crystalline, L can be chosen to make it horizontal crystalline. Consequently, for a de Rham Q_p-local system on a smooth quasi-separated rigid space X/K and a classical point x, there is an open neighborhood U of x in X_{k(x)} and a finite extension L/k(x) such that the restriction to U_L is horizontal de Rham and semistable at every classical point.
