If its stalk at x is potentially crystalline, all those stalks can be chosen crystalline. For qc X a single finite L/K makes all K-rational stalks semistable. This does not assert that a single model defines a globally semistable local system on all of X.

**Hypotheses and scope.** K complete discretely valued with perfect residue; locally choose an isogeny Z_p-lattice. Semistability of a stalk is over its own residue field.

**Construction or proof.**

1. For the horizontal theorem localize R at the prime (π), complete to a discretely valued field with possibly imperfect residue, and use horizontal monodromy there. The canonical constant field is K. Descend semistability back by the purity theorem, Shimizu Theorem 6.1. The specialization test forces N=0 in the crystalline case. Around a classical point choose a polydisk and shrink it until the flat connection has a full set of solutions, by the convergent Taylor construction of Theorem 9.7. Apply the horizontal theorem. Compactness of the set of K-points gives the qc consequence.

**Checks.** For a non-K-rational point the neighborhood lies after k(x)-base change. The union of these neighborhoods need not contain every nonclassical point of X.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/horizontal-relative-periods`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-horizontal-relative-periods), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/associated-de-rham-pairs`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-associated-de-rham-pairs), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/plan/p-adic-monodromy-theorem`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-3-plan-p-adic-monodromy-theorem).

**Sources.** [Koji Shimizu — A p-adic monodromy theorem for de Rham local systems](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2003.10951v2), Theorems 6.1, 7.4–7.5, pp.34,44–45; Theorem 9.2, Remark 9.3, Corollary 9.4 and Theorem 9.7, pp.49–53. Proves horizontal monodromy by purity and deduces the precise neighborhood and stalk assertions.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-relative-perfect-period-rings"></a>

### Perfect period rings over a perfect uniform algebra

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/relative-perfect-period-rings` (construction).

For a perfect uniform Banach F_p-algebra R with an open integrally closed subring R^+, form W(R), W(R)[1/p] and W(R^+). For x=Σ_i p^i[x_i], use the Witt Gauss norms λ_r(x)=max_i p^{−i}α(x_i)^r. Define the integral radius-r ring by the condition lim_{i→∞}p^{−i}α(x_i)^r=0 on x=Σ_{i≥0}p^i[x_i]; the bounded radius-r ring inverts p with bounded Witt coefficients. Complete bounded rings for max(λ_s,λ_r) to obtain the closed-interval ring R̃_R^{[s,r]}, take the inverse limit over s↓0 for R̃_R^r, and the direct limit over r↓0 for the Robba ring R̃_R. The bounded and integral Robba rings are the corresponding radius unions. For R^+, every integral radius ring is W(R^+), every bounded radius ring is W(R^+)[1/p], and R̃_R^+ is its completion for all λ_s, s>0; this can be smaller than ⋂_{r>0}R̃_R^r. Retain the specified R^+ rather than recovering it from rank-one points. Frobenius sends radius r to r/p and respects the interval maps. At a perfect analytic field these are the existing extended Robba rings, not a second field construction.

**Hypotheses and scope.** α is the power-multiplicative spectral norm; R is complete and perfect, and the specified R^+ is part of the adic algebra. All Witt expansions and all radius completions are the precise ones of KL Definition 5.1.1. R is an adic Banach algebra over a perfect analytic field, as in KL Hypothesis 5.0.1.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Extend the lower-stage field Witt-Gauss construction coefficientwise to R using Witt addition estimates. Prove the norm and completeness assertions, then the restriction maps for nested intervals. Use the rational-cover splitting argument of KL Lemma 5.3.2 to prove the sheaf and acyclicity statements only for the rings actually listed in Theorem 5.3.3. Positive variants have separate sheaf assertions and are not supplied the same acyclicity theorem.

**API.**

- `PerfectPeriods.gauss` (simp): λ_r(Σ p^i[x_i])=max_i p^{−i}α(x_i)^r on convergent Witt expansions.
- `PerfectPeriods.frobenius` (relation): φ transports λ_r to λ_{pr}, giving the stated radius transition.
- `PerfectPeriods.restriction` (functoriality): Nested intervals have continuous restriction maps satisfying identity and composition.
- `PerfectPeriods.field_agreement` (compatibility): For a perfect analytic field the constructions agree with the RD.0 extended Robba ring.
- `PerfectPeriods.rational_sheaf` (structure): Every variant listed in Definition 5.3.1 is a sheaf; ordinary acyclicity is asserted only for the Theorem 5.3.3 list.

**Unit tests.**

- `PerfectPeriods.teichmuller` (computation): λ_r([x])=α(x)^r and λ_r(p)=p^{−1}.
- `PerfectPeriods.frobenius_radius` (compatibility): λ_r(φ([x]))=α(x)^{pr}=λ_{pr}([x]).
- `PerfectPeriods.integral_plus` (non-example): Integral positive Witt sections do not inherit ordinary acyclicity from the nonpositive radius rings.
- `PerfectPeriods.zero` (degenerate): Zero has Gauss norm zero at every radius.

**Uses.** KL Definition 9.3.3: Evaluates every relative perfect period sheaf on a perfectoid subdomain.. KL Theorem 9.3.6: Provides the period rings in which pure and étale loci are tested..

**Checks.** The integral-positive and positive variants are omitted from the ordinary acyclicity list.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:WittVector`, `mathlib:WittVector.frobenius`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/extended-robba-ring`.

**Sources.** [Kiran S. Kedlaya, Ruochuan Liu — Relative p-adic Hodge theory: Foundations](https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.0792v5), Definition 5.1.1 and Lemma 5.1.2, pp.113–114; Definition 5.3.1 and Theorem 5.3.3, pp.121–122. Specifies the relative Witt-Gauss rings, interval and radius limits, and the restricted rational acyclicity list.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-relative-witt-and-robba-period-sheaves"></a>

### Relative Witt and Robba period sheaves

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/relative-witt-and-robba-period-sheaves` (definition).

Let X be a preadic space over Q_{p^d}, d≥1, with the KL pro-étale site. On a perfectoid subdomain Y let R=O(Y^flat) and R^+ its integral ring. Define Ã_X(Y)=W(R), Ã_X^+(Y)=W(R^+), B̃_X(Y)=W(R)[1/p], and the overconvergent integral, bounded and interval sheaves by the relative radius rings above: Ã_X^{†,r}=R̃_R^{int,r}, B̃_X^{†,r}=R̃_R^{bd,r}, C̃_X^I=R̃_R^I, with their radius limits Ã_X^†,B̃_X^†,C̃_X. Sheafify on the perfectoid basis. A φ^d-module is a finite locally projective module sheaf with an isomorphism φ^{d*}M≅M. Pure and étale mean those conditions on every geometric perfectoid evaluation; a lift-independent test suffices by pointwise slope theory. Integral-positive Witt sections have only almost acyclicity. Use ordinary acyclicity and unrestricted perfectoid evaluation only for the ring variants whose proof applies; no blanket acyclicity is imposed.

**Hypotheses and scope.** X and d satisfy KL Hypothesis 9.3.2; the positive and radius topologies are retained. This definition is independent of choosing a toric cover of X.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Apply the relative ring construction to the tilt on each perfectoid subdomain. Glue through the rational and pro-étale sheaf property. Transport Frobenius and finite projective modules through descent. For evaluation away from the basis, use the corrected cohomological restriction of Remark 9.3.17, not the false integral-positive clause of Lemma 9.3.4.

**API.**

- `PerfectPeriodSheaf.sections` (characterisation): On perfectoid subdomains sections are the displayed ring variants.
- `PerfectPeriodSheaf.phi` (structure): φ^d-pullback has its finite projective linearization isomorphism.
- `PerfectPeriodSheaf.pullback` (functoriality): Pullback commutes with the ring construction and φ linearization.
- `PerfectPeriodSheaf.etale` (characterisation): Étaleness is the pointwise slope-zero condition and is independent of the chosen perfectoid lift.
- `PerfectPeriodSheaf.integral_almost` (compatibility): Higher cohomology of Ã^+ is almost zero in the Witt almost sense, killed by [x] for each topologically nilpotent x.

**Unit tests.**

- `PerfectPeriodSheaf.point` (compatibility): For X=Spa(C,O_C), Ã^+=A_inf(C), whereas Ã=W(C^flat).
- `PerfectPeriodSheaf.positive` (non-example): The Artin–Schreier ramified perfectoid field example detects the false ordinary-acyclicity assertion for Ã^+.
- `PerfectPeriodSheaf.unit_module` (degenerate): The trivial rank-one module has semilinear Frobenius and slope zero.
- `PerfectPeriodSheaf.radius` (computation): φ sends a radius-r section to the correct radius-r/p ring; it is not a radius-preserving operator on one fixed annulus.

**Uses.** KL Theorems 9.3.7 and 9.3.13: Provides period-module realizations of local systems.. KL Remark 9.3.17: Evaluates modules on perfectoid objects with the corrected acyclicity restrictions..

**Checks.** A chosen free basis is unnecessary; finite locally projective sheaves are the objects.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/relative-perfect-period-rings`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-relative-perfect-period-rings), `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0`.

**Sources.** [Kiran S. Kedlaya, Ruochuan Liu — Relative p-adic Hodge theory: Foundations](https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.0792v5), Hypothesis 9.3.2, Definitions 9.3.3 and 9.3.5, Lemma 9.3.4, p.196; Remark 9.3.17, p.198. Defines the perfect period sheaves, their φ-modules and perfectoid evaluation; the integral-positive acyclicity clause is corrected by the source issue.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-relative-pure-and-etale-loci"></a>

### Pure and étale loci of relative Frobenius modules

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/relative-pure-and-etale-loci` (theorem).

For a φ^d-module M over C̃_X, its pure locus and its étale locus are partially proper open subsets of X. If X is taut, each locus is taut. The notion is independent of the choice of perfectoid lift; the slope normalization for φ^d divides Newton valuations by d. Only the locus where the whole module is pure is asserted open; the individual slope filtration need not glue across a changing polygon.

**Hypotheses and scope.** X is preadic over Q_{p^d}; M is finite locally projective with invertible Frobenius linearization.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Localize on X=Spa(A,A^+), choose a perfectoid faithfully covering algebra as in KL Lemma 3.6.26, and apply the pure-locus theorem on its relative Robba ring. Descend the locus through the spectral map and use lift-independent pointwise slopes. Tautness follows from partially proper openness.

**Checks.** A rank-one module φ^de=p^me has slope m/d; it is étale exactly when m=0.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/relative-witt-and-robba-period-sheaves`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-relative-witt-and-robba-period-sheaves), `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0`.

**Sources.** [Kiran S. Kedlaya, Ruochuan Liu — Relative p-adic Hodge theory: Foundations](https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.0792v5), Theorem 9.3.6, p.196; Corollaries 7.3.8 and 7.3.10, pp.159–160. Proves partially proper openness after perfectoid localization and ensures pointwise slope tests are lift-independent.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-relative-local-systems-and-frobenius-modules"></a>

### Local systems and relative Frobenius modules

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/relative-local-systems-and-frobenius-modules` (theorem).

For X preadic over Q_{p^d}, finite locally free étale Z_{p^d}-local systems are equivalent to φ^d-modules over Ã_X and over Ã_X^†. Rational Q_{p^d}-local systems are equivalent to étale φ^d-modules over B̃_X,B̃_X^† and C̃_X. The equivalences preserve rank, tensor products, duals and pullback. The inverse takes φ^d-fixed sections on sufficiently small pro-étale perfectoid objects; surjectivity of φ^d−1 is sheaf-local. Their curve realization is the pointwise degree-zero semistable vector-bundle category; its geometry and curve equivalence are supplied by the curve roadmap and are outgoing uses, not prerequisites of the local-system equivalence.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Finite projective φ-modules; the rational coefficient field is the unramified degree-d field Q_{p^d}. Retain étaleness on rational period modules; arbitrary φ-modules are not representations.

**Construction or proof.**

1. For the integral case apply perfect-field Artin–Schreier–Witt descent and the relative integral étale lattice theorem on each perfectoid basis object. Prove overconvergent extension is an equivalence and glue, using local-system descent. Invert p and use the pointwise slope-zero integral model to obtain the rational equivalences. Construct the inverse as locally constant fixed sections and prove the unit and counit locally before descent.

**Checks.** For the unit rank-one module the inverse is the constant Z_{p^d} or Q_{p^d} local system. A slope m/d line with m≠0 has no étale rational realization. Rational étale realization must not require a global unit-root lattice: the local invariant sheaf construction accommodates KL Examples 8.5.17–8.5.18, pp.176–178.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/relative-witt-and-robba-period-sheaves`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-relative-witt-and-robba-period-sheaves), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/relative-pure-and-etale-loci`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-relative-pure-and-etale-loci), `PerfectoidSpaces:P3`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1`.

**Sources.** [Kiran S. Kedlaya, Ruochuan Liu — Relative p-adic Hodge theory: Foundations](https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.0792v5), Theorems 9.3.7 and 9.3.13 and proofs, pp.196–198; Theorems 8.5.5 and 8.5.12, pp.181–183. Gives the integral and rational equivalences by localization of the perfectoid-base equivalences.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-relative-frobenius-cohomology-comparison"></a>

### Relative Frobenius cohomology

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/relative-frobenius-cohomology-comparison` (construction).

For a φ^d-module sheaf M define RΓ_{φ^d}(X,M) as the hypercohomology of [M→M], in degrees 0 and 1, with differential φ^d−1. For a local system T or V and the module realizations above, the natural maps identify pro-étale cohomology with this Frobenius cohomology over every integral or étale rational period variant. For a relative B-pair (M_e,M_dR^+,M_dR) with its two scalar-extension identifications, define RΓ_B as the hypercohomology of [M_e⊕M_dR^+→M_dR], (x,y)↦x−y. Once the relative B-pair equivalence supplies the same realization, the natural map identifies this cohomology with pro-étale cohomology. The B-pair is a sheaf pair with a common ambient module; it is not the quotient term of the fundamental period complex.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Use the integral or étale rational modules arising from a local system, not arbitrary positive sheaves. The relative B_e sheaf and period-patching equivalence are needed for the B-pair clause.

**Construction or proof.**

1. The sheaf exact sequence 0→T→M→M→0 follows from Artin–Schreier–Witt: the kernel is the fixed-section local system and φ^d−1 is made surjective by a pro-étale tower of finite étale covers. Compare the overconvergent sequence through its kernel and cokernel sheaves. Rationalize with the required limit control. The relative B-pair clause follows from the two-period-cover patching complex, whose derived identification must be established independently of blanket positive acyclicity.

**API.**

- `RelativePhiCohomology.differential` (data): The differential is φ^d−1, with degree-zero kernel the fixed sections.
- `RelativePhiCohomology.comparison` (equivalence): The Artin–Schreier–Witt resolution induces the pro-étale cohomology isomorphism.
- `RelativePhiCohomology.pullback` (functoriality): The natural comparison commutes with local-system pullback and coefficient maps.
- `RelativeBPairCohomology.difference` (data): The difference differential uses the two specified maps into the common M_dR.
- `RelativeBPairCohomology.period_patching` (compatibility): The Frobenius and B-pair resolutions agree under the relative period-patching realization.

**Unit tests.**

- `RelativePhiCohomology.zero` (degenerate): The zero module has zero cohomology.
- `RelativePhiCohomology.unit` (computation): The unit module has degree-zero kernel Z_{p^d} in the integral realization.
- `RelativeBPairCohomology.sign` (non-example): The differential is x−y; diagonal common sections lie in its kernel.
- `RelativePhiCohomology.rational` (compatibility): The rational comparison is functorial under extension of the unramified coefficient field.

**Uses.** KL Theorems 9.4.2 and 9.4.5: Compares integral and rational pro-étale cohomology with period cohomology.. Relative B-pair consumers: Receives the common-module complex from the curve-side period-patching realization..

**Checks.** For a unit local system in degree zero, the kernel of φ^d−1 recovers its constant sections.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/relative-local-systems-and-frobenius-modules`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-relative-local-systems-and-frobenius-modules), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/fundamental-period-complex`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-fundamental-period-complex), `AInfCohomology:AI.2`, [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/relative-two-period-pairs`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-relative-two-period-pairs).

**Sources.** [Kiran S. Kedlaya, Ruochuan Liu — Relative p-adic Hodge theory: Foundations](https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.0792v5), Definitions 9.4.1 and 9.4.4 and Theorems 9.4.2 and 9.4.5, pp.198–200. Defines both two-term complexes and compares them with local-system cohomology via sheaf exactness and period patching.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-filtered-derived-period-interface"></a>

### Filtered derived completion for period comparisons

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/filtered-derived-period-interface` (theorem).

Use decreasing sequences F^iA of complexes on a fixed small site, with gr^iA=Cone(F^{i+1}A→F^iA). Termwise quasi-isomorphisms define the filtered derived category; quasi-isomorphisms on gr define a distinct localization. If F^iA^n=0 for i≫0 in each degree and the filtration spectral sequence degenerates at E_1, all H^j(F^{i+1}A)→H^j(F^iA) are injective. If A→B is a graded quasi-isomorphism and A has these filtered cohomology objects, then B does too and the induced map on their filtration completions is an isomorphism. This does not assert an isomorphism on uncompleted cohomology.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Fix a κ-small basis/site within one universe. The degreewise boundedness is the hypothesis of the degeneration assertion; the comparison assertion assumes filtered cohomology. Completion is lim_i of finite filtration quotients with the required derived limit control.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Import the sequence and localization formalism from EnhancedDerivedSheaves. Identify gr by the displayed cone orientation. Degeneration kills the boundary maps in the long exact sequences and hence proves injectivity. Compare successive finite quotients by induction on the filtration interval, using Cone(F^k→F^j) for j≤k. Pass to inverse limits only after checking the R^1lim condition or using derived completion.

**Checks.** An associated-graded isomorphism alone does not imply that an incomplete filtered object is unchanged. The quotient F^j/F^k for j<k uses Cone(F^k→F^j), so reversal changes the cohomological shift.

**Prerequisites.** `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E0`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E4`.

**Sources.** [L. Alexander Betts and Jakob Stix — Galois sections and p-adic period mappings](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2204.13674), Appendix A, Lemmas A.2–A.3 and Remarks A.1,A.4,A.5, pp.56–58. Distinguishes the two localizations and proves the filtered-cohomology and completion assertions.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-de-rham-pair-derived-pushforward"></a>

### Derived pushforward of associated de Rham pairs

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/de-rham-pair-derived-pushforward` (construction).

For f:X→Y proper smooth between smooth rigid spaces over a finite extension K/Q_p and an associated pair (L,E,c) on X, form DR_{X/Y}(E)^n=Ω^n_{X/Y}⊗E with Fil^i term Ω^n⊗Fil^{i−n}E. Define H^i_dR(f,E)=R^if_*DR_{X/Y}(E), with filtration given by the images of R^if_*Fil^jDR. Its Gauss–Manin connection is the boundary of 0→f^{-1}Ω_Y^1⊗DR_{X/Y}(E)[−1]→DR_X(E)/σ^2→DR_{X/Y}(E)→0, where σ counts differentials from Y. Assume each R^if_*L is a lisse local system. The relative Poincaré map and the period projection map give the two filtered structural comparison maps; after filtration completion they are isomorphisms and recover a unique uncompleted associated de Rham pair. Hodge cohomology is locally free and the relative Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence degenerates at E_1.

**Hypotheses and scope.** The filtered connection on E is integrable and Griffiths transverse; f is smooth proper and the source’s local-system assumption is kept explicitly. The structural OB_dR filtration is not assumed complete.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Construct the two relative de Rham complexes and their filtered comparison maps. On gradeds apply the proper-smooth period projection formula and the relative Poincaré lemma. Degeneration proves that the cohomology filtration is an actual filtration; apply the filtered completion theorem to the graded quasi-isomorphisms. Recover the associated pair using full faithfulness of completion on period local systems. Naturality of the σ-extension yields a flat connection, the Leibniz rule and Griffiths transversality.

**API.**

- `DeRhamPair.pushforward` (constructor): R^if_*(L,E,c) uses the lisse direct image and the filtered Gauss–Manin bundle.
- `DeRhamPair.pushforward_filtration` (characterisation): Fil^j H^i is the image of R^if_*Fil^j DR.
- `DeRhamPair.gauss_manin` (relation): The σ-extension boundary is integrable, satisfies Leibniz and maps Fil^j into Ω_Y^1⊗Fil^{j−1}.
- `DeRhamPair.completed_comparison` (equivalence): The two structural comparison maps become filtered isomorphisms after completion.
- `DeRhamPair.pushforward_morphism` (functoriality): Morphisms of pairs induce compatible maps of direct-image pairs.

**Unit tests.**

- `PairPushforward.point` (degenerate): For the identity on a point only degree zero survives, and the associated pair is unchanged.
- `PairPushforward.filtration` (computation): In degree one the relative de Rham term uses Fil^{j−1}E, not Fil^jE.
- `PairPushforward.unit_elliptic` (compatibility): For an elliptic family the unit pair gives H^1_dR with rank-two comparison and rank-one Fil^1.
- `PairPushforward.completion` (non-example): The structural maps are not inferred to be isomorphisms before completion merely from their graded maps.

**Uses.** Betts–Stix Theorem 3.12: Constructs the relative cohomology pair used in period transport.. Caraiani–Scholze Proposition 2.2.5: Supplies associated relative cohomology to the first Hodge–Tate step..

**Checks.** For the unit pair on a family of elliptic curves, the result has rank two, Fil^1=f_*Ω^1 and the Gauss–Manin connection.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/associated-de-rham-pairs`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-associated-de-rham-pairs), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/filtered-derived-period-interface`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-filtered-derived-period-interface), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/early-relative-primitive-comparison`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-early-relative-primitive-comparison), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/relative-poincare-lemma`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-relative-poincare-lemma), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/plan/relative-bdr-plus-local-system-comparison`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-plan-relative-bdr-plus-local-system-comparison), `AdicSpacesPartII:R3`, [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/completion-on-period-local-system-image`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-completion-on-period-local-system-image).

**Proof ingredients.** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/relative-pushforward-of-graded-structural-sheaf`; their statements and locators appear in the proof-ingredient index.

**Sources.** [L. Alexander Betts and Jakob Stix — Galois sections and p-adic period mappings](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2204.13674), §3.2.2, Theorem 3.12 and proof, pp.20–22. Constructs pushforward with Gauss–Manin, compares after completion and obtains degeneration and association.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-completion-on-period-local-system-image"></a>

### Full faithfulness of structural period completion

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/completion-on-period-local-system-image` (theorem).

Let M_0,M_1 be filtered structural OB_dR-bundles with flat connection in the essential image of B_dR^+-local systems. Each filtered OB̂_dR-linear horizontal map M̂_0→M̂_1 is the completion of a unique filtered OB_dR-linear horizontal map M_0→M_1. The original map is invertible exactly when its completion is. The essential-image condition is part of the statement; this is not a completion theorem for arbitrary filtered OB_dR-bundles.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Completion is in the filtration, and the period local systems are finite locally free.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Apply the completed Poincaré lemma to identify Fil^0 horizontal sections of each completed bundle with its original B_dR^+-local system. Complete-period maps therefore restrict to maps of those local systems. Full faithfulness of the structural period functor reconstructs the original map; do the same for its inverse. Derived completion is controlled on perfectoid objects by graded Ô acyclicity and the inverse-limit lemma.

**Checks.** For the trivial rank-one period local system, a completed horizontal filtered endomorphism is exactly its original B_dR^+-linear endomorphism.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/associated-de-rham-pairs`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-associated-de-rham-pairs), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/filtered-derived-period-interface`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-filtered-derived-period-interface), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/plan/poincare-lemma-and-faltings-extension`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-local-rational-plan-poincare-lemma-and-faltings-extension).

**Sources.** [L. Alexander Betts and Jakob Stix — Galois sections and p-adic period mappings](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2204.13674), Lemma 3.14 and Remark 3.15, pp.22–23. Proves full faithfulness and reflects isomorphisms on the indicated essential image.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-de-rham-pair-pushforward-compatibilities"></a>

### Cup products, base change and analytification of de Rham pairs

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/de-rham-pair-pushforward-compatibilities` (theorem).

In the proper-smooth de Rham-pair setting with lisse higher direct images, a pairing of pairs induces the cup-product pairing of their direct-image pairs. Every commuting square with smooth proper vertical maps induces f^*R^iπ_*(L,E,c)→R^iπ′_*g^*(L,E,c); it is a morphism of filtered flat associated pairs, and is an isomorphism under the proper base-change hypotheses, in particular for a Cartesian square. For a smooth proper algebraic map of smooth K-varieties, analytification identifies filtered de Rham direct images and completed lisse étale direct images with their rigid counterparts. Consequently the absolute c_dR from this construction respects cup products, pullback, finite base extension and Künneth maps.

**Hypotheses and scope.** K is a finite extension of Q_p. Keep the completion on the Z_p-local system under analytification. Do not assert invertibility for a non-Cartesian commuting square.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Construct cup and base-change maps on the relative de Rham and local-system complexes. Naturality of the period projection and Poincaré maps makes the diagrams commute after completion; reflect them back using full faithfulness. Algebraic/analytic agreement uses coherent proper GAGA for de Rham complexes and the finite-coefficient étale comparison, then the controlled inverse limit for lisse Z_p. The Künneth compatibility follows from product projections and the cup-product identity.

**Checks.** For f:X→point the product X×X comparison agrees with the exterior cup product. The zero-to-nonzero map induced by a general non-Cartesian square need not be an isomorphism.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/de-rham-pair-derived-pushforward`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-de-rham-pair-derived-pushforward), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/completion-on-period-local-system-image`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-completion-on-period-local-system-image), `AdicSpacesPartII:R3`, `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H5`.

**Sources.** [L. Alexander Betts and Jakob Stix — Galois sections and p-adic period mappings](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2204.13674), Propositions 3.16–3.19, pp.23–27. Proves the pair compatibilities, algebraic/analytic agreement and formal compatibilities of the chosen absolute comparison.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-p8-relative-two-period-pairs"></a>

### Relative two-period pairs

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:P8/relative-two-period-pairs` (construction).

For X preadic over Q_{p^d} and a perfectoid subdomain Y, let R_1,R_2,R_3 be the untilt-patching rings of AI.2. Set B_e,X(Y)=R_1, B_dR,X^+(Y)=R_2 and B_dR,X(Y)=R_3. Equivalently R_2 is the ker θ-adic completion of B̃_X^{†,1}(Y), and R_3 inverts a generator of this ideal. The untilt complement description identifies R_1 with the coordinate ring of the complement of its canonical untilt divisor. A relative B-pair is a triple of finite locally projective sheaves (M_e,M_dR^+,M_dR), with specified identifications M_e⊗_{B_e}B_dR≅M_dR≅M_dR^+⊗_{B_dR^+}B_dR. Morphisms respect both identifications. Finite-projective patching gives the period-pair realization of relative φ^d-modules; the vector-bundle realization on the relative curve is an outgoing interface owned by RF1/VB1.

**Hypotheses and scope.** X and d satisfy KL Hypothesis 9.3.2. The period-pair descent is the finite-projective untilt patching theorem; flat-coefficient cohomological exactness is stated separately.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Sheafify the three untilt-patching rings and glue the scalar-extension identifications. Identify the rational completion with the integral-radius completion through the fact that p is already a unit after θ-adic completion. Apply finite-projective triple descent from AI.2 locally and glue it along perfectoid covers.

**API.**

- `RelativeBPair.period_rings` (data): The section rings are precisely the three untilt-patching rings, with their two maps into R_3.
- `RelativeBPair.glue` (constructor): Glue finite projective pairs through compatible local scalar-extension identifications.
- `RelativeBPair.tensor` (constructor): Tensor the three modules and their two identifications componentwise.
- `RelativeBPair.dual` (constructor): Dualize each finite projective module and transport the comparison maps.
- `RelativeBPair.phi_realization` (equivalence): Relative φ^d-modules have the period-pair realization supplied by finite-projective patching.

**Unit tests.**

- `RelativeBPair.unit` (degenerate): The triple (B_e,B_dR^+,B_dR) with the canonical maps is the tensor unit.
- `RelativeBPair.point` (compatibility): At a geometric untilt point with d=1, the triple recovers the usual field B-pair rings.
- `RelativeBPair.missing_map` (non-example): Equal module ranks do not replace a scalar-extension identification; incompatible maps cannot be glued.
- `RelativeBPair.completion` (computation): p is a unit in R_2; θ maps to the rational untilt, and the θ-adic generator is not a unit until passage to R_3.

**Uses.** KL Definition 9.4.4 and Theorem 9.4.5: Provides the coefficient objects of the two-period difference complex.. RF1/VB1 relative curve realization: Supplies the common period pair to be realized by a vector bundle..

**Checks.** The two comparison maps are data. A pair with no common ambient identification is not an object of this category.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/relative-perfect-period-rings`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-relative-perfect-period-rings), [`PadicHodgeTheory:P8/relative-witt-and-robba-period-sheaves`](#target-padichodgetheory-p8-relative-witt-and-robba-period-sheaves), `AInfCohomology:AI.2`.

**Sources.** [Kiran S. Kedlaya, Ruochuan Liu — Relative p-adic Hodge theory: Foundations](https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.0792v5), Definition 9.3.11 and Theorem 9.3.12, p.197; Definition 8.9.4 and Theorem 8.9.6, pp.187–188. Defines the three sheaves, their finite-projective triples and the patching realization.

### Worked example — Transversality and a relative elliptic Hodge step

On a disk with coordinate x, take E=Oe_1⊕Oe_2 with its trivial connection, Fil^1E=Fil^2E=O(e_1+xe_2), Fil^0E=E and Fil^3E=0. At i=2, the derivative e_2 dx lies outside Fil^1E⊗Ω^1, so this filtered bundle fails Griffiths transversality and cannot enter the associated local-system functor. The obstruction uses a gap of two in the filtration. For an elliptic scheme f:A→S, put M=f_*Ω^1_{A/S} and N=R^1f_*O_A. The first relative Hodge–Tate step gives 0→N⊗Ô_S→(R^1f_*Q_p)⊗Ô_S→M⊗Ô_S(−1)→0, with rank one at both ends. It is a filtration with its stated extension class; the comparison does not assert a canonical global splitting on S.


<a id="layer-r06-4"></a>

## R06.4 — Integral and small-weight interfaces

State the rational consequences of the integral classifiers without enlarging their essential image. Every small-weight or endpoint assertion fixes the coefficient field, the weight convention, the base-field ramification and any nilpotence requirement. The crystalline lattice classifications and finite-flat group constructions are supplied by R07.1, R07.3 and R07.4.

**Landmarks:** Fontaine–Laffaille admissibility theorem; Fontaine–Laffaille rational consequences; Ordinary representations; Ordinary representations are semistable; Small-weight ordinarity.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-r06-4-plan-fontaine-laffaille-crystalline-comparison"></a>

### Fontaine–Laffaille's rational functor is the dual of V_cris on weakly admissible modules with jumps in [0, p−1]

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/fontaine-laffaille-crystalline-comparison` (theorem).

Let K = K_0 = W(k)[1/p] be absolutely unramified (e = 1), σ its Frobenius. A filtered φ-module D over K is weakly admissible in the sense of R06.2/weak-admissibility; its jumps are the i with gr^i D ≠ 0. For Fontaine–Laffaille (FL) objects we use the notation of FL 1982: MF_tor^{f,p} (finite-length W(k)-modules M with M^0 = M, M^p = 0 and φ^i: M^i → M), strongly divisible lattices (FL 7.7), the ring Ŝ and Ŝ_K = K ⊗ Ŝ, and the contravariant functors U_S(M) = Hom_{MF}(M, Ŝ) (lattices), U_S(M) = Ext^1(M, S) (torsion) and U_{S_K}(Δ) = Hom_{MF_K}(Δ, Ŝ_K) (rational), all supplied by FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.3. Let MF^{wa,[0,p−1]}_K be the category of weakly admissible filtered φ-modules D over K with Fil^0 D = D and Fil^p D = 0. For D in it there is a natural G_K-equivariant isomorphism U_{S_K}(D) = Hom_{φ,Fil}(D, Ŝ_K) ≅ Hom_{φ,Fil}(D, B_cris) = V_cris(D)^* (FL: U_{S_K} ≅ V_B^* on MF^{f,p}_K). In particular D is admissible, D ≅ D*_cris(U_{S_K}(D)); U_{S_K} is exact and fully faithful on MF^{wa,[0,p−1]}_K, with quasi-inverse on its essential image U ↦ Hom_{Q_p[G_K]}(U, Ŝ_K) = D*_cris(U), and U_{S_K}(D) is crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights the jumps of D (in [0, p−1]).

**Hypotheses and scope.** K is absolutely unramified, with perfect residue, and the precise supported Fontaine–Laffaille weight interval and nilpotence conditions are those stated below. The period realization uses the explicit A_cris comparison with the Fontaine–Laffaille carrier and contravariant crystalline functor.

**Construction or proof.**

1. FL (proof of 8.4): Ŝ_K is identified, as a filtered Galois ring, with B_a^+ of [F2] §4 (a = {x ∈ R : v_R(x) ≥ p}); Hom_{MF_K}(D, B_a^+) ⊂ Hom_{MF_K}(D, B) = V_B(D) and (V^* ⊗ B_a^+)^G ⊂ D_B(V^*).
2. Replacement via A_cris (R06.1/crystalline-period-ring; R07.3 for Ŝ): Ŝ is the p-adic completion of W(R)[ξ^p/p] ⊂ A_cris (ξ^p/p = (p−1)!·γ_p(ξ)), with Fil^iŜ_K = Ŝ_K ∩ Fil^iB_dR (to be checked against FL §2, R07.3); φ(B_max^+) ⊂ Ŝ[1/p] because φ(ξ)/p ≡ ξ^p/p mod W(R).
3. Since D = φ(D) and Fil^0 D = D, any φ-compatible f: D → B_cris with f(D) ⊂ Fil^0 B_cris lands in B'_cris = {x : φ^n(x) ∈ Fil^0 ∀ n} and hence in φ(B'_cris) ⊂ B_cris^+ ⊂ B_max^+, so f(D) = φ(f(φ^{−1}D)) ⊂ φ(B_max^+) ⊂ Ŝ_K: Hom_{φ,Fil}(D, Ŝ_K) = Hom_{φ,Fil}(D, B_cris) = V_cris(D)^* (Berger survey II.3.4 for B'_cris).
4. Dimension: dim_{Q_p} U_{S_K}(D) = dim_K D (FL Proposition 7.17(i), via a strongly divisible lattice, FL Proposition 7.8; R07.3) and the evaluation map D → Hom(U_{S_K}(D), Ŝ_K) is injective (FL 7.17(ii)); hence dim D*_cris(U_{S_K}(D)) ≥ dim D, U_{S_K}(D) is crystalline and D ≅ D*_cris(U_{S_K}(D)) (R06.2/admissible-representations).
5. Full faithfulness and the quasi-inverse: FL Remarques 7.18(a) and 8.5; exactness from exactness of V_cris on admissible modules (R06.2).

**Checks.** D = K·e, φ(e) = p^n e, jump at n (0 ≤ n ≤ p − 1): U_{S_K}(D) = Q_p(n). D with jumps {0, p−1} (modular weight p) is covered; D with jumps {0, p} (modular weight p + 1) is not (Fil^p D ≠ 0).

**Prerequisites.** `FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.3`, [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/crystalline-period-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-crystalline-period-ring), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/de-rham-period-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-de-rham-period-ring), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/period-functors`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-period-functors), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/admissible-representations`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-admissible-representations), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/weak-admissibility`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-weak-admissibility), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/hodge-tate-weight-convention`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-hodge-tate-weight-convention).

**Sources.** [Jean-Marc Fontaine and Guy Laffaille — Construction de représentations p-adiques](http://www.numdam.org/item?id=ASENS_1982_4_15_4_547_0), 8.4 Théorème (ii) and its proof, pp. 595–596 (checked on the page images). The crystalline comparison with the rational Fontaine–Laffaille functor, with the filtration equality as a separate input. [Jean-Marc Fontaine and Guy Laffaille — Construction de représentations p-adiques](http://www.numdam.org/item?id=ASENS_1982_4_15_4_547_0), 7.18 Remarques (a), p. 594 (checked on the page image). Full faithfulness of the rational functor. [Laurent Berger — An introduction to the theory of p-adic representations](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0210184v1), II.3.4, p. 15. φ(B'_cris) ⊂ B_cris^+, used in the replacement argument.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-r06-4-plan-small-weight-admissibility"></a>

### Fontaine–Laffaille: weakly admissible filtered φ-modules of filtration length < p over K_0 are admissible

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/small-weight-admissibility` (theorem).

Let K = K_0 = W(k)[1/p] be absolutely unramified (e = 1), σ its Frobenius. A filtered φ-module D over K is weakly admissible in the sense of R06.2/weak-admissibility; its jumps are the i with gr^i D ≠ 0. For Fontaine–Laffaille (FL) objects we use the notation of FL 1982: MF_tor^{f,p} (finite-length W(k)-modules M with M^0 = M, M^p = 0 and φ^i: M^i → M), strongly divisible lattices (FL 7.7), the ring Ŝ and Ŝ_K = K ⊗ Ŝ, and the contravariant functors U_S(M) = Hom_{MF}(M, Ŝ) (lattices), U_S(M) = Ext^1(M, S) (torsion) and U_{S_K}(Δ) = Hom_{MF_K}(Δ, Ŝ_K) (rational), all supplied by FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.3. If D is a weakly admissible filtered φ-module over K = K_0 and there is j ∈ Z with Fil^j D = D and Fil^{j+p} D = 0 (filtration length < p), then D is admissible: D ≅ D_cris(V) for the crystalline representation V = V_cris(D), whose Hodge–Tate weights lie in [−j−p+1, −j] (convention HT(χ_p) = +1). In particular every crystalline representation of G_{K_0} whose Hodge–Tate weights lie in an interval of length ≤ p − 1 corresponds to such D, and conversely.

**Hypotheses and scope.** e = 1 (K = K_0); no restriction on p. This is a special case of the Colmez–Fontaine theorem (R06.2/colmez-fontaine-theorem) but FL's proof is independent of it and predates it.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Twist: choose a rank-one weakly admissible D_2 with its jump at j (e.g. D_cris(Q_p(−j))) and write D = D_1 ⊗ D_2 with D_1 weakly admissible, Fil^0 D_1 = D_1, Fil^p D_1 = 0 (FL proof of 8.4; weak admissibility is stable under ⊗ with rank one objects, R06.2/weak-admissibility).
2. D_1 is admissible by PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/fontaine-laffaille-crystalline-comparison (U_{S_K}(D_1) crystalline of dimension dim D_1 with D*_cris = D_1).
3. Rank-one weakly admissible objects are admissible (Fontaine [F1] 4.4.1 via FL; R06.2), and admissible objects are stable under ⊗ (R06.2/admissible-representations), so D = D_1 ⊗ D_2 is admissible.
4. Weights: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/fontaine-laffaille-sign-dictionary (1).

**Checks.** D_cris(Q_p(n)) for every n (length 0). D = D_cris(V_p(E)) for E/Q_p with good reduction: jumps {−1, 0}, length 1 < p for every p. Modular weight p: jumps {0, p − 1} (length p − 1 < p) — covered; modular weight p + 1: jumps {0, p} — not covered (needs R06.2/colmez-fontaine-theorem or Breuil–Kisin, PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/weight-p-plus-one-branch).

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/fontaine-laffaille-crystalline-comparison`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-4-plan-fontaine-laffaille-crystalline-comparison), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/hodge-tate-weight-convention`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-hodge-tate-weight-convention), `FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.3`, [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/period-functors`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-period-functors), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/weak-admissibility-is-admissibility`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-weak-admissibility-is-admissibility), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/weak-admissibility`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-weak-admissibility), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/admissible-representations`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-admissible-representations).

**Proof ingredients.** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/fontaine-laffaille-sign-dictionary`; their statements and locators appear in the proof-ingredient index.

**Sources.** [Jean-Marc Fontaine and Guy Laffaille — Construction de représentations p-adiques](http://www.numdam.org/item?id=ASENS_1982_4_15_4_547_0), 0.1 Théorème, p. 548 (checked on the page image). Statement. [Jean-Marc Fontaine and Guy Laffaille — Construction de représentations p-adiques](http://www.numdam.org/item?id=ASENS_1982_4_15_4_547_0), 8.4 Théorème (i), p. 595 (checked on the page image). Precise form.

### Rational and lattice consequences of Fontaine–Laffaille theory at e = 1 on the shifted interval [0, p−2]

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/fontaine-laffaille-rational-consequences` (theorem).

Let K = K_0 = W(k)[1/p] be absolutely unramified (e = 1), σ its Frobenius. A filtered φ-module D over K is weakly admissible in the sense of R06.2/weak-admissibility; its jumps are the i with gr^i D ≠ 0. For Fontaine–Laffaille (FL) objects we use the notation of FL 1982: MF_tor^{f,p} (finite-length W(k)-modules M with M^0 = M, M^p = 0 and φ^i: M^i → M), strongly divisible lattices (FL 7.7), the ring Ŝ and Ŝ_K = K ⊗ Ŝ, and the contravariant functors U_S(M) = Hom_{MF}(M, Ŝ) (lattices), U_S(M) = Ext^1(M, S) (torsion) and U_{S_K}(Δ) = Hom_{MF_K}(Δ, Ŝ_K) (rational), all supplied by FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.3. Let MF^{sd,[0,p−2]} be the category of strongly divisible lattices M (FL 7.7) with Fil^0 M = M and Fil^{p−1} M = 0, and T(M) := U_S(M) (contravariant). Then: (a) T(M) is a G_K-stable Z_p-lattice in the crystalline representation U_{S_K}(M[1/p]) = V_cris(M[1/p])^*, whose Hodge–Tate weights are the jumps of M (in [0, p−2]); (b) T is exact, faithful, rank-preserving and fully faithful: Hom_{Z_p[G_K]}(T(M), T(M')) = Hom(M', M); (c) for every n ≥ 1, T(M)/p^n ≅ U_S(M/p^nM) with M/p^nM ∈ MF_tor^{f,p} having jumps in [0, p−2], and U_S is fully faithful on such torsion objects; in particular Hom_{G_K}(T(M)/p^n, T(M')/p^n) = Hom_{MF}(M'/p^n, M/p^n); (d) the same statements hold on any common shifted interval [c, c + p − 2] after the Tate twist of PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/fontaine-laffaille-sign-dictionary (4); (e) on the wider interval [0, p − 1] (Fil^p M = 0), (a) holds and T is exact, faithful and rank-preserving, but (b)–(c) hold only for M whose reduction M/pM has no nonzero quotient N with N^{p−1} = N (resp. no nonzero subobject N with N^1 = 0) — the restrictions of FL §0.9/§6 — and fail in general (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/fontaine-laffaille-endpoint-non-example); (f) rationally, U_{S_K} is fully faithful on all of [0, p − 1] with no restriction. For p = 2 the interval [0, p − 2] is {0}: only unramified representations are covered by (b)–(c).

**Hypotheses and scope.** K = K_0; the integral classification (strongly divisible lattices, MF_tor^{f,p}, U_S, FL Theorems 3.3, 6.1 and Propositions 7.8, 7.15, 7.17) is imported from FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.3. Essential surjectivity onto all G_K-stable lattices of crystalline representations with weights in [0, p−2] is not asserted here (FL do not state it; FL Remarque 6.13(a) notes the essential image is hard to characterise); it is supplied by R07.3/R07.4.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a): FL Proposition 7.15(i) (rank preservation) and 7.14 (U_S(M) = lim U_S(M/p^n), a lattice), with U_S(M)[1/p] = U_{S_K}(M[1/p]) (FL 7.16–7.17) identified with V_cris^* by PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/fontaine-laffaille-crystalline-comparison; weights by PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/fontaine-laffaille-sign-dictionary.
2. (b): Fil^{p−1}M = 0 forces M/pM ∈ MF_tor^{f,p'} (a quotient N with N^{p−1} = N is a quotient of the zero module Fil^{p−1}, hence 0), so FL Proposition 7.15(ii) gives full faithfulness (R07.3).
3. (c): FL Théorème 3.3 (exactness, faithfulness, length) and Théorème 6.1(ii) on MF_tor^{f,p'} (R07.3), with U_S(M/p^nM) = Hom_{MF}(M, S_n) = T(M)/p^n (FL 7.14).
4. (d): twist; (e): FL §0.9, Théorème 6.1 and Proposition 7.15(ii); (f): FL Remarques 7.18(a), 8.5.

**Checks.** Q_p(n), 0 ≤ n ≤ p − 2: M = Z_p·e with Fil^n M = M, Fil^{n+1}M = 0, φ_n(e) = e; T(M) = Z_p(n) and T(M)/p = F_p(ω^n); the characters ω^0, …, ω^{p−2} are pairwise distinct, so no two such objects collide (PARI/GP for p = 3, 5, 7, 11). Tate module of an elliptic curve with good reduction over Q_p (p ≥ 3): Hodge–Tate weights {0, 1} ⊂ [0, p − 2], T_p(E) = U_S(M) for the strongly divisible lattice of the Dieudonné module of E[p^∞] (FL §9, R07.3); Hom_{G}(T_p(E)/p, T_p(E')/p) is computed by filtered Dieudonné modules. Non-example at weight p − 1: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/fontaine-laffaille-endpoint-non-example (Z_p and Z_p(p−1) have isomorphic reductions while the FL modules M(1;0), M(1;p−1) have no nonzero maps).

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/fontaine-laffaille-crystalline-comparison`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-4-plan-fontaine-laffaille-crystalline-comparison), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/hodge-tate-weight-convention`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-hodge-tate-weight-convention), `FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.3`, [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/period-functors`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-period-functors), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/weak-admissibility-is-admissibility`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-weak-admissibility-is-admissibility), `mathlib:ZMod.units_pow_card_sub_one_eq_one`.

**Proof ingredients.** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/fontaine-laffaille-sign-dictionary`, `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/fontaine-laffaille-endpoint-non-example`; their statements and locators appear in the proof-ingredient index.

**Sources.** [Jean-Marc Fontaine and Guy Laffaille — Construction de représentations p-adiques](http://www.numdam.org/item?id=ASENS_1982_4_15_4_547_0), 7.15 Proposition, pp. 593–594 (checked on the page images). Lattice functor: exact, faithful, rank-preserving. [Jean-Marc Fontaine and Guy Laffaille — Construction de représentations p-adiques](http://www.numdam.org/item?id=ASENS_1982_4_15_4_547_0), 7.15 Proposition (ii), p. 594 (checked on the page image). Full faithfulness on the restricted subcategories. [Jean-Marc Fontaine and Guy Laffaille — Construction de représentations p-adiques](http://www.numdam.org/item?id=ASENS_1982_4_15_4_547_0), 0.10, p. 552 (checked on the page image). Only almost fully faithful on the full range.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-r06-4-plan-ordinary-representation"></a>

### Ordinary p-adic representations (Perrin-Riou)

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/ordinary-representation` (definition).

Let K/Q_p be finite and E/Q_p finite. An E-linear representation V of G_K is ordinary if it has a decreasing, exhaustive, separated filtration (Fil^iV)_{i∈Z} by G_K-stable E-subspaces such that the inertia group I_K acts on gr^iV = Fil^iV/Fil^{i+1}V through χ^i (i.e. gr^iV(−i) is unramified). The filtration is part of the data required to exist; its jumps are the Hodge–Tate weights of V (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/ordinary-implies-semistable), with sub-objects of higher weight: Fil^iV is the part of weight ≥ i.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Convention HT(χ_p) = +1: gr^i carries Hodge–Tate weight i, and higher weights sit lower in the flag (sub-objects). Berger 2002 §6 (after Perrin-Riou [37, 1.1]) states the definition for an arbitrary perfect residue field; here K/Q_p is finite.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Definition; the unramified characters are those trivial on I_K (Mathlib ValuationSubring.inertiaSubgroup gives the inertia subgroup of a decomposition group).
2. Stability: subquotients by G_K-stable subspaces inherit ordinary filtrations (induced filtrations); duals are ordinary with Fil^i(V^*) = (Fil^{1−i}V)^⊥ and weights negated; tensor products are ordinary with the tensor filtration.

**API.**

- `IsOrdinary` (constructor): ∃ decreasing exhaustive separated G_K-stable filtration with I_K acting on gr^i through χ^i.
- `IsOrdinary.subquotient` (functoriality): Subrepresentations and quotients of ordinary representations are ordinary (induced filtrations).
- `IsOrdinary.dual` (functoriality): V ordinary ⇒ V^* ordinary with Fil^i(V^*) = (Fil^{1−i}V)^⊥.
- `IsOrdinary.tensor` (functoriality): V, W ordinary ⇒ V ⊗ W ordinary with Fil^n = Σ_{i+j=n} Fil^iV ⊗ Fil^jW.
- `IsOrdinary.hodgeTateWeights` (characterisation): HT(V) = {i with multiplicity dim gr^iV} (via PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/ordinary-implies-semistable).

**Unit tests.**

- `isOrdinary_tate_twist` (computation): Q_p(n) is ordinary with the one-step filtration at n.
- `isOrdinary_unramified` (degenerate): Every unramified representation is ordinary with Fil^0 = V, Fil^1 = 0.
- `not_isOrdinary_supersingular` (non-example): V_p(E) for E/Q_p with good supersingular reduction is not ordinary: it is irreducible with weights {0,1} (Brinon–Conrad Theorem 8.3.6, no unit Frobenius root).
- `not_isOrdinary_wrong_order` (non-example): A non-split extension 0 → Q_p → V → Q_p(1) → 0 (Hodge–Tate, not de Rham) is not ordinary: the weight-0 line is the sub-object.
- `isOrdinary_cyclotomicCharacter` (compatibility): The character given by Mathlib's cyclotomicCharacter is ordinary with gr^1 = V (I_K acts by χ).

**Uses.** Berger 2002, Corollaire 6.3: ordinary representations are semistable. LocalGaloisDeformationRings:L7: ordinary deformation functors with a full invariant flag. Khare–Wintenberger (I), Theorem 5.1(2): weight-2 lifts with inertial WD parameter (id, N ≠ 0) at k(ρ̄) = p + 1 are ordinary (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/two-dimensional-ordinarity-criterion).

**Checks.** Q_p(n) is ordinary with Fil^nQ_p(n) = Q_p(n), Fil^{n+1} = 0. V_p(E) for E/Q_p with good ordinary or multiplicative reduction is ordinary: Fil^1 = the Q_p(1)-part up to an unramified twist, gr^0 unramified.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:cyclotomicCharacter`, `mathlib:ValuationSubring.inertiaSubgroup`, [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/hodge-tate-weight-convention`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-hodge-tate-weight-convention).

**Sources.** [L. Berger — Représentations p-adiques et équations différentielles](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0102179v3), Proof of Corollaire 6.3, p. 63. Definition used by Berger (after Perrin-Riou). [O. Brinon and B. Conrad — CMI Summer School notes on p-adic Hodge theory](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/notes.pdf), Theorem 8.3.6, p. 121. Ordinary two-dimensional crystalline representations.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-r06-4-plan-ordinary-implies-semistable"></a>

### Extensions of semistable representations that are de Rham are semistable; ordinary representations are semistable

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/ordinary-implies-semistable` (theorem).

Let K/Q_p be finite. (a) If E is a de Rham representation of G_K which is an extension of W by V with V, W semistable, then E is semistable. (b) If V is de Rham with all Hodge–Tate weights ≥ 1 (HT(χ_p) = +1), then every extension of Q_p by V is de Rham: H^1(K, V) = H^1_g(K, V). (c) Every ordinary representation of G_K is semistable (in particular de Rham), and its Hodge–Tate weights are the jumps of its ordinary filtration.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Uses the p-adic monodromy theorem (R06.3); for finite residue field (c) was known (Perrin-Riou) by Galois-cohomological dimension counts, which Berger's argument avoids. Weights ≥ 1 in (b) is the convention HT(χ_p) = +1 (Berger's 'poids ⩾ 1'), e.g. V = Q_p(1).

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a) Lemma 6.4: E is de Rham, hence potentially semistable (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/plan/p-adic-monodromy-theorem); for L/K with E|_{G_L} semistable, 0 → D_st,L(V) → D_st,L(E) → D_st,L(W) → 0 is exact (R06.2), and taking Gal(L/K)-invariants, H^1(Gal(L/K), D_st,L(V)) = 0 (a Q_p-vector space, |Gal(L/K)| invertible) gives dim D_st(E) = dim V + dim W.
2. (b) Lemma 6.5: weights ≥ 1 give H^1(K, B_dR^+ ⊗ V) = 0 (Hodge–Tate decomposition of V ⊗ C(i), Tate's H^1(K, C(j)) = 0 for j ≠ 0 (R06.2/hodge-tate-decomposition-tate), and 0 → t^{i+1}B_dR^+ → t^iB_dR^+ → C(i) → 0); so 1 ∈ (B_dR^+)^{G_K} lifts to (B_dR^+ ⊗ E)^{G_K} outside (B_dR^+ ⊗ V)^{G_K}, and dim D_dR(E) = dim V + 1.
3. (c) Corollary 6.3: induction on the length of the ordinary filtration: E = V extension of gr^{i_min} (lowest weight, unramified twist of χ^{i_min}) by Fil^{i_min+1}V (weights > i_min); twisting by the inverse of the character on gr^{i_min} reduces to an extension of Q_p by a de Rham representation of weights ≥ 1, de Rham by (b); then (a) and induction give semistability.
4. Weights: gr^iV is χ^i times unramified, of Hodge–Tate weight i (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/hodge-tate-weight-convention).

**Checks.** V_p(E_q) (Tate curve): ordinary, semistable, not crystalline. Kummer extensions 0 → Q_p(1) → V → Q_p → 0 (Berger survey II.4.4): all semistable, crystalline iff the Kummer class lies in Q_p ⊗ Ô_K^×.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/ordinary-representation`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-4-plan-ordinary-representation), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/plan/p-adic-monodromy-theorem`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-3-plan-p-adic-monodromy-theorem), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/period-functors`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-period-functors), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/admissible-representations`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-admissible-representations), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/hodge-tate-decomposition-tate`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-hodge-tate-decomposition-tate), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/de-rham-period-ring`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-de-rham-period-ring), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/hodge-tate-weight-convention`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-hodge-tate-weight-convention), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/plan/tate-sen-theorem`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-1-plan-tate-sen-theorem).

**Sources.** [L. Berger — Représentations p-adiques et équations différentielles](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0102179v3), Théorème 6.2, p. 62. Statement (a). [L. Berger — Représentations p-adiques et équations différentielles](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0102179v3), Corollaire 6.3, p. 62. Statement (c). [L. Berger — Représentations p-adiques et équations différentielles](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0102179v3), Lemme 6.5, p. 63. Statement (b).

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-r06-4-plan-two-dimensional-ordinarity-criterion"></a>

### Ordinarity criteria for two-dimensional crystalline and semistable representations of G_{Q_p}

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/two-dimensional-ordinarity-criterion` (theorem).

Let K = Q_p and V a two-dimensional p-adic representation of G_{Q_p} with Hodge–Tate weights {0, r}, r ≥ 1 (HT(χ_p) = +1). (a) If V is crystalline and not a direct sum of two characters, let f(X) = X² + aX + b ∈ Z_p[X] (v_p(b) = r) be the characteristic polynomial of r(Frob_p) on WD(V), equivalently of φ on D*_cris(V). Then V is reducible — equivalently ordinary, V ≅ (ψ'χ^r *; 0 ψ) with ψ, ψ' unramified — iff f has a root μ ∈ Z_p^×; then ψ(Frob_p) = μ and ψ'(Frob_p) = b/(p^rμ). If f has no unit root (e.g. f irreducible, or a double root), V is irreducible. (b) If V is semistable and not crystalline then r = 2m + 1 is odd, and V is reducible iff m = 0, i.e. r = 1; in that case V is ordinary, a non-split extension of an unramified character ψ by ψχ, with trivial inertial type and N ≠ 0 on WD(V). (c) In particular a two-dimensional semistable non-crystalline representation with Hodge–Tate weights {0, 1} (modular weight 2 with inertial Weil–Deligne parameter (id, N ≠ 0)) is ordinary.

**Hypotheses and scope.** K=Q_p and V is two-dimensional over Q_p. The claim that a noncrystalline semistable weight difference is odd is asserted only with Q_p coefficients; it fails for ramified E-coefficients with fractional valuation slopes. No non-split crystalline extension of ψ'χ^r by ψ exists for r ≥ 1: the weight can only drop up a Jordan–Hölder filtration (Brinon–Conrad after Theorem 8.3.6).

**Construction or proof.**

1. By Colmez–Fontaine (R06.2/colmez-fontaine-theorem), V corresponds to a weakly admissible filtered (φ,N)-module over Q_p with jumps {0, r} (contravariant D*).
2. (a): Brinon–Conrad Theorem 8.3.6: the only non-trivial weakly admissible subobject is the φ-eigenline for a unit eigenvalue, when it exists; r(Frob_p) on WD(V) has the same characteristic polynomial as φ on D*_cris(V) (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/plan/convention-comparison-with-r01 (4)).
3. (b): Brinon–Conrad Proposition 8.3.8: N ≠ 0 forces eigenvalues λ, pλ; ker N is the φ-stable line of the smaller slope m, and weak admissibility t_H(ker N) = 0 ≤ t_N = m, with equality exactly when m = 0.
4. Ordinarity: in the reducible cases the sub-object has weight r and the quotient weight 0, which is Berger's ordinary filtration (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/ordinary-representation).

**Checks.** V_p(E) for E/Q_p with good reduction: f = X² − a_pX + p; ordinary iff p ∤ a_p (PARI/GP: y² = x³ − x, p = 5, 13 ordinary; p = 3, 7 supersingular). V_p(E_q) (Tate curve, r = 1, m = 0): reducible, ordinary, N ≠ 0. Weight p + 1 (r = p): V ordinary iff f has a unit root; this is the ordinary branch of PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/weight-p-plus-one-branch.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/weak-admissibility-is-admissibility`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-weak-admissibility-is-admissibility), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/weak-admissibility`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-weak-admissibility), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/ordinary-representation`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-4-plan-ordinary-representation), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/hodge-tate-weight-convention`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-hodge-tate-weight-convention), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/plan/convention-comparison-with-r01`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-3-plan-convention-comparison-with-r01), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/plan/weil-deligne-parameter`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-3-plan-weil-deligne-parameter).

**Sources.** [O. Brinon and B. Conrad — CMI Summer School notes on p-adic Hodge theory](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/notes.pdf), Theorem 8.3.6, p. 121. Crystalline criterion (a). [O. Brinon and B. Conrad — CMI Summer School notes on p-adic Hodge theory](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/notes.pdf), Proposition 8.3.8, p. 123. Semistable criterion (b). [Chandrashekhar Khare and Jean-Pierre Wintenberger — Serre's modularity conjecture (I)](https://www.math.ucla.edu/~shekhar/papers/results.pdf), Theorem 5.1(2), p. 9. The weight-2 semistable lifts used at k(ρ̄) = p + 1.

<a id="target-padichodgetheory-r06-4-plan-barsotti-tate-crystalline-criterion"></a>

### Crystalline criterion in weight 2 for every p (including p = 2): Hodge–Tate weights {0,1} ⇔ p-divisible group

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/barsotti-tate-crystalline-criterion` (theorem).

Let K/Q_p be finite (any ramification) and p any prime, including p = 2. (a) A p-adic representation V of G_K is crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights in {0, 1} (HT(χ_p) = +1) iff V ≅ V_p(G) = Q_p ⊗ T_p(G) for a p-divisible group G over O_K. (b) V is potentially Barsotti–Tate (V|_{G_L} ≅ V_p(G) for some finite L/K and G over O_L) iff V is de Rham with Hodge–Tate weights in {0, 1} and N = 0 on WD(V) (potentially crystalline). (c) For e = 1 and p ≥ 3, (a) and its lattice version are also given by Fontaine–Laffaille ([0, 1] ⊂ [0, p − 2]); for p = 2, or for e > 1, the Fontaine–Laffaille range does not reach weight 1 and (a) rests on the Breuil–Kisin classification (Breuil and Kisin for p > 2; Kisin for connected groups and Kim, Lau, Liu for all groups at p = 2).

**Hypotheses and scope.** The integral classification (G ↦ T_p(G) is an equivalence onto G_K-stable lattices in crystalline representations with weights in {0,1}) is FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4's; this node states the rational criterion in the HT(χ_p) = +1 convention and its potentially crystalline form. Weights {0,1} in our convention: V_p(G) has det with weight dim G.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a) ⇐: V_p(G) is crystalline with weights in {0,1} (Fontaine; imported with the R07.4 request). ⇒: R07.4 (Breuil–Kisin: Kisin modules of height ≤ 1, including p = 2).
2. (b): by PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/plan/weil-deligne-descent (b), N = 0 iff V|_{G_L} is crystalline for some L; apply (a) over L; conversely V_p(G) over L is crystalline over L, so V is de Rham with N = 0.
3. (c): PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/fontaine-laffaille-rational-consequences with [0,1] ⊂ [0, p−2] for p ≥ 3 and FL §9 (finite flat groups ↔ MF_tor^{f,2}, R07.3); at p = 2, [0, p−2] = {0}.

**Checks.** V_p(E) for E/K with good reduction: crystalline with weights {0, 1}, G = E[p^∞]. Q_p(1) = V_p(μ_{p^∞}); Q_p = V_p(Q_p/Z_p). V_p(E_q) (Tate curve): weights {0,1} but N ≠ 0, so not potentially Barsotti–Tate.

**Prerequisites.** `FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4`, `FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.3`, [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/plan/weil-deligne-descent`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-3-plan-weil-deligne-descent), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/fontaine-laffaille-rational-consequences`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-4-plan-fontaine-laffaille-rational-consequences), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/hodge-tate-weight-convention`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-hodge-tate-weight-convention).

**Sources.** [Chandrashekhar Khare and Jean-Pierre Wintenberger — Serre's modularity conjecture (I)](https://www.math.ucla.edu/~shekhar/papers/results.pdf), §9, Remark, p. 18. Statement (a) as used in Khare–Wintenberger (the '6=' is the text layer's rendering of ≠). [O. Brinon and B. Conrad — CMI Summer School notes on p-adic Hodge theory](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/notes.pdf), Part III, introduction, p. 155. Breuil–Kisin branch beyond Fontaine–Laffaille.

### The endpoint branch: Hodge–Tate weights in [0, p−1] (modular weight p)

**Target:** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/weight-p-endpoint-branch` (theorem).

Let K = K_0 = W(k)[1/p] be absolutely unramified (e = 1), σ its Frobenius. A filtered φ-module D over K is weakly admissible in the sense of R06.2/weak-admissibility; its jumps are the i with gr^i D ≠ 0. For Fontaine–Laffaille (FL) objects we use the notation of FL 1982: MF_tor^{f,p} (finite-length W(k)-modules M with M^0 = M, M^p = 0 and φ^i: M^i → M), strongly divisible lattices (FL 7.7), the ring Ŝ and Ŝ_K = K ⊗ Ŝ, and the contravariant functors U_S(M) = Hom_{MF}(M, Ŝ) (lattices), U_S(M) = Ext^1(M, S) (torsion) and U_{S_K}(Δ) = Hom_{MF_K}(Δ, Ŝ_K) (rational), all supplied by FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.3. Let p ≥ 3 and V a crystalline representation of G_K (K = K_0) with Hodge–Tate weights in [0, p − 1] (e.g. modular weight k = p: weights {0, p − 1}). (a) Rationally V is covered by Fontaine–Laffaille: V = U_{S_K}(D) = V_cris(D)^* for D = D*_cris(V) with jumps in [0, p−1] (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/small-weight-admissibility, PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/fontaine-laffaille-crystalline-comparison), and U_{S_K} is fully faithful there. (b) On strongly divisible lattices with jumps in [0, p − 1], U_S is exact, faithful and rank-preserving, and fully faithful exactly on those M with M/pM in MF_tor^{f,p'} (no nonzero quotient N = N^{p−1}) or in MF_tor^{f,p''} (no nonzero subobject N with N^1 = 0); unrestricted full faithfulness fails (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/fontaine-laffaille-endpoint-non-example). (c) The integral statements needed beyond (b) — lattices whose reduction has both a trivial-weight and a weight-(p−1) constituent, and the reductions used in Khare–Wintenberger I Theorem 4.1 at k = p — are supplied by the Breuil–Kisin classification of FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4, not by Fontaine–Laffaille.

**Hypotheses and scope.** p ≥ 3 (for p = 2, p − 1 = 1 and the weight-2 case is PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/barsotti-tate-crystalline-criterion). The §0.9/§6 restrictions are imposed as hypotheses, never replaced by a change of notation.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a): nodes cited in the statement; the interval [0, p−1] has length p − 1 < p.
2. (b): FL Proposition 7.15 (R07.3) and the endpoint non-example.
3. (c): request to R07.4; the ordinary sub-case is decided by PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/two-dimensional-ordinarity-criterion.

**Checks.** Two-dimensional V with weights {0, p−1} over Q_p: V = V_cris(D)^* for D with jumps {0, p−1}, and V is ordinary iff the Frobenius polynomial has a unit root. Z_p and Z_p(p−1) have isomorphic reductions, so an extension of Z_p(p−1)/p by F_p may have several non-isomorphic FL models — the restricted categories exclude this.

**Prerequisites.** [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/fontaine-laffaille-rational-consequences`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-4-plan-fontaine-laffaille-rational-consequences), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/fontaine-laffaille-crystalline-comparison`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-4-plan-fontaine-laffaille-crystalline-comparison), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/small-weight-admissibility`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-4-plan-small-weight-admissibility), `FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.3`, [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/hodge-tate-weight-convention`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-hodge-tate-weight-convention), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/plan/period-functors`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-plan-period-functors), [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/weak-admissibility-is-admissibility`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-2-weak-admissibility-is-admissibility), `mathlib:ZMod.units_pow_card_sub_one_eq_one`, [`PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/plan/two-dimensional-ordinarity-criterion`](#target-padichodgetheory-r06-4-plan-two-dimensional-ordinarity-criterion), `FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4`.

**Proof ingredients.** `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/fontaine-laffaille-endpoint-non-example`; their statements and locators appear in the proof-ingredient index.

**Sources.** [Jean-Marc Fontaine and Guy Laffaille — Construction de représentations p-adiques](http://www.numdam.org/item?id=ASENS_1982_4_15_4_547_0), 0.9 (i)–(ii), pp. 551–552 (checked on the page images).
